facts: Insured was hospitalized for suspected malaria, but pathological tests showed no blood parasites and there was no medical advice for hospitalization. The insurer's repudiation was upheld.
Claim for backache was repudiated, and the insured made a representation after 18 months, rendering the complaint time-barred under policy conditions. Complaint dismissed.
Wife underwent ear surgery and claim was rejected for pre-existing chronic mastoiditis. The medical opinion was speculative rather than definitive, so the insurer was ordered to pay.
Personal Accident claim where insurer initially offered 3 weeks temporary total disablement, later revised to 5 weeks. Surgeon recommended 6 weeks, which was awarded.
Personal accident claim experienced delay in paying temporary total disablement. The complainant already received the balance amount and sought better administrative efficiency. Case closed.
Claim for laminectomy was repudiated for delayed filing and pre-existing spinal stenosis. Proof established the policy was active since 1999, waiving time limits. Claim allowed with deductions.
Wife underwent TKR after policy running for 14 years. Insured repudiated based on old X-ray reports showing osteoarthritis. Repudiation set aside and full relief granted.
Husband underwent rectopexy and hernia repair. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing condition, supported by statements signed by the insured regarding long-term symptoms. Dismissed.
Child underwent appendectomy, but claim was rejected citing 2-year prior stomach pain. Explanation found convincing and doctor's certificate gave weight, so repudiation was set aside.
Insurer reduced cumulative bonus citing a 9-day renewal delay, offering a lower payout. Ombudsman noted consistent policy treatment and awarded full claim with cumulative bonus.
Claim for hysterectomy was repudiated under exclusion. During hearing, the insurer could not trace the file or justify the cut, and agreed to pay the full claimed amount.

Daughter was operated for correction of congenital absence of vagina. Insurer rejected under external congenital anomaly exclusion. Ombudsman ruled it a congenital deformity, setting aside the rejection.
Claim for fracture treatment was rejected claiming hospitalization was unnecessary and under 24 hours. Ombudsman noted treatment was under specialist advice and time of discharge was missing.
Claim for piles and colitis rejected because the hospital had only 8 beds and unqualified nurses, despite the medical report admitting validity. Ombudsman ordered payment.
Accidental ankle injury claim rejected because the complainant had pre-existing diabetes linked to wound healing. Ombudsman ruled exclusions should not defeat the main purpose of the cover.
First-year hysterectomy claim rejected due to pre-existing irregular periods mentioned in hospital notes. Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existing cancer and set aside repudiation.
Claim for kidney failure was repudiated based on pre-existing chronic renal failure and diabetes history. Conflicting medical opinions led to upholding the repudiation.
Claim rejected on grounds of pre-existing palpitation. Insurer failed to provide cogent evidence or consultation papers proving the exact duration prior to policy inception. Allowed.
Incisional hernia surgery claim repudiated because hernia developed on the scar of an undisclosed prior appendicectomy. Repudiation upheld for non-disclosure.
Two-year-old child operated for cataract, claim rejected as congenital. One medical referee found the claim admissible without confirming it as congenital, so order was passed to pay.

Complainant's son was hospitalised for epilepsy. Insurer repudiated claim citing non-disclosure of pre-existing epilepsy and treating the policy as new due to a break in continuity from previous group policy. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.

Insurer refused to renew complainant's wife's mediclaim policy. Ombudsman held that renewal cannot be refused simply due to claims or onerous risk resulting from contracted diseases during the policy period, directing the insurer to renew the policy.

Complainant met with an accident and was hospitalised after initial treatment. Insurer repudiated claim arguing it could have been treated conservatively without admission. Ombudsman set aside repudiation as hospitalisation was on doctor's advice.

Complainant's mother was hospitalised and claim was rejected under exclusion clauses relating to pre-existing diabetes and pre-hospitalisation consultations. Ombudsman noted diabetes was declared at inception without exclusion, setting aside repudiation.

Complainant underwent CABG. Claim was repudiated for suppression of pre-existing ischemic heart disease and diabetes, which was established by hospital records prior to policy inception. Complaint dismissed.

Complainant's wife underwent surgery for incisional hernia which developed on the scar of an earlier hysterectomy. Insurer invoked exclusion clauses linking the current condition to the past surgery. Repudiation sustained.

Complainant's wife underwent surgery for tubo-ovarian mass. Insurer rejected claim because the hospital had fewer than 15 in-patient beds as per exclusion rules. Ombudsman ruled the marginal short-fall in beds was not fundamental enough to deny benefits.

Complainant's wife underwent knee replacement surgery. Insurer offered a reduced settlement based on historical tabular benefit limits, linking it to an osteotomy performed eight years prior. Ombudsman held the reduction unjustified and awarded the full amount.

Complainant underwent surgery for fistula in anus. Claim was repudiated under waiting period exclusion clauses as there was a 73-day gap in policy renewal, making it a fresh policy and the surgery occurred within the first year.

Complainant's wife suffered accidental fracture and was hospitalised. Insurer offered a reduced amount due to duplicate bills and excluded payments. During hearing, insurer conceded payments against duplicate bills backed by affidavit were admissible. Full claim awarded with interest.

Complainant's daughter was hospitalised and underwent surgery. Insurer initially repudiated on pre-existence grounds, then sent a reduced discharge voucher, but ultimately admitted during the hearing that repudiation was wrong and full amount was payable. Awarded with interest.

Complainant sought reimbursement for hospitalisation and surgery. Insurer disallowed a portion because the medical bill voucher was issued on the hospital's letterhead. Ombudsman directed full payment with interest.

Complainant underwent PTCA for unstable angina. Insurer repudiated claim alleging suppression of past cardiac history and non-submission of documents. Ombudsman noted insurer's panel doctor had medically examined and certified the complainant fit prior to policy issuance, setting aside repudiation.

Insurer issued a 15-day notice of cancellation for a running mediclaim policy without providing specific reasons. Ombudsman held the cancellation bad in law due to inadequate notice period and lack of valid reasons, setting it aside.

Complainant's son underwent laminectomy for backache in the first year of the policy. Insurer repudiated on pre-existence grounds. Ombudsman noted medical referee opinions were inconclusive or favored the insured, thus setting aside repudiation.

Complainant's wife underwent CABG. Insurer repudiated for non-disclosure of past insurance in proposal form. Ombudsman observed that the insurer had treated the policy as continuous by awarding cumulative bonuses, effectively knowing of past coverage, and thus estopped from denying liability.

Complainant's wife was hospitalised after weeks of OPD treatment. Insurer repudiated the claim based on a medical referee's opinion that it could be treated as OPD. Ombudsman set aside repudiation given the treating doctor's prolonged care and prolonged policy standing.

Complainant was hospitalised for tuberculosis. Claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause based on a panel doctor's presumptive opinion. Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existence prior to policy inception and ordered full payment.

Complainant underwent left eye cataract surgery but failed to disclose a prior right eye cataract operation in the proposal form. Suppression of material fact was established, and repudiation was upheld.

Under a personal accident policy, the complainant sustained injuries in a scooter accident. Insurer offered 3 weeks temporary total disablement against 6 weeks advised by the treating doctor. Ombudsman applied the golden mean principle and awarded 4.5 weeks compensation.

Wife of the complainant underwent TKR. Claim repudiated for delayed submission, non-disclosure of past Hysterectomy, and Cervical Spondylosis. Ombudsman noted that treated and cured Spondylosis from 4 years prior cannot be a sole reason to repudiate TKR and non-disclosure was not proved material. Repudiation set aside.

Complainant was hospitalised and claim was repudiated as treatment could be on OPD basis. Treating doctor certified hospitalisation was necessary. Repudiation set aside in the first case. In the second companion case involving the same insurer, hospitalisation ended in angiography and diagnosis only, so repudiation was upheld under policy clause 4.10.

Wife of the complainant was hospitalised. Claim repudiated on the ground that hospitalisation was not necessary and treatment could be done in OPD. Ombudsman observed hospitalisation was on the advice of a qualified surgeon. Repudiation set aside.

Complainant's wife diagnosed with ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Claim repudiated under exclusion clause 4.12 for conditions traceable to pregnancy, which was upheld. In a companion case against National Insurance, a claim for Ovarian Cyst and Appendicitis was repudiated for pre-existence based on a written statement by the insured; repudiation sustained.

Insurer deducted a portion of hospitalisation expenses based on medical referee opinion. Subsequently, the same medical referee issued an opinion advising release of the deducted amount. No justification for withholding found. Insurer directed to pay the balance.

Daughter of complainant hospitalised for ENT problem. Claim repudiated as domiciliary treatment was sufficient and the hospital did not meet policy condition 2.1 regarding registration/bed strength. Ombudsman held infrastructural shortfall is not tenable for repudiation. Insurer directed to pay.

Claim for hospitalisation and treatment of Gouty Synovitis repudiated under clause 4.1 and medical referee opinion that hospitalisation was unnecessary. Policy was in force for 15 years. Hospitalisation was under advice of treating surgeon. Repudiation set aside.

In the first case, parties reached an amicable settlement of Rs. 4856 for a Tonsillectomy claim. In the second case against New India Assurance regarding back-ache hospitalisation, claim was repudiated for lack of active treatment and rest only; ombudsman ruled in favour of complainant as hospitalisation was under medical advice and policy was long-standing.

Complainant underwent bilateral knee replacements. Insurer settled left knee claim but repudiated right knee claim citing pre-existence and 4th-year policy restrictions. Ombudsman found no blanket policy exclusions for 4th-year claims or proof of pre-existing osteoarthritis. Insurer directed to pay.

Wife of complainant underwent vaginal hysterectomy. Claim repudiated on grounds of undisclosed prior miscarriages and D&E. Ombudsman noted no proof that miscarriages occurred prior to policy inception in 1999, and medical referee's post-script advising rejection lacked weight. Repudiation set aside.

In the first case against Oriental Insurance, the insurer failed to appear or defend the file, and was ordered to pay the claim. In the second case against New India Assurance, claim for Aortic Stenosis and Rheumatic Heart Disease was repudiated on pre-existing grounds due to age. Ombudsman ruled generic blanket exclusions for RHD are unfair. Insurer to pay full amount with interest.

Claim for hospitalisation of complainant's mother repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1. Discharge summary showed history of CVA for the past 2 years, which was accepted as admissible evidence. Repudiation upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Under a floater policy, complainant claimed for bilateral cataract surgeries. Insurer paid for the right eye but treated the left eye as 'no claim' because the maximum limit for cataract had been exhausted. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on policy limits. In a companion case against National Insurance regarding Cortical Sinus Thrombosis, repudiation on pre-existing grounds was set aside and Rs. 1,07,474 awarded.

Insurer refused renewal of mediclaim policy without medical tests, alleging delay, despite receiving the renewal cheque before the due date. Ombudsman found no delay and directed the insurer to renew the policy continuously without break upon collecting the premium.

Complainant operated for CAD twice within 45 days. Insurer repudiated claims citing varying durations of diabetes (19 years vs 7-8 years) in hospital summaries and short interval between surgeries. Ombudsman gave benefit of doubt to complainant as evidence was contradictory. Insurer to pay Rs. 2,61,000.

Complainant's son sustained severe injuries in an explosion and was admitted for observation. Claim repudiated on the ground that admission was for observation only. Ombudsman noted the insurer's action was too rigid given the emergency circumstances of an injured child. Insurer to pay Rs. 2,629.

Claim for gynaecological problem (Dysfunctional Uterine Bleeding) repudiated alleging pre-existence 15-20 years back. Medical records and treating gynecologist certified the condition was acute and of 8 months duration. Benefit of doubt given to complainant due to conflicting documents. Insurer to pay Rs. 45,971.

Complainant experienced severe delay in claim settlement through the TPA. Insurer sent a discharge voucher for a slightly lesser amount after grievance intervention but could not justify the deduction. Claim allowed for full amount along with 8% simple interest.

Claim for CABG surgery repudiated after insurer issued policy documents with cardiac disorders excluded following a 5-month renewal break. Computer-generated policy initially showed no exclusions, and exclusion documents were only sent after claim lodging. Repudiation set aside. Insurer to pay Rs. 1,60,582.

Complainant disputed the imposition of exclusions and lack of cumulative bonus after switching from a group policy to an individual policy with New India Assurance. Insurer passed an endorsement removing exclusions for the first year and issuing the second year without exclusions. Complainant expressed satisfaction; complaint disposed.

Insured claimed for fracture treatment. Insurer repudiated based on hospital eligibility criteria, but hospital was registered and networked with TPAs. Ombudsman ordered payment of Rs. 5370 with 8 percent interest.

Two similar cases where claims were initially repudiated for exclusions or pre-existing conditions, but insurers later reconsidered, issued discharge vouchers for Rs. 7000 and Rs. 28000 respectively, and payments were accepted by complainants, closing the complaints.

Complainant hospitalized for tonsils. Claim repudiated alleging pre-existing condition since last 3 years based on doctor report, but report lacked such mention and insurer failed to produce proposal or underwriting records. Insurer ordered to pay Rs. 20837.
Insured underwent IVF after unsuccessful laparoscopic surgery for infertility. Claim repudiated under policy clause excluding sterility. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.

Claim for osteoporosis and other conditions repudiated as pre-existing based on an old proposal form from 1999, despite continuous renewals and new ailments developing later. Repudiation set aside and claim ordered to be settled.

Bypass surgery claim repudiated alleging suppression of pre-existing angina and a mild stroke in 1995-1996. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 111031 as discharge certificate did not specify exact duration and insurer lacked employer records or doctor statements.
Claim for exorbitant medical expenses following hemicolectomy delayed on pretext of investigation. Ombudsman directed insurer to pay sum insured of Rs. 320000.

Angioplasty claim repudiated on ground of pre-existing hypertension, despite long policy history. Cardiologist opinion showed no definitive prior record. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 210000 including claim-free bonus.
Overseas mediclaim for hydrocephalus surgery rejected due to non-disclosure of past brain surgery and high blood pressure, and because treatment was for a non-emergent condition. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for frozen shoulder treatment at an ayurvedic centre repudiated on grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. Ombudsman held that hospitalization necessity is decided by the treating physician, not the insurer, and ordered payment.

Claim for neurological observation after a fall repudiated as hospitalization was allegedly for investigation only. Ombudsman held admission was on specialist advice and tests were part of treatment, ordering payment.
Insurer disallowed admission fee and room service charges. Ombudsman found nursing service charges and admission fees are valid reimbursable expenses, awarding Rs. 190.

Granddaughter's post aural abscess claim repudiated as pre-existing because of an ear swelling 5-6 years prior. Ombudsman held that full recovery means recurrence is not a pre-existing disease and ordered payment.
CABG claim repudiated due to pre-existing long-standing diabetes and hypertension. Complainant submitted tampered medical certificates to mislead the forum. Complaint dismissed.

Varicose veins claim repudiated and policy cancelled alleging 12-year pre-existing ailment and non-disclosure. Investigation confirmed disease duration was only 1.5 years. Insurer ordered to reimburse expenses and restore policy.
Chronic liver disease claim repudiated based on a test report mistakenly dated prior to policy inception instead of the actual later date. Insurer directed to reimburse medical expenses.
Claim for hypertension and giddiness repudiated as hospitalization was solely for investigation without significant hospital treatment, with diagnostic scans done outside. Complaint dismissed.

COPD claim repudiated as pre-existing. Insurer admitted policy inception predated the illness onset and agreed to settle, but TPA delayed. Ombudsman ordered settlement up to sum insured of Rs. 60000 plus 8 percent interest.
Hemiplegia claim repudiated due to non-disclosure of 15-year diabetes history which had a medically acknowledged nexus to the stroke. Complaint dismissed.
Angioplasty claim repudiated under exclusion clause as CAD pre-existed the policy inception, supported by past hospital records from 1996. Complaint dismissed.

Insured underwent repair of split ear lobule and depressed scar. Insurer repudiated the claim stating treatment was cosmetic and excluded under the policy. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as no accidental happening was proved.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalised for Chronic Sinusitis/Deviated Nasal Septum and underwent FESS/Septoplasty. Insurer repudiated claim citing 15 years history of nose block. Attending doctor later certified history as 1 year. Ombudsman held pre-existence not tenable and directed payment.

Insured claimed reimbursement for treatment of fissure in ano, BPH, hemorrhoids, DM, HTN, and gastric ulcer. Insurer repudiated entire claim citing pre-existing HTN, excluded DM, and waiting period for piles. Ombudsman held treatment for fissure in ano and gastric ulcer were independent and directed reimbursement for those.

Insured underwent CABG for CAD. Claim was partially settled because chest pain manifested one month before sum insured was increased from Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 2,00,000. Ombudsman upheld the settlement restricted to pre-increased sum insured.

Insured's wife was hospitalised for Bilateral Ovarian Cyst and underwent laparoscopy. Insurer repudiated claim stating hospitalisation was related to infertility treatment. Medical opinion confirmed surgery was primarily for ovarian cyst, making infertility procedure incidental. Repudiation set aside.

Insured was hospitalised for multiple renal calculi 10 months after policy inception. Insurer repudiated claim as pre-existing. Ombudsman noted lack of evidence of prior symptoms and attending doctor's opinion that stones could form in 5-6 months, setting aside repudiation.

Insured claimed for hemoptysis, aortic stenosis, and coronary artery disease. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing pulmonary tuberculosis causing hemoptysis. Ombudsman held hemoptysis was linked to prior TB but aortic stenosis and CAD were unrelated, directing payment for unrelated treatments.

Insured's spouse was hospitalised for Cervical Cerclage due to cervical incompetence. Insurer repudiated claim under exclusion for treatments related to pregnancy or childbirth. Ombudsman upheld repudiation as procedure was for maintenance of pregnancy.

Insured underwent PTCA for Ischaemic Heart Disease. Claim was repudiated because insured had a 15-20 year history of hypertension, a risk factor for CAD. Ombudsman upheld repudiation establishing hypertension as pre-existing proximate cause.

Insured was hospitalised for portal hypertension, hepatic failure, and alcoholic liver disease. Insurer repudiated claim under exclusion for diseases arising from alcohol consumption. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision based on medical records confirming alcoholic cirrhosis.

Insured was hospitalized for ureteric calculus under Universal Health Insurance Policy. Insurer repudiated claim for pre-existence and hospital bed capacity violation. Ombudsman noted bed condition was not communicated to insured and allowed 75% on ex-gratia basis.

Insured claimed for injuries sustained in a road accident while traveling as a pillion rider. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion for alcohol use. Ombudsman held insurer failed to prove intoxication caused the accident and ordered claim payment.

Insured's 7-year-old daughter was hospitalised for Chronic Adeno Tonsilitis. Insurer repudiated claim as pre-existing. Ombudsman noted medical records traced symptoms only to a date after policy inception and set aside repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife underwent CABG for CAD. Insurer repudiated claim under pre-existing disease exclusion citing history of hypertension since 1980 and TIA. Ombudsman upheld repudiation establishing hypertension as proximate cause for CAD.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent CABG for Coronary Artery Disease. Insurer repudiated claim citing old myocardial infarction 20 years ago. Ombudsman noted insured remained asymptomatic and unmedicated for 20 years, making pre-existence untenable, and ordered claim payment.

Overseas medical policy claim for US$ 1147.59 was partly settled by foreign settling agent. Insurer failed to provide balance due to internal communication issues with agent. Ombudsman directed insurer to settle the balance amount immediately.

Overseas mediclaim policy claim was repudiated for pre-existing chest pain. Ombudsman noted policy defines pre-existing conditions as treatments sought within 12 months prior to travel, and no such treatment occurred, but dismissed the specific petition text outcome formulation due to mislabeling in source text summary logic.
Insurer refused to renew mediclaim policy due to bad claim experience after continuous renewals from 1992 to 2004. Ombudsman held refusal was arbitrary and directed renewal upon payment of premium.
Insurer disallowed Rs. 7,000 for a ceramic crown fixed to teeth injured in a road accident, citing cosmetic exclusion. Ombudsman held crown was necessitated by accident and ordered payment.

Insured's mother underwent operation for hidradenitis under general anesthesia. Insurer repudiated claim for hospitalization under 24 hours. Ombudsman held operation required proper operation theater and ordered claim allowance.

Claim was repudiated because the insured was admitted for investigation only, which did not require hospitalisation and could have been done on an OPD basis. Separately, a small balance for pre-natal expenses was discussed in another claim part.

The insured underwent bypass surgery for blockages detected shortly after policy inception. Medical records from a prior hospital confirmed a known history of hypertension, diabetes, and ischemic heart disease which was not declared in the proposal form.
Claim for an operation of an abscess behind the knee was repudiated because hospital confinement was less than 24 hours, violating the minimum 24-hour hospitalization policy condition.

The insured underwent a hysterectomy due to a ruptured ectopic pregnancy and cornual pregnancy complications. The insurer repudiated the claim on the ground that pregnancy is an excluded condition under the standard mediclaim policy.

Complainant underwent surgery for gall bladder stones shortly after policy inception. The insurer repudiated the claim based on panel doctor opinion that chronic cholecystitis existed for 1 to 2 years prior to policy inception.

Claim was repudiated after 1.5 years on the ground that the patient was admitted only for investigations and tests rather than actual treatment, and the records showed no specific treatment for porphyria.

The insurer imposed a high compulsory excess of Rs. 5000 per claim on a Rs. 20000 sum insured due to a high claim ratio on a long-standing policy. The Ombudsman held the 25 percent excess unreasonable for senior citizens and advised replacing it with a small token excess for small claims.

Complainant underwent emergency laparotomy for an ovarian cyst and ruptured appendix shortly after policy inception. The insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing based on previous medical history of ovarian cystectomy and prior symptoms.

Claim for rheumatic heart disease treatment was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease, supported by medical consensus that valve involvement takes years to develop. Additionally, a dental claim was rejected due to lack of hospitalization.

TPA deducted a small amount for home visits from a hospitalisation claim without proper review of policy terms. The Ombudsman held that deductions without giving the insured an opportunity to represent were improper and directed re-examination.

The claim for an ovarian tumor and urinary dilatation treatment was delayed indefinitely by the TPA despite all details being submitted. The Ombudsman criticized the reckless irresponsibility of the TPA and ordered settlement.
Hysterectomy expenses were rejected because there was a break in insurance due to non-renewal during the grace period, making the policy a fresh contract and hitting first-year exclusion clauses.

Claim for angioplasty was repudiated alleging 30 years of hypertension was undisclosed in the proposal. The Ombudsman found the entry was likely a clerical error for 30 days given the insured's foreign manual labor with routine medical checks, and allowed the claim up to sum insured.

Claim for liver cirrhosis and hypertension was repudiated for non-disclosure of prior diabetes and liver condition. While upholding the repudiation due to admitted prior illness, the Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount considering the claimant's poor health and financial distress.

Hernia surgery claim was repudiated and policy cancelled due to undisclosed history of prior hernia repair. Although cancellation without proper notice was faulted, the repudiation and cancellation of the policy were upheld.
Accident claim for a bathroom fall was rejected because records showed treatment was actually for an ayurvedic rheumatic condition rather than a visible accidental injury.

Surgical treatment for deflected nasal septum in the complainant's daughter was rejected as a congenital disorder. The Ombudsman held that deflected nasal septum without external deformity does not constitute a congenital external exclusion and ordered payment.

Claim for oral carcinoma treatment was delayed and contested based on a disputed investigator statement regarding disease duration. Finding no proof of pre-existing disease or misrepresentation, the Ombudsman allowed the claim.
Claim reimbursement for wife's treatment was rejected because the condition was attributable to pregnancy, which is explicitly excluded under policy clause 4.12.

Claim for osteosarcoma and leg amputation of the insured's son was repudiated for alleged suppression of prior illness dates. The Ombudsman found the date discrepancy was an inadvertent clerical error and no suppression existed, ordering full claim payment.
Insured claimed reimbursement for hospitalisation due to Seborrhic Dermatitis. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing Diabetes mellitus of 5 years not disclosed in the proposal form.
Claim for son's treatment of kidney problems and Urinary Tract Infection was repudiated due to pre-existing nature of the disease and misrepresentation.
Claim for father's treatment was rejected because he suffered from pre-existing Diabetes Mellitus which was concealed at the time of taking the policy.

Insurer rejected mediclaim on the grounds that admission was for general checkup and investigation, and patient was under medication for 5 years. Ombudsman found medication claim unproven and ordered payment for actual medicine bills.
Insurer closed mediclaim because the insured obtained the policy after knowing about her disease, concealing material facts at the time of proposal.

Claim for cancer treatment was repudiated alleging pre-existing symptoms from policy inception. Ombudsman noted panel doctor's report was insufficient to prove prior knowledge and set aside the rejection.
Claim for piles surgery was partially paid based on the original sum insured of Rs. 50,000 rather than the enhanced Rs. 2,00,000, as the condition pre-dated the enhancement waiting period.
Insurer rejected claim for a fracture treated with plaster on the grounds that hospitalisation was not required. Ombudsman ruled that restricted movement for 5 weeks qualified for reimbursement.
Claim for Disc Derangement syndrome was rejected citing pre-existing lower back pain. Ombudsman noted renewal without fresh proposal made the rejection untenable and ordered full payment.
Insurer partially paid dental treatment claim based on expert opinion. Ombudsman found no reason to disbelieve the complainant and ordered full reimbursement.
Claim for medical expenses was rejected for suppression of material facts regarding mother's pre-existing Hypertension and Periarthritis at proposal and revival.

Claim for Hernia was rejected alleging pre-existing symptoms for 5 years. Ombudsman set aside the repudiation noting the insured was a bank employee eligible for full medical refund anyway, indicating lack of prior awareness.

Insurer partially paid claim, denying expenses beyond 30 days of pre-hospitalisation and 60 days post-hospitalisation, and rejected a hand-written professional fee bill due to late submission and questionable credibility.
Claim for wife's treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis was repudiated for pre-existing nature of the disease and non-disclosure of vital information.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for Incisional Hernia Post Hysterectomy was rejected because the treatment was a continuation of a pre-existing condition spanning 4 years prior to the policy.
Ear surgery claim was rejected as hospital records showed symptoms existed within the first 30 days of the policy period, attracting the waiting period exclusion.

Insurer rejected child's claim for Acute Glomerulo Nephritis and Acute Gastro Enteritis assuming it was a longstanding problem. Ombudsman allowed the claim as the insurer failed to establish prior illness.
Claim for Acute Angle Closure Glaucoma was rejected alleging pre-existing condition. Hospital records proved sudden onset within 1-3 days, so the Ombudsman allowed the claim.
Claim for diabetic foot treatment was rejected because hospital records proved the insured had diabetes for 23 years, constituting suppression of material facts.
Claim for heart treatment was rejected because renewal payment cheque bounced, causing a break in policy continuity; the new policy commenced later, and the illness predated it.

Complainant sought reimbursement for wife's incisional hernia surgery. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing condition, as the hernia developed at the site of a previous caesarean section performed six years prior to policy commencement. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Policyholder underwent treatment for cardiac diseases and died of heart disease. Insurer rejected the claim for non-disclosure of pre-existing heart ailments from 1995 when renewing the policy after a gap. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint due to intentional suppression of material facts.

Claim for inguinal hernia treatment was rejected due to non-disclosure of pre-existing medical history dating back years before policy inception. Ombudsman upheld dismissal based on suppression of material facts.

Claim for low back ache hospitalisation was repudiated due to a duration discrepancy between the discharge summary and medical certificate. The doctor later rectified the summary. Ombudsman allowed the claim, ruling the initial discrepancy was a minor clerical error by a non-attending junior doctor.

Claim for father's treatment of portal hypertension and cirrhosis under a group mediclaim policy was repudiated due to pre-existing disease of 8 years. Considering the complainant's severe financial distress, the Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount while upholding the repudiation.

Insurer rejected a renal transplantation claim citing pre-existing illness based on a bland hospital record statement. Ombudsman found no substantive medical evidence of prior kidney ailments, ruled the insurer's decision invalid, and ordered settlement of the claim.

Claim for treatment received at a hospital in Kenya and subsequent outpatient treatment in Trivandrum was rejected because the policy permitted reimbursement only for inpatient hospital treatment in India. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for thyroid gland surgery was repudiated as pre-existing. Investigations and large surgical dimensions proved the ailment existed for several years. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for treatment at a nursing home was rejected because the facility did not conform to the policy's definition of a hospital registered with local authorities. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for an abortion operation due to severe bleeding was rejected under policy clause 4.12 excluding pregnancy-related complications. Records did not prove it was a life-saving procedure. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for hospitalisation under a Jana Seva Insurance Policy was rejected due to alleged pre-existing disease. At the Ombudsman's intervention, parties compromised, and the insurer agreed to pay an amount in full and final settlement.
Complainant sought compensation for a 100-day delay by the TPA in settling a mediclaim. Ombudsman allowed travelling expenses and short-term interest on the settled claim amount.
Claim for coronary artery bypass surgery was rejected because the insured suffered from the illness prior to proposing for insurance and failed to disclose it. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for abdominal hysterectomy was rejected as the operation occurred during the policy exclusion period. During the hearing, the complainant expressed willingness to withdraw the case, leading to dismissal.

Claim for hernia surgery was rejected on the grounds that it was an after-effect of a hysterectomy performed 7 years prior to the policy and not disclosed in the proposal. Ombudsman upheld the rejection but awarded an ex-gratia amount due to the complainant's financial hardship.

Claim for oesophagitis and sinusitis hospitalisation was rejected on the basis that hospitalisation was unnecessary. The Ombudsman found issues with policy validity due to bigamy, but awarded hospital charges as ex-gratia considering the complainant's impecunious condition.

Claim for high myopia astigmatism surgery was rejected because the condition was pre-existing from childhood, as confirmed by family testimony regarding spectacles use. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Insurer partially rejected a bypass surgery claim citing pre-existing diabetes and TURP history not disclosed in the proposal. Ombudsman found the insurer's reasoning arbitrary and directed payment of the sum insured under a secondary policy.

Complainant sought full reimbursement for post-hospitalisation expenses following heart attacks. Insurer disallowed expenses incurred beyond the 60-day policy limit. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's strict adherence to policy conditions and dismissed the complaint.

Insurer rejected claims for Motor Neuron Disease citing pre-existing neck pain and spondylosis. Ombudsman ruled that initial neck pain treatments were pre-existing and properly rejected, but the subsequent Motor Neuron Disease developed during policy coverage and ordered payment for those specific treatments.
A group mediclaim reimbursement claim for a third child's delivery was rejected because policy terms restricted coverage to the first two children only. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A mediclaim for dental root canal treatment without hospitalization was rejected based on policy exclusion clauses. The Ombudsman upheld the dismissal due to lack of merit.

The insurer rejected a mediclaim for a wife's treatment because the health club had already settled the medical expenses and the complainant incurred no out-of-pocket costs. The complaint was dismissed.

A claim for caesarian and sterilization was partially repudiated as sterilization was excluded. Since the health club directly settled the admissible reduced sum and the complainant incurred no personal expense, the complaint was dismissed.

A claim for cancer treatment was restricted to the pre-enhancement sum insured of Rs. 50,000 because the disease was detected prior to the sum insured enhancement to Rs. 1 lakh. The Ombudsman found the insurer's action fair.

A claim for chronic bronchitis and pharyngitis was rejected due to undisclosed pre-existing ailments and the fact that expenses were paid by the health club, not the complainant. The repudiation was upheld.

Following a bypass surgery, the insurer limited the claim to the sum insured applicable at the time of the initial myocardial infarction detection rather than the later enhanced sum insured. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stand.

A claim for uterine prolapse treatment was repudiated due to pre-existing illness, suppression of facts, and because treatment expenses were paid by the health club. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's action.

A claim for inguinal hernia surgery was repudiated because the policy's renewed terms introduced a two-year exclusion period for specific diseases, which was accepted by the insured. The complaint was dismissed.
An individual mediclaim policy explicitly excluded known pre-existing conditions like diabetes and hypertension. The insurer's rejection of a related claim was upheld as justified.

A claim for a coronary angiogram was rejected on grounds of pre-existing heart disease, despite no medical evidence proving the condition existed prior to continuous policy coverage. The Ombudsman set aside the rejection and ordered full settlement.

A maternity and caesarian section claim was rejected because a scanning report showed a uterine fibroid during the first policy year and alleged pregnancy diabetes. The Ombudsman found the rejection arbitrary and awarded the claimed amount.

A maternity claim was rejected on the grounds that delivery occurred one day short of the 270-day waiting period. The Ombudsman calculated that the waiting period expired at midnight the previous day and awarded the expenses.

A claim for Prolapsed Intervertebral Disc was repudiated for non-disclosure of prior back and leg pain treated over two years. Medical records confirmed the pre-existence and suppression of symptoms, leading to dismissal.

Following partial settlement of cataract operation claims involving complications like glaucoma and retinal damage, the Ombudsman directed the insurer to pay an additional amount considering the insureds' advanced age and surgical complexity.

A dispute arose over partial settlement of a hysterectomy claim regarding pre- and post-hospitalization expenses. The Ombudsman directed the TPA and claimant to reconcile documents and ordered settlement of the balance with 6% interest.

A claim for varicose veins hospitalization in the second policy year was rejected because the history of the ailment was not disclosed in the proposal form. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

A claim for craniospinal tumor surgery was repudiated for non-disclosure of past knee replacement, hypothyroidism, angina, and hypertension. Noting lack of medical nexus with the tumor, the Ombudsman ordered an ex-gratia payment of 30% of admissible expenses.
A claim for bile duct calculus was rejected because the insured failed to disclose a prior gall bladder removal surgery in 1987. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's non-disclosure defense.

An overseas mediclaim for eye surgery in the USA was stalled due to pre-existing condition exclusions handled by a foreign agency. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to coordinate and process the claim on merits, disposing of the case.

Insured claimed reimbursement for a cataract operation. The insurer repudiated under exclusion clause 4.3 due to a policy gap. During the proceedings, the insurer agreed to settle the principal amount, and the Ombudsman directed payment of the admissible amount with interest due to unjustifiable delay.

Insured underwent a tonsillectomy and microlaryngoscopy for vocal cord mass and septic tonsils. The insurer rejected the claim as a pre-existing condition. The Ombudsman noted that throat and vocal cord issues are closely interrelated and hair-splitting is difficult post-surgery, ordering a partial settlement of 75% of admissible expenses.

Insured hospitalized for chronic liver disease, renal calculus, and hypertension. Insurer repudiated based on pre-existence and alcohol intake exclusion. Hospital records showed symptoms existed for 18-20 months prior to taking the first policy. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for incisional hernioplasty with abdominoplasty. Insurer repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing disease based on a hernia operation 30 years prior. The Ombudsman held the repudiation unsustainable as the previous condition was well-managed and declared in the proposal 15 years ago.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was admitted for administration of Eprex injections and investigation of myelodysplastic syndrome/refractory anaemia. The insurer repudiated under clause 4.10 for hospitalization solely for investigation and lasting less than 24 hours. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation noting no emergency or critical health status required hospitalization.

Insured underwent surgery for left leg varicose veins. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existence based on medical opinions. The Ombudsman found the complaint not sustainable after reviewing case papers and medical assessments indicating a long duration of the condition.

Insured sought enhancement of sum insured from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 5 lakhs shortly before undergoing coronary artery bypass graft. The insurer offered settlement based on the original sum insured, stating severe blockages could not develop in three months. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for hospitalization due to acute coronary syndrome, diabetes, and other complications was restricted by the insurer to the original sum insured because the enhancement was made around the time diabetes was diagnosed. The Ombudsman held the claim for the enhanced amount was not sustainable.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for a meniscus tear and ligament sprain. The insurer rejected the claim under clauses 4.2 and 4.10. The Ombudsman held the claim sustainable because correction was advised even if surgery was not elected, and directed settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for coronary artery disease and partial settlement was made. Investigation and confirmation from doctors revealed the insured had a similar episode four years prior. The Ombudsman held the claim was not sustainable due to pre-existence.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for general weakness, fever, and pain for diagnostic purposes. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion 4.10 as hospitalisation was solely for investigation and not clinically required. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for endometrial carcinoma was rejected under exclusion 4.1 due to pre-existing history of irregular bleeding dating back several years prior to policy inception. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on clinical and CT scan findings.

Insured hospitalized for renal failure and related conditions. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing hypertension and high creatinine from 1990, disputing the policy inception date. The Ombudsman established policy continuity from 1988-1989 and directed the insurer to settle the claim with interest.

Claim for incisional and umbilical hernia was rejected for non-disclosure of a prior hysterectomy in 1986. Sonography confirmed herniation through the previous surgical scar. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision that material facts were withheld and the condition was pre-existing.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's mother was hospitalized for a cerebellar and occipital disorder. The insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.1. The Ombudsman found no evidence of deliberate non-disclosure at inception, and considering the policy had run for 3 years, awarded 60% of costs on an ex-gratia basis.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured claimed for two hernia operations resulting in partial settlement by the insurer. The Ombudsman found unreasonable delay and failure to consolidate bills, directing the insurer to settle the full amount along with simple interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent knee replacement after continuous policy coverage for 8 years. Insurer repudiated under clause 4.1 citing osteoarthritic changes. The Ombudsman noted that while osteoarthritis develops over time, the long policy history warranted fairness, ordering a 50% ex-gratia settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for cervical spondylosis. The insurer repudiated under exclusion clause 4.10 as admission was for investigation and physiotherapy which could be handled as an outpatient. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for knee replacement and osteoarthritis was repudiated as pre-existing. X-rays and second opinions indicated chronic osteoarthritis of 10-15 years duration. Since the policy started in 1999, the Ombudsman upheld the insurer's repudiation.

Insured hospitalized for chest and back pain undergoing extensive tests which ruled out coronary artery disease. The insurer repudiated under clause 4.10 for hospitalization solely for investigation without required medical treatment. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured claimed reimbursement for breast surgery. Insurer made a short payment of Rs. 1,148 and delayed settlement. The Ombudsman held the deduction in order but awarded 9 percent interest for the delayed payment from 17.05.2003 to 28.08.2003.

Complainant challenged the non-renewal of their mediclaim policy by the insurer. The Ombudsman noted that general insurance is an annual contract and insurers have the option to deny renewal based on underwriting decisions, hence dismissing the complaint.

Insured underwent knee surgery for Genu Verus deformity and osteoarthritis. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing condition under exclusion clause 4.1. The Ombudsman noted the first claim was paid and directed the insurer to settle on an ex-gratia basis at 50% of admissible expenses.

Insured claimed Rs. 31,510 and Rs. 1,35,009.50 for hospitalisations due to sub-acute intestinal obstruction. Insurer repudiated stating hospitalisation was primarily for diagnostic purposes. Ombudsman held that while stay could have been avoided, the patient suffered pain, and directed settlement to the extent of 40% of admissible expenses.

Insured hospitalized for laryngeal stridor and dyspnoea. Insurer repudiated for pre-existing hypertension and IHD. Ombudsman noted non-disclosure of hypertension at proposal stage and directed settlement to the extent of 75% of admissible expenses.

Insured claimed Rs. 98,000 for carbuncle surgery, but insurer offered Rs. 40,000 as reasonable amounts towards room and medical charges. As the divisional office failed to provide records to the forum, the Ombudsman reverted the matter back to the regional office for direct handling and explanation.

Insured claimed Rs. 3,00,000 for bypass surgery of his spouse. Insurer offered Rs. 1,00,000 initially and later repudiated citing pre-existing ischemic heart disease and non-disclosure of diabetes. Ombudsman found evidence of old ailment and upheld the repudiation.

Insured claimed Rs. 75,366 for excision of lesion in armpit and groin. Insurer offered Rs. 55,614. Ombudsman reviewed surgical fees and directed insurer to settle for Rs. 65,614 along with 6% simple interest.

Insured claimed Rs. 20,000 for father's hospitalisation due to uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. Insurer repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1 for pre-existing disease. Medical records confirmed long-standing diabetes predating the policy, and Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured claimed Rs. 9,407.50 for wife's one-day hospitalisation for chest pain and tests. Insurer repudiated under exclusion clause 4.10 for investigation-only admission. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as tests could be performed on an outpatient basis.

Insured claimed Rs. 52,500 for coronary artery disease and angioplasty. Insurer repudiated as pre-existing. Insured admitted having pre-existing hypertension but not disclosing it. Ombudsman upheld repudiation due to non-disclosure of material fact.

Insured claimed expenses for coronary angiography. Insurer delayed and failed to process. Records showed a 15-year history of hypertension leading to triple vessel coronary artery disease prior to the proposal. Ombudsman held the claim not tenable.

Insured's husband was hospitalized for cardio-respiratory arrest. Insurer repudiated claiming non-disclosure of a stroke 10 years prior. Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim taking the sum insured as Rs. 1,50,000.

Insured claimed for wife's bilateral femoral thromboemboectomy due to rheumatic heart disease. Insurer repudiated citing pre-existing condition and a break in policy continuity. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured claimed Rs. 44,476.20 for calculous cholecystitis (gallbladder stones) surgery within a month of taking the policy. Insurer repudiated under clauses 4.1 and 4.2 for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured claimed hospitalisation expenses for cervical spondylosis and related investigations. Insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.10 as hospitalisation was not essential and done purely for diagnostic purposes. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured claimed for thyroidectomy with multimodular goitre. Insurer repudiated under clause 4.1 based on a US hospital report. Ombudsman noted duration was unproven in foreign papers and directed insurer to entertain the claim and pay admissible expenses.

Insured claimed for unstable angina and diabetes mellitus. Insurer repudiated due to policy lapse and renewal delay, treating it as a fresh policy. As the insured filed a writ petition in the High Court, the Ombudsman adjourned proceedings pending court outcome.

Insured claimed Rs. 1,13,600.95 for ureteric colic treatment, but insurer settled for Rs. 1,03,656, disallowing Rs. 6,701. Finding it purely administrative, the Ombudsman reverted the case to the insurer to resolve based on policy terms.

Insured claimed for hospitalization due to diabetes mellitus, cerebrovascular accident, and ischemic heart disease. Medical records revealed a 15-20 year history of proven diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman held the claim not sustainable.

Insured had an accidental fall in USA causing right femoral neck fracture and right shoulder injury. The insurer repudiated the hip replacement part based on a specific policy exclusion, but approved settlement for the shoulder treatment. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and ordered payment of the approved shoulder treatment amount.

Insured claimed reimbursement for cardiac hospitalisation due to severe aortic stenosis. The insurer repudiated the claim on the ground of pre-existing disease based on tests dating back years. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as the cardiac condition was long-standing and pre-existing.

Insured's wife underwent cardiac treatment including CABG. The insurer repudiated the claim and refused policy renewal alleging non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and ischaemic heart disease. The Ombudsman held that the repudiation was not sustainable and ruled in favor of the complainant.

Insured underwent surgery for stomach cancer followed by chemotherapy and radiotherapy. The insurer paid for surgery but rejected chemotherapy and radiotherapy expenses. The Ombudsman held that post-surgery cancer treatments are part of one continuous illness and directed the insurer to pay admissible expenses up to the sum insured.

Insured's wife was hospitalised for diagnostic hysteroscopy and hysterectomy. The insurer settled the claim after making certain deductions. The complainant contested the partial deduction. The Ombudsman found the insurer's deductions and application of reasonable expenses in order and dismissed the complaint.

Insured was hospitalised for heart treatment at a health foundation that was not registered as a hospital or nursing home under local authorities, leading to repudiation. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation under policy definitions but awarded an ex-gratia lump sum payment considering the valid ayurvedic/heart treatment received.

Insured was hospitalized for a heart attack and angioplasty. The insurer repudiated the claim citing non-disclosure of pre-existing medical history including epilepsy and spinal tuberculosis in the proposal form. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision due to material non-disclosure.

Insured's wife was hospitalised for anxiety neurosis. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds that hospitalisation was not necessary and treatment could have been handled on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman sustained the insurer's rejection under the relevant exclusion clause.

Insured lodged a claim for hospitalisation due to idiopathic gynaecomastia, which the TPA rejected as pre-existing. During the ombudsman proceedings, the insurer settled the claim by issuing a cheque to the complainant, closing the case.

Insured was hospitalised for recurrent adenoma prostatis and underwent TURP. The insurer repudiated the claim due to a break in policy continuity and non-disclosure of a past TURP operation done years prior. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle 50% of admissible expenses on an ex-gratia basis.

Insured was hospitalised for acute tracheo bronchitis. The insurer repudiated the claim alleging inflated bills based on investigation reports. The Ombudsman found no conclusive proof of fraud but directed a lump sum partial payment as suggested by the TPA.

Insured was hospitalised for growth hormone releasing pituitary tumour (acromegaly). The insurer repudiated the claim stating it was a pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as medical evidence proved the chronic and pre-existing nature of the condition prior to policy inception.

Insured underwent PTCA and stenting for CAD. The insurer offered partial settlement based on the original sum insured prior to an enhancement, citing a pre-existing history of myocardial infarction predating the sum insured increase. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's calculation based on the lower sum insured tier.

Insured claimed reimbursement for his wife's hospitalisation for hypertension, COPD, and pulmonary tuberculosis, which the insurer repudiated. As the complainant had also approached a Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum for the same issue, the Ombudsman dismissed the complaint without going into merits.

Insured's wife was hospitalised for unstable angina and segmental lumbar spondylosis. The insurer rejected the claim on the grounds that hospitalisation was unnecessary and management could have been done on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured underwent a second staged operation for pelvic abscess with diverticulitis under a renewed policy. The insurer rejected the claim alleging the insured intentionally postponed the surgery to claim under the new policy. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation, holding that a short delay without medical emergency does not invalidate the claim.

Insured underwent coronary angioplasty following a sudden myocardial infarction. The insurer repudiated the claim stating that diabetes and hypertension were pre-existing and undisclosed at proposal. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation, noting the established medical nexus between diabetes, hypertension, and CAD.

Insured was hospitalised for hyponatraemia due to SIADH. The insurer repudiated the claim based on a policy exclusion for heart and circulatory diseases. The Ombudsman observed mixed contributory causes and lack of conclusive proof, directing the insurer to pay 50% of the hospitalisation expenses.

Insured underwent cataract surgery and preferred a claim. The insurer made deductions primarily on the surgeon's fees. The Ombudsman reviewed the case and awarded a higher partial settlement amount as a fair via media solution.

Insured was hospitalised for cirrhosis of the liver with portal hypertension and subsequently passed away. The insurer repudiated the claim under policy exclusion for pre-existing diseases, noting a policy break and long-standing liver disease history. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured claimed reimbursement for spouse's hospitalisation for migraine and diagnostic tests lasting less than 24 hours. Insurer repudiated as hospitalisation was unnecessary and could be done as an outpatient, violating policy conditions.

Claim for eye surgery for Myopic Choroidal Neovascularisation was rejected by the insurer on grounds of pre-existing long myopia and non-disclosure. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on medical opinions that myopia set in childhood.

Insured contested a 100% premium loading charged by the insurer due to high claim ratio. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint, stating underwriting and premium fixing issues fall outside his jurisdiction under RPG Rules.
Claim for Myringoplasty surgery of the ear in a first-year policy was rejected due to pre-existing chronic ear inflammation dating back to childhood. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured's claim for angioplasty was partially settled after an administrative reduction of the sum insured without proper intimation or refund. Ombudsman held the company's action irregular and ordered full payment.

Claims for renal failure and kidney transplant in the first policy year were rejected under exclusion clauses for congenital and pre-existing polycystic kidney disease. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insurer offered partial payment for husband's hospitalisation citing sum insured limits, ignoring a prior enhancement. Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim based on the enhanced sum of Rs. 2,00,000.

Claim for bypass surgery was partially settled by the TPA on the old sum insured, alleging pre-existing heart disease. Ombudsman found no conclusive proof of pre-existence and ordered settlement on the enhanced sum insured.

Claim for lumbo discogenic surgery after 3 years of policy inception was rejected due to past back pain history. Ombudsman considered the pain of recent origin and allowed 50% of the claim on an ex-gratia basis.

Insured complained of short settlement for hospitalisation expenses. Ombudsman directed the insurer to re-verify disallowed items against submitted prescriptions and documents to pay any valid additional amount.

Claim for hernia surgery was partially paid after the insurer slashed charges citing market standards. Ombudsman reviewed benchmark rates and ordered a slight upward revision for surgery and anesthetist charges.

Claim for post-menopausal bleeding and polyp removal in the second policy year was repudiated because the condition was treated previously in 1998 and constituted a pre-existing non-disclosure. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Claim for pelvic endometriosis surgery was rejected under pregnancy and sterility exclusions. Expert medical opinion confirmed endometriosis is a disease independent of fertility status. Ombudsman set aside repudiation and ordered settlement.

Claim for obstructed ventral hernia surgery was rejected under pre-existing clauses due to a 1993 umbilical hernia and a 2001 surgery. Ombudsman ruled that the 2001 surgery broke the chain of causation and ordered full settlement.
Claim for cardiac/giddiness hospitalisation was rejected due to suppression of pre-existing hypertension and diabetes history. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's repudiation.

Claim for angiography and angioplasty was repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and borderline diabetes. Hospital records confirmed conscious suppression of history. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim for cataract surgery was rejected because a 5-month policy gap caused National Insurance to treat it as a fresh policy subject to first-year exclusions. Ombudsman awarded 50% on an ex-gratia basis due to administrative continuity issues.
Claim for excision of axillary lipomas was rejected because the policy explicitly excluded diabetes, which caused ulceration of the lipomas. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for severe complications and surgery following initial Ayurvedic treatment for fistula-in-ano with allopathic medicines was rejected. Ombudsman allowed 25% of expenses incurred at the hospital for emergency treatment.

Claim for sub-arachnoid haemorrhage due to aneurysm in the first policy year was repudiated due to non-disclosure of childhood headaches indicating a pre-existing congenital defect. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured preferred claims for myocardial infarction and bypass surgery. Insurer repudiated based on non-disclosure of hypertension and lack of cooperation in providing treatment particulars. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured hospitalized for prostatic hypertrophy and TURP. Claim repudiated due to non-disclosure of prior UTI and symptoms. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.
Insured hospitalized for myocardial infarction. Insurer partially settled, excluding enhanced sum insured due to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Complainant approached Consumer Forum.
Insured's wife treated for cardiac arrhythmia (ventricular tachycardia). Insurer repudiated claim invoking exclusion for pre-existing conditions and diabetes. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.
Claim for breast cancer treatment repudiated due to non-disclosure of prior surgical removal of a benign breast lump. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stance.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for memory loss and transient ischaemic attack rejected because hospitalization was only for investigation and related to pre-existing hypertension with altered medical records. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for head injury from a fall repudiated under exclusion clause regarding alcohol consumption, as hospital records showed the patient was under the influence of alcohol.

insurer: The United India Insurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for interstitial lung disorder and pulmonary hypertension repudiated due to non-disclosure of pre-existing asthma and lung disease. Ombudsman upheld the decision.

insurer: The United India Insurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for CABG surgery repudiated due to non-disclosure of long-standing hypertension and high cholesterol. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for post renal transplant treatment repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension linked to renal failure. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for retinal detachment surgery rejected due to non-disclosure of prior cataract surgery and high myopia. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for surgery of Patent Ductus Arteriosus in a child repudiated as a congenital internal disease excluded under the policy. Ombudsman upheld the decision.
Claim for CABG and TVD repudiated due to pre-existing hypertension and diabetes. Considering long policy continuity and past settled claims, Ombudsman recommended 50% ex-gratia settlement.
Claim for angioplasty and IHD repudiated on grounds of pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision due to medical nexus between hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and heart disease.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for excision of scalp swelling rejected under exclusion 4.1. Since the policy was continuous for 9 years and the swelling was initially silent without prior knowledge, Ombudsman held the claim tenable.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for hospitalization following a fall and quadriplegia rejected under exclusion 4.8 due to alcohol consumption (hangover) and non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and physical deformities. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for duodenitis and piles repudiated on grounds that colonoscopy was purely an investigative procedure not requiring hospitalization. Ombudsman held hospitalisation was justified due to symptoms requiring sedation and monitoring, making the claim tenable.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for cancer, pulmonary kochs, and hepatitis rejected because the insured was HIV positive, which falls under exclusion clause 4.9. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insurer short-paid a cancer claim and forced a renewal with a cancer exclusion. Ombudsman set aside the insurer's decision to treat the policy as fresh and upheld the complaint against unfair underwriting practices.

Complaint regarding delay and lack of processing for a heart attack claim handled through a marketing agency and public sector insurer. Ombudsman directed the agencies to resolve the matter per policy terms.

Insured hospitalized for anginal pain. Insurer repudiated claim under clause 4.10 stating hospitalization was avoidable and solely for investigations which could be done as outpatient. Ombudsman found the complaint not sustainable.

Claim for breast cancer treatment rejected due to pre-existing disease exclusion. Family was previously covered by same insurer under a different policy. Ombudsman noted merits in insurer's stand but ordered 50 percent ex-gratia settlement.

Claim for heart ailment repudiated as pre-existing due to long-standing diabetes and hypertension. Medical records confirmed history of diabetes for over 15 years. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Daughter hospitalized for malignant hypertension. Insurer rejected claim alleging pre-existing disease. Ombudsman observed that hypertension was sudden and detected only three months prior, and policy had run for nearly two years, making repudiation unsustainable.

Claim for son's congenital heart ailment and subsequent CABG repudiated due to non-disclosure and exclusion clauses. Earlier policy was cancelled for non-disclosure and new policy was within waiting period. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.
Claim for cataract and glaucoma surgery rejected as pre-existing since condition could not develop in 18 months. Doctor certified cataract as hyper-mature. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.

Claim for IHD and CAD repudiated on grounds of pre-existing diabetes. Insurer had noticed high blood sugar in proposal but did not apply exclusion. Ombudsman directed 50 percent settlement of admissible expenses.

Claim for coronary artery disease and bypass surgery rejected due to policy break and pre-existing diabetes/hypertension. Insurer had insured him for 12 years with a 12-day break. Ombudsman set aside total rejection and ordered partial settlement.

Claim for knee injury from an accident rejected because the accident occurred prior to the effective date of insurance renewal following a gap. Investigation and railway records confirmed the accident date fell outside coverage. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.

Claim for coronary angiography and echocardiogram rejected on grounds of short hospitalization and diagnostic purpose under clause 4.10. Insured had continuous coverage for years without claims. Ombudsman found complaint sustainable for full settlement.
Claim for prostate hypertrophy and diagnostic tests rejected under clause 4.10 due to lack of 24-hour hospitalization. Insurer paid health check-up benefit. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.

Claim for hospitalization solely for coronary angiography rejected under clause 4.10. Patient had hypertension and underwent invasive catheterization. Ombudsman awarded 50 percent of admissible expenses.
Claim for IHD and diabetes hospitalization rejected under clause 4.10 for being diagnostic. Angiography confirmed double vessel disease requiring medical management. Ombudsman held the claim tenable.

Claim for heart attack treatment and subsequent death rejected as pre-existing based on post-death cardiological review. Insurer had medically examined the 72-year-old insured at inception and issued policy without exclusions. Ombudsman ordered 50 percent settlement.
Claim for Hepatitis C treatment repudiated under clause 4.1 as pre-existing. In the absence of conclusive proof of infected blood transfusion, Ombudsman ordered 50 percent ex-gratia settlement.

Claim for appendicitis, MTP, sterilisation, and subsequent pulmonary edema rejected for pregnancy-related exclusions. Insurer partially paid but denied MTP and respiratory care. Ombudsman found partial payment in order and granted 50 percent of Hinduja hospital expenses.
Claim for laparatomy and abdominal wall repair rejected because complications stemmed from prior excluded surgeries (hysterectomy, hernia, appendicitis). Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.

Claim for hospitalization for coronary angiography rejected under clause 4.10 as purely diagnostic without emergency. Stress test was positive for ischaemia and angiography showed minor blockage. Ombudsman upheld insurer's repudiation.

Claim for CABG hospitalization settled partially after accounting for prior hospitalizations and post-hospitalization expense limits under policy terms. Ombudsman found the insurer's calculation in order.

Claim for coronary angiography rejected under clause 4.10 as diagnostic. Insured experienced chest discomfort, had positive stress test, underwent angiography, and later bypass surgery. Ombudsman found the claim sustainable.

Insured underwent treatment for Vatha Vikaram at a nursing home involving natural therapy. Insurer repudiated under general debility and naturopathy exclusion clauses. Ombudsman found some ailments existed and ordered payment of 25% of admissible expenses on an ex-gratia basis.

Insured's minor son underwent emergency surgery for circumcision due to phimosis and balanoposthitis. Insurer rejected the claim citing exclusion for circumcision and lack of 24-hour hospitalization. Ombudsman set aside the repudiation as it was an emergency surgery and directed payment of admissible expenses.

Insured suffered multiple fractures in a car accident abroad under an Overseas Mediclaim Policy and returned to India for major surgery. Insurer and settling agents failed to respond to the claim. Ombudsman directed reimbursement of treatment costs incurred in Mumbai.

Insured was hospitalized for typhoid. Insurer repudiated the claim alleging fraudulent alteration of discharge dates in hospital records. Ombudsman found no conclusive proof of fraud by the insured, but noted discrepancies, ordering a 50% settlement of the claim.

Insured was hospitalized for inguinal hernia and benign prostatic hypertrophy during the first year of the policy. Insurer rejected the claim under first-year exclusion. Ombudsman confirmed that diagnosis was established during the first policy year and surgery was delayed, upholding the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Policyholder hospitalized for liver cirrhosis and portal hypertension, later passed away. Insurer rejected claims citing pre-existing condition and alcohol abuse exclusion. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision given the established history of chronic alcoholism.

Claim for daughter's squint correction surgery was rejected by the insurer on grounds of pre-existing disease and congenital defect. Ombudsman noted the condition existed since age nine and before policy inception, upholding the repudiation.

Insured preferred a high-value claim for cardiac hospitalization. Insurer offered settlement restricted to original sum insured plus cumulative bonus, ignoring a subsequent sum insured increase. Ombudsman upheld settlement based on the base sum insured and cumulative bonus.

Under an Overseas Mediclaim Policy, insured sought reimbursement for a wheelchair purchased after an accident abroad. Insurer rejected the claim. Ombudsman held that external aids like wheelchairs are not covered medical expenses, upholding the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured underwent CABG surgery and claimed enhanced sum insured. Insurer restricted settlement to original sum insured due to pre-existing ischemic heart disease detected prior to enhancement. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's restricted payout.

Insured hospitalized for slipped disc surgery. Insurer scaled down surgeon fees based on panel expert advice and partially settled the claim. Ombudsman awarded an additional amount to resolve the long-standing dispute.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for knee haemarthrosis hospitalization was repudiated by TPA on grounds that it did not require hospitalization. Ombudsman relaxed the necessity clause given the patient's age, sedation, and risk of complications from IV injections, allowing the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured underwent bypass surgery following cardiac complications. Insurer repudiated claim because declared diabetes and related complications were excluded under the policy terms. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured's spouse was hospitalized for intestinal tear and surgery. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing abdominal tuberculosis and non-disclosure of past illness in proposal. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured's spouse underwent total abdominal hysterectomy for longstanding adenomyosis shortly after the first policy year expired. Insurer repudiated claim for pre-existing disease. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured challenged deduction of admission and registration charges from her hospital claim. Ombudsman found the deductions appropriate under the group policy terms and declined to interfere.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was admitted to cardiac clinic for hypertension control. Insurer rejected claim on grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as there was no medical emergency justifying inpatient admission.

Insured passed away following aortic rupture due to arteriosclerosis during the first policy year. Insurer repudiated claim for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and diabetes. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on records.
Claim for para umbilical hernia repair was rejected by insurer due to non-disclosure of a prior caesarean section and pre-existing scar weakness causing the hernia. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Elderly insured hospitalized for uterine fibroids, hypertension, and other conditions. TPA repudiated the claim citing lack of necessity for hospitalization and excess investigations. Ombudsman approved 70% of the claim cost considering her advanced age.
Insured hospitalized for unstable angina and coronary artery disease. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing hypertension not disclosed in proposal. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.
Insured underwent angiography for ischemic heart disease. Claim rejected as longstanding hypertension was not disclosed at inception. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.
Insured hospitalized for secondary infertility and ovarian endometrioma. Claim repudiated under exclusion clause for sterility or infertility treatment. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.
Insured hospitalized for renal failure with diabetes and hypertension, and subsequently expired. Claim repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing ailments. Ombudsman upheld the decision.
Insured died of acute cardio-respiratory arrest following stroke and myocardial infarction. Claim rejected due to pre-existing diabetes. Ombudsman ordered 30% ex-gratia payment.
Insured hospitalized for chronic liver disease and congestive cardiac failure. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing un-disclosed cardiac issues and diabetes. Ombudsman upheld rejection.
Insured's daughter underwent surgery for right eye squint. Claim rejected under exclusion for cosmetic or congenital conditions. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Insured hospitalized for diabetes, gastritis, reflux oesophagitis, and hypertension. Claim repudiated for pre-existing conditions. Ombudsman ordered 20% payment for the new gastritis complication.
Insured hospitalized for diabetes, depression, and uterine prolapse. Claim repudiated for non-disclosure. Ombudsman directed settlement of 20% of expenses for proportionate treatment.
