Insured hospitalized for pulmonary tuberculosis and hepatitis triggered by treatment drugs. Claim repudiated for pre-existing illness. Ombudsman allowed 50% of hospitalisation expenses.
Insured underwent angioplasty for coronary heart disease. Claim rejected because long-standing diabetes caused the cardiovascular condition. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Insured hospitalized for iron deficiency anaemia. Claim rejected as hospitalisation was deemed unnecessary since investigations could be done as an outpatient. Ombudsman upheld rejection.
Insured underwent bilateral lower limb angiography for diabetic microangiopathy. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing diabetes. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Insured's son hospitalized for ear cholesteatoma. Claim rejected due to policy gap and non-disclosure of pre-existing condition. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Insured hospitalized for cancer treatment. Claim repudiated due to short gap in policy renewal and pre-existing disease. Ombudsman ordered full claim settlement given long history.
Insured admitted for chest pain and diagnosed with hiatus hernia. Claim rejected for pre-existing illness and investigation-only stay. Ombudsman allowed 50% of the claim.
Insured hospitalized for gall bladder stones surgery. Claim rejected for pre-existing cholelithiasis, but insurer offered restricted sum. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial payout.
Insured hospitalized for acute renal failure. Claim repudiated due to non-disclosure of past ailments and pre-existing condition. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Insured hospitalized for backache and abdominal pain. Claim repudiated as confinement was under 24 hours and tests could be done as outpatient. Ombudsman upheld rejection.
Insured underwent cataract surgery following a policy renewal with a 13-day gap. Claim rejected as first-year claim. Ombudsman set aside repudiation considering long prior continuous coverage.

Insured underwent excision of multiple lipomas in the right forearm. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.5 for cosmetic surgery. The Ombudsman observed that investigation and removal were necessary to rule out malignancy and ordered the insurer to settle 50% of the admissible expenses.

Insured was hospitalized for hepatic encephalopathy and unfortunately expired due to cardiopulmonary arrest with diabetes mellitus and cirrhosis of liver. The insurer repudiated the claim under general debility exclusion. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection due to non-disclosure of long-standing diabetes and prior abdominal ailments existing before the policy inception.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for anterior wall infarction. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing diabetes mellitus, non-disclosure, and non-cooperation for failing to provide past medical records. The Ombudsman noted inconclusive proof of duration and directed the insurer to pay 50% of the expenses incurred.

Insured claimed reimbursement for his wife's bilateral cataract surgeries. The insurer made deductions based on top hospital rate charts, deeming charges excessive. The Ombudsman found the hospital charges steep and proper for standard deductions, but recommended an additional sanction of Rs. 6,000 for surgeon fees.

Insured sought reimbursement for hospitalization due to diabetic foot resulting in amputation. The insurer repudiated the claim under pre-existing disease exclusion based on medical notes showing diabetes of long duration. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as the severity of the condition suggested age-old disease.

Insured was hospitalized for ischaemic heart disease, upper GI bleed, and haematemesis. The insurer repudiated the claim due to non-disclosure of past myocardial infarction and pre-existing heart disease after a policy break. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection based on material non-disclosure and false statements.

Insured preferred a claim for hospitalization due to incisional hernia. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing condition and non-disclosure of a past caesarean section performed 14 years earlier. The Ombudsman upheld the decision, stating the previous incision acted as a predisposing pre-existing factor.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was hospitalized for bleeding, diabetes, hypertension, and underwent hysterectomy. The insurer repudiated the claim under pre-existing disease exclusion. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection due to non-disclosure of prior cataract surgery and ongoing medication for diabetes and hypertension at inception.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was admitted to an ayurvedic hospital for cervical spondylosis treatment. The insurer rejected the claim stating hospitalization was not necessary. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection, noting the long stay was for general wellness and inconsistent with policy terms for acute necessity.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured's husband was hospitalized for hypertensive heart disease for less than 24 hours. The insurer rejected the claim under less than 24 hours and exclusion clauses. The Ombudsman found the emergency nature justified and noted the policy had been active since 1997, making hypertension non-pre-existing, thus setting aside the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was hospitalized for interstitial lung disease and breast cancer, and subsequently expired. The insurer repudiated the claim. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection because the insured failed to disclose past treatment for breast cancer and ongoing chemotherapy in the proposal form.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent prostate surgery for benign prostatic hypertrophy. The insurer repudiated the claim under pre-existing disease exclusion. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection based on medical certificates confirming urinary symptoms dating back 10 years prior to the policy.

Insured was hospitalized for removal of an intradural extramedullary tumour with decompressive laminectomy. The insurer rejected the claim on grounds of non-disclosure and pre-existing ailment. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection based on conclusive MRI and clinical findings.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured claimed reimbursement for fees paid in cash to an assistant cardiac surgeon during angioplasty. The insurer settled the main bill but deducted the assistant's cash fee. The Ombudsman upheld the deduction as cash payments lack proper substantiation and necessity was not established.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was hospitalized for excision of a mass on his vocal cord. The insurer rejected the claim because he had a similar vocal nodule operation 20 years prior, constituting non-disclosure and a pre-existing condition. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured was hospitalized at a hospital for fever evaluation. The insurer rejected the claim stating investigations could be done on an outpatient basis. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection under policy terms requiring necessary hospitalization, noting tests were routine outpatient procedures.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for total abdominal hysterectomy. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing menorrhagia and hypertension. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as records showed a history of menorrhagia and hypertension prior to policy inception.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for supra ventricular tachycardia and anemia. The insurer repudiated the claim due to undisclosed pre-existing hypertension. The Ombudsman noted lack of proof linking hypertension to the diagnosis and directed the insurer to pay 50% of the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for abdominal pain and diagnosed with thickening of the IC junction through colonoscopy. The insurer rejected the claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary. The Ombudsman held that hospital admission was required for diagnosis and directed the insurer to entertain the claim.

Insured underwent total abdominal hysterectomy. The insurer rejected the claim due to pre-existing gynecological disorders and past treatments not disclosed. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection, noting a policy break and extensive prior history related to the current surgery.
Insured died of cardiac and hepatic failure. Insurer repudiated the claim because heart ailments were specifically excluded under the policy terms. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for heart failure treatment was rejected by insurer due to pre-existing diabetes and cardiomyopathy. Medical reports indicated a chronic condition predating policy inception. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Claim for hip replacement was restricted to original sum insured prior to enhancement. However, insurer was ordered to pay for concurrent treatment of Crohn's disease and ulcers under the long-standing policy.
Claim for hospitalization due to chest pain was repudiated as admission was solely for investigations. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Insured underwent angiography and angioplasty. Insurer paid original sum insured of 1 lakh as cashless. Ombudsman directed insurer to settle an additional 50 percent of the remaining balance claim.

Claim for bile duct stone treatment was repudiated under exclusion clause regarding gall bladder. Since insurer had paid an earlier related claim for acute cholangitis, repudiation was held unsustainable.

Claim for meningitis, pneumonia, and COPD was rejected as pre-existing and undisclosed. Considering 12 years of continuous policy operation and advanced age, Ombudsman awarded 50 percent of admissible expenses as a special case.
Claim for ureteric colic rejected due to non-disclosure of past left ureteric calculi surgery 7 years prior. Repudiation upheld.
Claim repudiated because hospitalization was for observation following an accident. Ombudsman ruled hospitalization was on doctor's advice and ordered full payment.
Insurer deducted an amount without justification but paid the balance upon receiving notice of hearing. Complaint settled in full.
Fissurectomy/fistula claim was excluded, but stricture of urethra resulted from an accidental fall. Ombudsman applied rule of thumb and ordered 60 percent payout.
Hernia claim repudiated under first-year exclusion clause, but hospitalization occurred in the second policy year. Repudiation set aside and full claim awarded.
Disputed deductions for medicines and ambulance charges for head injury were challenged. Ombudsman ruled ambulance and prescribed medicines were admissible, partly allowing the complaint.
Multiple claims for renal failure, hypertension, and diabetes rejected due to non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and diabetes in proposal form. Repudiation upheld.
Claim for ruptured ectopic pregnancy rejected as complication of prior undisclosed gynaecological surgery. Repudiation upheld.
Bypass surgery claim repudiated for alleged suppression of prostatectomy during sum insured enhancement. Since the same branch processed both renewal and settlement, repudiation was set aside.
Claim for carcinoma of buccal mucosa rejected based on tobacco chewing history. In absence of indisputable proof of pre-existence, repudiation was set aside.
Dental treatment and TIA claims. Dental expenses beyond 60 days were rejected, but Ombudsman ruled continuous treatment rules should not defeat the policy purpose and ordered payment.
Hernia surgery for 4-year-old rejected as congenital pre-existing condition. Child specialist certificates contradicted insurer; insurer ordered to pay claim.
Congenital heart disease claim treated as pre-existing based on cardiologist opinion. Repudiation upheld with no relief.

Insured hospitalized for sinus surgery after policy was 1 year old. Admitted in writing to suffering from cold, allergy, and nasal obstruction for years prior to inception. Repudiation for pre-existing disease upheld.
Claim for coronary angiography was repudiated because hospitalization was solely for investigation. Ombudsman noted instructions to decide angiography on merits and directed full payment.
Hospitalization for acute chest pain was rejected as being for investigations. Ombudsman ruled that severe chest pain led to admission under a qualified doctor, so full claim must be paid.
Claim for acute chest pain rejected for unjustified hospitalization. Ombudsman directed full payment since admission was on cardiologist's advice due to severe symptoms.
Claim for cardiovascular stroke and hypertension repudiated for non-disclosure of prior kidney and valve treatments. Repudiation upheld.
Claim for interest due to delay dismissed because payment had already been accepted via a signed discharge voucher in full and final settlement.
Claim for tenosynovitis repudiated on grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. Ombudsman noted admission was per specialist advice and ordered payment of Rs. 2,844.
Hernia treatment claim rejected under first-year exclusion clause. Fresh proposal submitted without declaring previous policies, treating it as a first-year policy.
Cataract surgery under householders policy repudiated due to underwriting rule restricting claims if policy taken above age 50. Ombudsman upheld complainant since rule was never disclosed.
Mediclaim repudiated for lack of hospitalization necessity. Ombudsman ruled that once hospitalization occurs on medical advice, subsequent treatment type is medical management. Ordered Rs. 4,273.
Repudiation for unjustified hospitalization set aside since patient followed expert doctor's advice. Treating doctor's advice prevails over insurer referee's opinion.
Heart disease claim repudiated due to pre-existing hypertension noted in the family physician's first certificate. Repudiation upheld.
Repudiation for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure set aside as insurer could not prove exact dates or produce proposal form. Ordered Rs. 70,337.

Mediclaim for road traffic accident with head injury rejected as fit for OPD. Ombudsman set aside repudiation noting accident and hospital admission were genuine, and personal accident claim was paid.
Claim for heart disease rejected for lack of ICU intravenous treatment. Ombudsman held treating doctor's advice is paramount and awarded Rs. 4,965.
Mediclaim repudiated because hospitalization for head injury debridement and suturing lasted less than 24 hours and did not meet listed exceptions. Repudiation upheld.
Repudiation for knee trauma hospitalization lasting under 24 hours set aside. Treating doctor's advice and prescribed rest justified admission.
Claim for anemia treatment in a child within the first 30 days of policy inception was correctly repudiated under clause 4.2.
Mediclaim repudiated for non-disclosure of recent hospitalizations for kidney stone and tract dilation just two months before policy inception. Repudiation upheld.
Claim for wife's treatment rejected as complainant could not substantiate that a proposal was submitted to cover her; premium was used to enhance his own sum insured.

Mediclaim was repudiated on the ground that hospitalisation was for investigation only. The insured was admitted for severe pain in left upper limb and neck indicating cardiac origin, confirmed by treating neurologist. Ombudsman held hospitalization was necessary and set aside repudiation.

Claim rejected as accidental injuries did not require 24 hours hospitalization. Surgeon certified necessity and duration. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 2,908. In a separate case involving same insurer, ambulance charges and lumber support were denied, but nursing charges for home care post spine surgery were allowed.

Claim for Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia was rejected as pre-existing based on history notes. Since there was no definite proof of date and policy ran continuously for six years, benefit of doubt went to insured. Full claim awarded.

Treatment for IHD, LVF, and UTI was taken after a 3-day break in policy renewal. Due to the break, the policy was treated as fresh from the renewal date, making the condition pre-existing and non-admissible. Complaint dismissed.
Claim repudiated because chest pain was musculoskeletal and could be managed on OPD basis. Ombudsman noted complainant's age and late night emergency, set aside repudiation, and ordered full payment.

Cashless facility for angiography was refused by TPA. Ombudsman held that policy provides reimbursement and cashless mode refusal is beyond forum's jurisdiction. Several other clubbed cases on prostate surgery, accident paperwork, diabetes complications, and knee replacement were dismissed.
Claim for sebaceous cyst excision repudiated because hospital stay was under 24 hours due to modern technology. Insurer agreed claim was genuine. Ombudsman directed full payment of Rs. 2,400.

Claim for fibroid uterus surgery during the first policy year was excluded under clause 4.3. Repudiation justified. In other clubbed cases, hospitalization for investigation of vertigo and non-disclosure of prior knee pain leading to knee replacement were also dismissed.

Claim rejected on grounds that hospitalization following a vehicular accident was not required. Treating doctor confirmed need for round-the-clock parenteral analgesics. Ombudsman held medical referee opinion cannot override treating doctor and ordered payment of Rs. 2,620.

Insurer partially paid medical expenses, allowing only Rs. 3,000 for a disposable hernia stapler costing Rs. 12,200. Operating surgeon justified necessity. Ombudsman directed insurer to pay full stapler cost of Rs. 12,200.

Mediclaim for nasal obstruction repudiated due to pre-existing condition of recurrent cold spanning 12-15 years. Repudiation upheld. In a connected case, temporary total disablement (TTD) period for ankle fracture was increased to 11 weeks and Rs. 33,000 awarded.

Claim for hospitalization due to major anxiety and depression disorder with suicide risk was rejected for lack of necessity. Repudiation set aside given the critical nature of the condition certified by an MD physician. Rs. 6,076 awarded.
Claim for cystoscopy hospitalization was repudiated under clause 4.1 since admission was strictly for further investigation advised by urologist. Repudiation upheld by Ombudsman.

Claim repudiated as hospitalization for hypoproteinemia and renal proteinuria was deemed unnecessary by medical referee. Treating physician's advice for stabilization and renal biopsy prevailed. Repudiation set aside and Rs. 6,862 awarded.

Fever contracted within 30 days of policy inception was rightly repudiated under clause 4.2. In a clubbed case, gynaecological bleeding caused by an old retained IUCD inserted in 1974 was held not to be a pre-existing disease, and Rs. 27,500 was awarded.

Claim for thromboembolic complications following past valve replacement was repudiated because cardiac problems were explicitly excluded in the policy schedule. Repudiation upheld. In another case, execution of an unqualified discharge voucher barred reopening the claim.

Claim repudiated based on medical referee's opinion that pelvic inflammatory disease did not require hospitalization. Treating physician's certificate confirmed diagnosis and need for treatment. Repudiation set aside.

Hospitalization for renal stone within months of policy inception was repudiated under waiting period exclusion. Other clubbed matters included partial settlement of knee arthritis, separate knee replacements treated as independent illnesses, non-disclosure of past fevers, and hospital non-compliance.

Cataract claim repudiated due to exclusion. Although exclusions were inadvertently omitted from the policy document, the error was corrected prior to treatment, so no contractual benefit arose. In a separate case, renal failure non-disclosure justified repudiation.

CABG claim unsettled due to complainant's failure to provide past health reports. Investigation revealed prior treadmill tests within six months of policy inception, contradicting complainant's statements. Repudiation upheld.

Insured underwent angioplasty for coronary artery disease. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing disease based on panel doctor opinion. Ombudsman noted lack of definitive evidence of prior existence and ordered payment of Rs. 184,996.

Complainant incurred medical expenses abroad under an overseas mediclaim policy. Claim was delayed due to inaction by successive service providers. Ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the claim positively within the specified timeframe.

Complainant underwent surgery for Atrial Septal Defects. Insurer repudiated claim citing congenital disease exclusion. Ombudsman noted the policy schedule stated exclusion as none, and ordered insurer to pay Rs. 111,564.

Outpatient treatment claims were partially repudiated because the insured failed to submit original prescriptions and diagnostic test reports as required by policy conditions. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured's wife underwent hysterectomy for fibroid uterus. Claim was repudiated under first-year exclusion. Ombudsman noted the policy bond stated exclusion as none, and directed the insurer to pay Rs. 59,000.

Maternity claim was rejected by insurer due to delay in submission caused by administrative errors of the employer and TPA. Ombudsman held the insured was not responsible for the delay and ordered payment of Rs. 16,762.

Claim for bilateral hydrocele surgery during the first policy year was repudiated under policy exclusions. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as the insured failed to prove the condition was caused by a recent accident rather than being pre-existing.

Insured was hospitalized for a mild heart problem. Claim was repudiated on the grounds that the ailment resulted from pre-existing hypertension, even if the insured was unaware of it prior to admission. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Renewal of mediclaim policy had a 15-day gap due to delayed renewal notice. Insurer treated it as a fresh policy and rejected a claim as pre-existing. Ombudsman ordered condonation of the gap, settlement of the claim, and 7 percent interest for delay.

Claim for hospitalization due to syncope was repudiated on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary and related to pre-existing coronary artery disease. Ombudsman ruled the repudiation unjustified and ordered the liability to be admitted.

Insurer disallowed charges for air-conditioning and admission fees during hospitalization. Ombudsman held that air-conditioning charges cannot be denied without a specific bar against AC rooms and ordered reimbursement of AC and admission charges.

Claim for knee replacement following a fall was repudiated because the insured had both knees replaced earlier in 1995. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation, noting that artificial knee replacements are palliative and the disease process continues.

Cataract surgery claim was repudiated because the TPA detected a three-day gap in policy renewal and treated it as a fresh policy. Ombudsman ruled there was no valid reason not to condone the minor gap since a health certificate was submitted, and ordered the claim payable.

Cashless claim for scar contracture surgery following a prior accident was rejected because the earlier injury had not been formally claimed. During the hearing, the TPA agreed to pay. Ombudsman allowed the complaint with interest.

Claim for hospitalization following convulsions was repudiated on the ground that tests were normal and admission was only for investigation. Ombudsman ruled that convulsions constitute an acute deviation from health requiring hospitalization, allowing the complaint.

Insurer restricted bypass surgery claim reimbursement to the sum insured applicable when a prior heart ailment occurred in 1997, ignoring subsequent sum insured enhancements and 'none' recorded under excluded diseases. Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia payment of 50 percent of the balance claim.
Claim for lithotripsy treatment of renal calculi was repudiated as pre-existing based on medical records showing kidney stones predating policy inception. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for chronic kidney disease and cystitis was repudiated due to pre-existing renal failure since 1994. Ombudsman noted that the cystitis and bleeding treated during hospitalization were a distinct condition, and partly allowed the claim for cystitis treatment.

Claim for coronary artery bypass graft was repudiated on the ground that coronary artery disease was a complication of pre-existing hypertension and diabetes. Ombudsman ruled that hypertension alone was not proven as the sole proximate cause of CAD and allowed the claim.

Hospitalization claim for portal hypertension and liver biopsy was repudiated on the ground that admission was solely for investigation. Ombudsman found that the invasive procedure under general anesthesia warranted hospitalization and allowed the claim.

Insured underwent CAG and CABG. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing old myocardial infarction based on discharge summary, but lacked prior ECG records or definitive proof from policy inception date. Ombudsman held pre-existence was not conclusively proved and allowed the complaint.

Insured hospitalized for CAD and PTCA. Insurer rejected claim alleging pre-existing hypertension and coronary artery disease based on panel doctor assumptions. Ombudsman noted lack of medical evidence proving pre-existence before policy inception and allowed the claim.

Insured hospitalized for chest pain, which tests ruled out as cardiac. Incidental asymptomatic renal calculi was found but not treated. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion for investigative admissions without positive disease requiring treatment. Ombudsman upheld dismissal.

Insured underwent hysterectomy for fibroid uterus in the second policy year. Insurer rejected claim citing first-year exclusion for hysterectomy. Ombudsman noted treatment occurred in the second year, rendering the first-year exclusion inapplicable, and allowed the complaint.

Insured suffered knee injury from a fall and underwent surgery. Claim submitted after a nearly three-month delay instead of the stipulated 30 days. Insurer repudiated for late submission. Ombudsman held the delay did not materially alter the claim and allowed reimbursement.

Insured hospitalized for Brachial Neuralgia. Investigations were negative and treatment was merely analgesic medication manageable on an outpatient basis. Insurer rejected claim for lack of emergency or necessity of hospitalization. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Insured hospitalized for myocardial infarction. Insurer repudiated claim for non-disclosure and pre-existing hypertension. Discrepancies in medical records and attending doctor's statements failed to conclusively prove pre-existence at proposal date. Complaint allowed.

Insured underwent Ayurvedic treatment for cervical spondylosis. Insurer restricted claim to Rs. 25,000/- citing a sub-limit clause for non-allopathic treatments. Ombudsman found ambiguity in the policy clause wording and directed the insurer to pay the balance amount.

Claim for ectopic pregnancy under an overseas mediclaim policy was rejected due to general pregnancy exclusion. Ombudsman noted company circular stating termination of ectopic pregnancy is payable as it poses life danger, and allowed the complaint.

Claim for total abdominal hysterectomy due to fibroid uterus in the second policy year was repudiated on multiple incorrect grounds. Ombudsman noted fibroid uterus was diagnosed during the policy and exclusion for menorrhagia did not apply. Complaint allowed.

Insured died after hospitalization for Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and acute renal failure. Insurer restricted kidney treatment to Rs. 1,00,000/-. Ombudsman ordered a fresh, transparent bifurcation of expenses between kidney ailments and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

Insured hospitalized for stroke exhausted sum insured under 'Any One Illness' clause. Insurer denied further amounts. Ombudsman noted terminally ill status and continuous renewals, directing an ex-gratia payment of Rs. 1,00,000/-.

Claim for heart disease rejected under pre-existing exclusion after policy renewal following a break, despite policy print showing no exclusion. Ombudsman ordered a one-time ex-gratia payment due to the insurer's misleading policy print, denying continuity of benefits.

Insured diagnosed with urinary bladder cancer shortly after policy inception had history of painless hematuria three months prior. TPA and insurer rejected claim as pre-existing based on medical opinion. Ombudsman dismissed complaint due to prior symptom timeline.

Insured underwent kidney transplantation. Claim rejected as patient was a long-standing diabetic whose renal failure stemmed from diabetic nephropathy un-disclosed in proposal form. Ombudsman dismissed complaint due to non-disclosure of pre-existing diabetes.

Insured hospitalized for ischemic heart disease. Claim rejected on ground of cardiac exclusion and pre-existence, despite prior claim for same disease being paid and continuous renewals. Ombudsman held insurer's repudiation unjustified and allowed the complaint.

Insured admitted for severe mitral regurgitation and advised valve replacement. Claim rejected for pre-existing disease. Ombudsman noted continuous renewals since 1998 and accepted premium payment, ruling insurer cannot shirk responsibility. Complaint allowed.

Insured's son underwent ureteral reimplantation for bilateral grade IV vesico-ureteral reflux. Claim rejected as pre-existing under exclusion 4.1. Advanced stage diagnosis shortly after policy inception supported insurer's contention. Complaint dismissed.

Insured underwent right upper lobectomy and claimed expenses. Insurer rejected claim as pre-existing lung cancer. Treating doctor clarified disease was not pre-existing and patient was asymptomatic. Ombudsman ruled in favor of insured, allowing complaint.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured submitted outpatient treatment bills for esophageal cancer. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion 17 for outpatient treatment and minimum 48-hour hospitalization requirement. Ombudsman found no merit in complaint and dismissed it.

Insured was hospitalised for cirrhosis of the liver during a renewed policy period treated as fresh due to a break in insurance. The hospital records showed the disease was in an advanced stage, justifying rejection as a pre-existing condition.

Insured claimed for Hepatitis C and Hyper Spleenism after sudden blood vomiting. The insurer rejected it as pre-existing, but medical records and a treating hospital certificate confirmed symptoms manifested only a day prior, disproving prior existence.

Claim for bypass surgery was repudiated because hospital records revealed a history of chronic unstable angina, chest pain, and hypertension which were not disclosed in the proposal form, thereby suppressing material facts.

Insured's daughter was treated for blood cancer and the insurer partially paid before rejecting the rest based on the 'any one illness' clause. The Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount to mitigate financial hardship.
Insured's father was hospitalised for Progressive Cerebellar Ataxia and the claim was rejected as pre-existing due to underlying diabetes and blood pressure.
Overseas mediclaim policyholder claimed for delayed baggage clothing expenses after arrival. Although technically correct on timing, an ex-gratia payment was admitted.

Overseas policyholder had multiple hospitalisations involving diabetes, hypertension, and GI bleeding. Initial claims were rejected for non-disclosure of past cardiac and diabetic history, while a third claim for GI bleeding was ordered to be paid.
Claim for cancer metastasis and other conditions was ignored by the TPA despite reminders. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to settle the claim with interest due to TPA negligence.
Health check-up claim was rejected because a break in policy renewal meant the insured had not completed four continuous claim-free years.
Claims for knee replacements due to osteoarthritis were repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusions since medical history confirmed the condition existed for three years.
Insured fell in the bathroom and was hospitalised, but regular cardiac medicines were disallowed from the claim as they formed part of pre-existing treatment unrelated to the accident.
Claim for fibroid uterus treatment was rejected because investigation revealed the condition existed for several years prior to policy inception.
Insured underwent treatment for vomiting, hemorrhoids, and reflux during the first year of a fresh policy. The insurer correctly applied first-year disease exclusions.

Claim for diabetic foot ulcer treatment was repudiated based on a subsequent doctor's certificate stating 10 years of diabetes. The initial treatment certificate held primacy, so the claim was allowed.
Glaucoma treatment claim remained unanswered by the TPA until a hearing was fixed, prompting the insurer to agree to settle.
Chemotherapy hospitalization bills faced inordinate delay from the TPA, but the matter was settled between parties prior to the hearing.
Surgery bills faced delayed settlement until the insurer issued an assurance to pay just before the hearing.
Hospitalisation bills faced inordinate delay, leading to a complaint before the Ombudsman and a subsequent undertaking by the insurer to settle.

Cashless treatment and reimbursement for rheumatic complaints were denied on grounds of a 5-year pre-existing condition. Doctor certificates showed the condition was only 2.5 years old, leading the Ombudsman to allow the claim.
Motor bike accident claim under a group personal accident policy was rejected because hospital records and the insured's own admission confirmed he was under the influence of alcohol.

A 10-year-old child was hospitalized for severe headaches initially suspected to be internal disorders, but finally diagnosed as caused by dental caries. The insurer rejected the claim stating treatment was for dental issues and diagnostics. The Ombudsman held that tests were incidental to severe symptoms and allowed the claim.

The insured was hospitalized for diagnostic tests regarding Menorrhagia without additional medication or rest advised. The policy excluded investigative tests when hospitalization was not for treatment of disease. The insurer's repudiation was upheld.

The beneficiary under a family scheme suffered a myocardial infarction and underwent bypass surgery. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing coronary problems dating back to 1984, which were actually disclosed in the proposal form. The exclusion of pre-existing diseases applied, and the complaint was dismissed.

The insured underwent Ayurvedic treatment for vision correction. The insurer repudiated the claim based on a policy exclusion stamp regarding Ayurvedic treatments. Although a previous similar claim was mistakenly paid by the TPA, the clear policy exclusion stood. The complaint was dismissed.

The insured underwent gallbladder surgery shortly after taking a fresh policy without continuity. As she had gallbladder problems prior to commencement and failed to disclose them, the insurer rightly repudiated the claim under pre-existing disease exclusion.

The insured met with a road accident fracturing jawbones and losing teeth. The insurer paid inpatient bills but refused dental outpatient treatment. The Ombudsman noted that injuries arose directly from the accident and covered all consequential treatments, setting aside the partial repudiation.

The insured's wife underwent a hysterectomy within two months of policy inception. The insurer rejected the claim under the first-year exclusion clause for specific conditions including hysterectomy. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

insurer: Cholamandalam MS Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured's wife underwent a hysterectomy for fibroid uterus within the first year of policy. The insurer rejected the claim under first-year general exclusions and declined cashless due to incomplete information. The complaint was dismissed.

The insured was admitted for chest pain evaluation and coronary angiography, being discharged the same day. The insurer rejected the claim citing hospitalization was solely for diagnostic evaluation without 24-hour critical management. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claims for renal failure and encephalopathy were rejected due to non-disclosure of prior hypertension, with hospital records showing conflicting durations due to tampering. Noting the long policy history without claims, the Ombudsman granted 50 percent of the claim.

The insured challenged policy endorsements excluding diabetes, hypertension, and pacemaker ailments under a scheme policy. Given prior history and claims paid under earlier policies, the insurer's underwriting safeguard to exclude pre-existing conditions on a fresh scheme was upheld.

The insurer capped payouts for specific ailments like fistula and piles under a group mediclaim policy offered to credit card holders. The insured challenged the partial payment, but the Ombudsman upheld the insurer's right to limit liability per modified policy conditions.

A claim for angioplasty and bypass surgery was rejected on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension noted as 7 years old in hospital records. Granting benefit of doubt regarding exact duration and policy tenure approximating 6 years, the Ombudsman awarded 50 percent of the claim.

A claim for laparoscopic cholecystectomy was repudiated because historical jaundice and prior medical interventions were not disclosed, alongside evidence of document tampering in hospital records. The insurer's rejection for pre-existing illness was upheld.

The insured was hospitalized for migraine and neuralgia. The insurer repudiated the claim stating that investigations and oral medicines could be done as an outpatient without needing hospital confinement. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

A claim for thyroid cyst surgery was rejected for pre-existing disease based on a history of 7-8 years. Considering the patient remained asymptomatic and continuous coverage existed for four years, the Ombudsman awarded 50 percent of admissible expenses.

A claim for ischemic heart disease and PTCA was rejected due to a 12-day technical break in policy renewal caused by a bounced cheque. The Ombudsman held that treating the policy as a first-year policy was unjustified given 13 years of continuous prior coverage and prior settled claims.

A claim for tongue cancer surgery was rejected on the grounds of non-disclosure of a 10-year tobacco chewing habit. The Ombudsman noted lack of conclusive proof of prior treatment and awarded 50 percent of admissible expenses for the Bombay Hospital treatment.

Hospitalization for 30 days for degenerative cervical spine using low-level therapy was rejected because it lacked criticality and could be managed as outpatient treatment. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection but awarded 50 percent of specific laser therapy and medicine costs as a lenient measure.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims for Guillian Barrie Syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis were repudiated due to non-disclosure of childhood rheumatoid arthritis and joint deformities. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision that material misrepresentation rendered the contract void ab initio.

Insured hospitalized for Coronary Artery Disease and angiography. Claim repudiated under exclusion clause citing past history of hypertension. Ombudsman noted borderline hypertension and continuous policy coverage since 1990-91 without claims, ruling that the claim should be paid.

Insured hospitalized for total left knee replacement. Claim repudiated due to a policy break of 26 days during renewal caused by administrative/cheque-tagging error. Ombudsman directed insurer to pay 80 percent of the admissible amount with a penalty.

Claim for minor soft tissue knee injury treated with a plaster cast and requiring no hospitalization or fracture management. Insurer repudiated the claim as hospitalization was not warranted. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for coronary and renal angiography. Claim rejected on pre-existing disease grounds (hypertension and diabetes detected in 1994). Ombudsman found the policy was continuous from 1993, which the insurer failed to disprove, and directed settlement for angiography expenses.

Insured sought settlement for cataract surgery and extension of domestic mediclaim policy during overseas travel. Insurer settled cataract claim but rejected policy renewal request due to revised administrative guidelines issued after expiry. Ombudsman noted technical delay by insured and advised re-examination.

Insured hospitalized for internal piles surgery and offered partial settlement. Insurer deducted amounts for higher surgeon fees, missing receipt tallies, and nursing charges related to excluded polio condition. Ombudsman awarded additional amount towards surgery, medicines, and nursing charges.

Insured underwent CABG for severe triple vessel disease under a critical illness policy. Insurer repudiated the claim for non-disclosure of pre-existing coronary artery disease based on hospital records showing past history, while the insured alleged hospital record tampering. Ombudsman found claims non-entertainable due to disputed/inconclusive documents.

Claim for laparoscopic hysterectomy repudiated due to non-disclosure of past surgeries in 1991 (ovarian cystectomy) and 1995 (laparoscopy for infertility). Ombudsman confirmed non-disclosure of pre-existing conditions and upheld the rejection.

Claim for liposuction of bilateral gynaecomastia repudiated under cosmetic surgery exclusion clause. Insured contended it was a painful medical condition. Ombudsman held it was largely cosmetic but ordered 50 percent payment of hospitalization expenses.

Insured claimed reimbursement for cataract surgery, partially settled after deductions for pre-hospitalization expenses and excessive surgeon fees. Ombudsman allowed an additional amount towards the cost of surgery.
Claims for eye bleb repair and skin gangrene repudiated for pre-existing conditions and non-disclosure of prior trabeculectomy surgery. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Claim for vaginal hysterectomy with AP repair repudiated due to non-disclosure of pre-existing symptoms of uterine prolapse, depression, and other past treatments in the proposal form. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for COPD treatment rejected because the insured submitted duplicate bills instead of mandatory original hospital bills and cash memos. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation for violation of contract terms.

Claim for gastric ulcer and perforation surgery in the second policy year repudiated under exclusion clause C2 barring specific conditions during the first two to four years. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for bypass surgery initially withheld and later rejected for non-submission of initial consultation and diagnostic documents. Ombudsman directed settlement of admissible expenses for surgery at Breach Candy hospital subject to a 15 percent penalty for non-submission of initial records.

Claim for cataract extraction repudiated under first-year waiting period clause due to an 18-day gap in renewal. Ombudsman noted the policy had run for 14 years with maximum cumulative bonus, ruling the first-year rejection unethical.

Claim for inguinal hernia surgery rejected under pre-existing disease clause as hospital records indicated the swelling existed for 30 years despite insured's claims of recent onset. Ombudsman sustained the repudiation.

Claim for hospitalization due to Hepatitis C and skin rashes rejected under general exclusions and pre-existing disease evaluation following past tuberculosis treatment. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Claim for angiography following hospitalisation for chest pain and gastric evaluation rejected because hospitalization was solely for evaluation and due to pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim for total knee replacement under a group good health policy partially paid, with the balance cut due to policy sub-limits/caps on specific surgeries. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's settlement as per policy terms.

Insured hospitalized for paralytic stroke. Insurer repudiated claim invoking policy exclusion for heart ailments and circulatory disorders. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision as brain stroke is a circulatory problem.

Insured's wife hospitalized for vertigo and fever. TPA and insurer repudiated claim stating hospitalization was primarily for investigation and evaluation without need for confinement. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for child's hernia and hydrocele surgery was rejected as a congenital external disease exclusion. Ombudsman noted it was likely congenital but recommended a 50 percent ex-gratia settlement.

Insured hospitalized for unstable angina and underwent CABG. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing breathlessness for 15 years. Ombudsman set aside the repudiation due to lack of clinching medical evidence of past cardiac disease.

Claim for haematemesis hospitalization was rejected because confinement was under 24 hours and primarily for an endoscopy investigation that could be done on an OPD basis. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim for liver cirrhosis and bleeding complications was rejected for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of past kidney stone surgery and medical history. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for kidney transplantation due to end stage renal disease was rejected as pre-existing since the patient was on maintenance hemodialysis prior to policy inception. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for coronary artery bypass graft was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing diabetes and hypertension linked to coronary artery disease. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for lumbar laminectomy was rejected on grounds of pre-existing chronic back pain and non-disclosure when the husband was selectively added at renewal. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for grade I hypertension hospitalization was repudiated due to pre-existing hypertension and related thyroid history of several years. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for cerebrovascular stroke resulting in death was rejected because of a policy exclusion for heart ailments following prior CABG. Ombudsman allowed 50 percent of admissible expenses on an ex-gratia basis.
First-year policy claim for ischaemic heart disease and myocardial infarction was rejected by the insurer on grounds of pre-existing illness based on medical findings. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim for bilateral cataract surgery in the second policy year was rejected under first-year specific disease exclusion. Ombudsman ordered a 50 percent ex-gratia settlement due to doubts over deliberate delay.
Claim for acute coronary syndrome and spondylolysis was rejected for pre-existing hypertension and non-disclosure of medical history. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for coronary angioplasty in the second year of the policy was rejected due to pre-existing hypertension evidenced by concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Claim for emergency laparotomy due to intestinal obstruction by band adhesion was rejected based on inferred old pelvic colon infection. Ombudsman ruled the condition was an independent occurrence and ordered full settlement.
Claim for total hip replacement due to advanced avascular necrosis was rejected as pre-existing since the deformity took years to develop. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for CABG surgery was rejected solely due to delayed submission of claim papers beyond the stipulated policy timeline. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's strict application of the condition.
Claim for hospitalization to evaluate left facial nerve twitching was rejected under exclusion for non-necessary hospitalization without emergency or risk. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for coronary artery bypass graft was rejected due to delayed submission of documents past the policy deadline. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's reliance on the policy condition.

Insured was hospitalised for CAD, Aneurysmal aorta, and Bilateral Renal artery stenosis. Insurer repudiated claim under exclusion clause 4.1 citing pre-existing hypertension since 1982. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as longstanding hypertension has adverse renal impacts.

Insured was hospitalised for Acute Coronary Syndrome, Diabetes Mellitus, and Hypertension. Insurer repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1 due to pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman upheld the decision, noting nexus between hypertension, diabetes, and heart ailments.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was admitted for hypertension with giddiness for investigation. Insurer rejected the claim stating hospitalisation was unnecessary. Ombudsman upheld the rejection, noting admission lacked emergency and was solely for investigative evaluation.

Insured's wife was hospitalised for chronic abdominal pain and investigations. The TPA rejected the claim under clause 4.10 for lack of necessary hospitalisation and seriousness. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as treatment status did not justify inpatient admission.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim lodged for myomectomy and hysterectomy. Insurer rejected on grounds of non-disclosure of past surgery in 1994 and pre-existing illness including primary infertility treatment. Ombudsman upheld the decision due to non-disclosure affecting risk assessment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for viral hepatitis treatment for a child was rejected due to unsigned chemist bills and date discrepancies. Ombudsman noted medicines were supplied as prescribed and granted 50 percent of admissible expenses while levying 50 percent penalty for discrepancies.

Claim for massive jejunal bleeding was repudiated solely due to delay in submitting claim papers beyond policy timeline. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's strict enforcement of submission deadlines without evaluating merits.
Claim for acute LVF with infarction was rejected due to delayed submission of claim papers to the insurer. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision not to waive the time limit clause.

Claim for myocardial infarction and stenting was rejected as insurer claimed suppression of eight-year history of hypertension. Ombudsman observed attempted tampering of hospital records regarding disease duration and upheld repudiation for non-disclosure and pre-existence.

Claim for acute PID and radiculopathy involving 12 days of confinement was repudiated after investigation. Ombudsman upheld the rejection, noting 12 days hospitalisation for back pain and excessive treatment visits were unjustified.

Claim for hospitalisation due to obsessive compulsive disorder and extra pyramidal syndrome was rejected on grounds that hospitalisation was unnecessary and only investigations were done. Ombudsman allowed 50 percent of admissible expenses considering psycho-somatic complexities.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for ischaemic heart disease and angiography was repudiated due to pre-existing symptoms of chest discomfort before policy inception. Ombudsman allowed 50 percent of the claim, giving benefit of doubt as pre-existence was not conclusively proved.

Claim for hospitalisation covering diabetes, cardiomyopathy, osteoarthritis, and obesity was rejected for lack of necessity. Ombudsman allowed a maximum of 30 percent of total admissible expenses for emergency heart-related treatment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for angioplasty was rejected due to alleged concealment of diabetes duration. Ombudsman noted inability to prove pre-policy treatment and awarded 50 percent of the claim while setting aside total rejection.

Claim for dental treatment following a fall from bed and loss of dentures was rejected under clause 4.7. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as hospitalisation necessity was unproven and dentures are excluded.

Claim for surgery of left irreducible inguinal hernia was repudiated under clause 4.1 based on hospital records showing swelling existed for 3 to 4 years prior to the policy. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Claim for coronary angiography and bypass surgery was rejected on the assumption that triple vessel disease could not develop in a year and a half. Ombudsman set aside total rejection and allowed 50 percent of the claim due to lack of strong evidence of pre-existence.

Claim for diabetic foot with toxic hepatitis and septicemia was repudiated as pre-existing diabetes existed for over two decades. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation based on hospital case papers and treating doctor's records.

Claim for accelerated hypertension and dyslipidemia hospitalisation was rejected under clause 4.10. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as blood pressure management could have been handled at home through therapy.

Claim for pericolic retroperitoneal abscess was repudiated based on pre-existing diabetes mentioned in hospital notes. Considering continuous policy coverage since 1991, the Ombudsman ordered 70 percent settlement, deducting 30 percent for diabetes-related expenses.

Insured claimed reimbursement for replacement of a worn-out CPAP machine for sleep disorder without any new hospitalization or treatment. The insurer rejected the claim under policy conditions stating apparatus replacement without hospitalization is not covered. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured underwent coronary bypass surgery for triple vessel disease linked to diabetes. The insurer repudiated the claim as diabetes and related ailments were excluded due to pre-existence. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured's daughter was hospitalized for renal stones with UTI. The claim was rejected as hospital records and past history indicated pre-existing abdominal and renal issues. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for acute renal colic with UTI. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing renal calculus disease based on past medical records. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured's son underwent surgery for a sebaceous cyst on the lip with hospital stay under 24 hours. The insurer rejected the claim citing lack of necessity and short stay. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation, ordering full payment minus a 10 percent deduction for room charges.

Insured claimed for slip disc treatment following a reported bathroom fall. The insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing based on discrepancies in hospital records and lack of fresh injury signs. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for less than 24 hours to receive an epidural injection for back pain. The insurer rejected the claim due to stay under 24 hours and lack of hospitalization necessity. The Ombudsman upheld the decision.

Insured underwent brain surgery for a blocked shunt related to a colloid cyst surgery performed in 1985. The insurer rejected the claim as a pre-existing condition. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for D&C and laparoscopic tubal ligation due to irregular bleeding. The insurer offered partial settlement of Rs. 4000. The Ombudsman set aside the partial payment and directed full settlement of admissible expenses.

Insured underwent coronary artery bypass graft surgery. The insurer repudiated the claim due to non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension, diabetes, and asthma. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for chronic conditions including diabetes, hypertension, and osteoarthritis for conservative management and investigations. The insurer rejected the claim citing lack of necessity. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured's wife underwent exploratory laparotomy and appendicectomy along with adhesiolysis. The TPA paid 70 percent of the claim, deducting 30 percent attributed to prior tubectomy adhesions. The Ombudsman found the partial deduction reasonable and dismissed the complaint.

Insured underwent kidney removal surgery due to renal abscess and chronic pyelonephritis. The insurer rejected the claim for non-disclosure of pre-existing abdominal and health complications. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured underwent dental surgery for total tooth extraction and alveolectomy. The insurer rejected the claim on the grounds of pre-existing advanced dental decay. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured doctor claimed for cataract surgery, but the insurer rejected it due to lack of substantiating indoor case papers and inconclusive investigation. The Ombudsman noted lack of power to investigate and closed the matter without ruling.

Insured's wife underwent coronary angiography and PTCA stent. The insurer rejected the claim citing a 15-day break in policy renewal and pre-existing sinus bradycardia. The Ombudsman held the rejection unsustainable as bradycardia was unrelated to heart disease.

Insured's son was hospitalized for head injury after being hit by a cricket ball. The insurer rejected the claim alleging hospitalization was only for investigations and unnecessary. The Ombudsman granted 50 percent of the claim amount.

Insured was hospitalized for septicaemia, pneumonia, and perianal abscess, and died. The insurer rejected the claim citing long-standing pre-existing diabetes, hypertension, and heart disease. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured was hospitalized for low blood pressure and drowsiness caused by alcohol abuse. The insurer rejected the claim under policy exclusion for alcohol consumption. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured received outpatient treatment for frozen shoulder over several weeks. The insurer rejected the claim as there was no hospitalization for a minimum of 24 hours. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured was hospitalized for loss of encephalopathy, chronic constipation, and Hirschsprung's disease. Insurer repudiated claim under clauses 4.1 and 4.8 due to pre-existing congenital conditions and alcohol abuse. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Insured claimed for fibroids after hospitalisation. Claim was repudiated due to policy lapse/breaks during renewals and loss of cumulative bonus benefits. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant alleged delay in settlement of mother's hospitalization claim. Insurer fully settled the claim up to maximum sum insured plus cumulative bonus during the process, but faced procedural delays due to TPA implementation. No monetary award for harassment was given.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for coronary angiography after being advised by another hospital. Insurer rejected the claim stating CAG is a diagnostic test performable at OPD. Ombudsman noted the test followed formal medical advice and was validly part of treatment/post-hospitalization.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured claimed reimbursement for a CPAP machine for obstructive sleep apnea without being hospitalized. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 2.3. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as external apparatus without hospitalization is not covered.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for iron deficiency anemia and cervical spondylosis. Insurer rejected the claim arguing menorrhagia was pre-existing for 4 years causing the anemia. Ombudsman allowed 50% of expenses considering contributory factors.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's son underwent septoplasty for Deviated Nasal Septum and chronic rhinitis within 7 months of policy inception. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion 4.3 for sinusitis and related disorders during the first year. Ombudsman upheld the decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured claimed for hospitalization for acute bronchitis and sleep apnea, including a CPAP machine. TPA settled hospital expenses but excluded the CPAP machine cost. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial disallowance for external equipment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for upper GI bleed, drug-induced gastritis, and alcoholic liver cirrhosis. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.8. Ombudsman upheld the decision as complications arose from alcohol abuse.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for chest pain, and investigations showed no major abnormality. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.10 stating hospitalization was unnecessary and only for investigations. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for coronary artery disease and underwent PTCA. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.1 due to a 20-year history of diabetes. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured underwent right eye cataract surgery under a group mediclaim policy. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.1 because cataract surgery was explicitly excluded during policy shifts. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's underwriting terms.

Insured's father was hospitalized for acute exacerbation of COPD. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing illness and non-disclosure of bronchial asthma. Ombudsman held that the insurer took a narrow view and directed full settlement.

Insured preferred claims for unstable angina and coronary artery disease. Insurer rejected the claims under exclusion clause 4.1 due to non-disclosure of prior angina history. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured and wife took naturopathy treatment for arthritis and obesity at a trust. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.13. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as naturopathy and stays at such trusts are outside policy scope.

Insured claimed for cerebrovascular accident after a brief policy lapse due to a dishonored cheque. Insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.1. Ombudsman took a lenient view and ordered 75% payment of admissible expenses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for evaluation of apraxia of speech and cortico basal ganglionic degeneration. Insurer rejected the claim stating it was for investigation and evaluation without necessity of hospitalization. Ombudsman directed settlement of 50% of admissible expenses.

Insured claimed for back pain diagnosed as disc bulge after a brief renewal gap. Insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.1 for pre-existing illness. Ombudsman allowed the claim with a 25% deduction due to the policy break.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for strangulated ventral hernia. Insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.1 due to pre-existing history of past caesarean surgeries and obesity. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured claimed hospitalisation expenses including private nursing charges for mother-in-law treated for fracture neck femur. TPA disallowed private nursing charges. Ombudsman upheld the disallowance as the hospital was fully equipped.

Claim for hernia surgery was rejected on the ground that it was an incisional hernia linked to a caesarian section from 1973. The Ombudsman noted multiple independent causes for hernia and set aside the insurer's rejection, ordering full payment.

Claim for appendicitis and endometriosis treatment was repudiated under pre-existing disease and infertility exclusion clauses. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection for infertility/endometriosis treatment but allowed expenses for appendicectomy on a 50 percent basis.

Claim for tympanoplasty due to chronic bilateral otitis media was rejected on the grounds of a pre-existing long-standing disease and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's repudiation as sustainable.

Claim for revision of pilonidal sinus scar was repudiated under the plastic surgery exclusion clause. The Ombudsman held that the surgery was not cosmetic and allowed the claim with a 30 percent deduction for excess expenses.
Claim for incisional hernia surgery was rejected due to pre-existing condition and non-disclosure of past caesarian surgery. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Claim for transient ischaemic attack was rejected on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman ordered 50 percent of admissible expenses to be paid on an ex-gratia basis.
Claim for Hashimoto's thyroiditis with goitre was rejected due to pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of 1983 treatment history. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for retinal detachment and scleral buckling was repudiated under pre-existing disease clauses following a policy renewal gap. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.
Claim for correction of nasal deformity was rejected under plastic surgery exclusions. The insured failed to produce contemporaneous evidence of an accident. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.
Mediclaim for cataract surgery was repudiated because the hospital registration was allegedly for a commercial establishment. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and ordered full payment.
Claims for hospitalisation were repudiated under pre-existing disease clauses as hospital records showed a history of hypertension and old myocardial infarction. Repudiation was upheld.
Claim settlement was severely delayed because the insurer misplaced original documents. The Ombudsman allowed the full claim amount with 8 percent simple interest for deficiency in service.
Mediclaim for hospital treatment was repudiated because admission was solely for diagnostic workup and investigation. Repudiation was upheld.
Mediclaim for CRF and hypertension was repudiated on the grounds of a pre-existing condition dating back 10 years. Repudiation was upheld.
Mediclaim for fibroids uterus was rejected under first-year exclusions because the policy had a renewal gap of 35 days. Repudiation was upheld.
Claim was partially repudiated for physiotherapy expenses that lacked date, name, and medical prescription following screw removal. Repudiation was upheld.

Mediclaim for discogenic lower lumbar pain was rejected on the grounds that hospitalisation was unjustified. The Ombudsman held that hospitalisation advised by a qualified surgeon justifies the claim and set aside the repudiation.
Mediclaim for intra-hepatic cholestasis was repudiated under pre-existing disease and pregnancy-related exclusion clauses following a policy break. Repudiation was upheld.
Mediclaim for L5-S1 disc prolapse was rejected due to pre-existing disease dating back to 1995. Repudiation was upheld.
Mediclaim for aorta bifemoral bypass surgery was rejected because the initial bypass surgery occurred prior to the claim. Repudiation was upheld.

Claim for angiography and angioplasty was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing Myocardial Infarction. The policy was switched to Mediguard after continuous coverage from 1999 without break. Under relaxations, pre-existing exclusions do not apply after three consecutive claim-free years from initial inception. Repudiation was set aside and full amount ordered.
Mediclaim repudiated as disease was an excluded condition added at renewal. The Ombudsman found the matter outside its powers, advising the complainant to approach another appropriate forum.
Insured had continuous coverage for 4 years but failed to disclose chronic inguinal hernia and testicular swelling, and past surgery 20 years prior. Repudiation by the insurer was upheld.
Repudiation on grounds that bronchial asthma was excluded and hospitalization was for acute bronchitis. Medical opinion confirmed the conditions were related, so repudiation was upheld.

Daughter was hospitalized for vehicle accident head injury with unconsciousness and eye injury. Insurer claimed hospitalization was unwarranted, but treatment papers and good claim history supported the claim. Repudiation set aside.
Complainant signed a discharge voucher accepting claim as full and final settlement, and was estopped from reopening the claim. Repudiation was upheld.

Insurer deducted Rs. 69,110 for knee replacement surgery, including Rs. 50,000 paid to an incorrect surgeon. Operation was performed by another qualified surgeon whose bill was allowed after discount. Insurer directed to pay Rs. 15,640.

Repudiated for acute intestinal obstruction related to prior appendicitis. The proposal form disclosed the operation, but no exclusion was added to the policy schedule. Ombudsman ruled insurer cannot repudiate when omission was on their part, directing full payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for balloon mitral valvuplasty done in 2004 repudiated because the policy commenced July 1996 and surgery was done 17 days later, indicating the ailment existed prior to inception. Repudiation upheld.
Repudiation for diabetes mellitus history not disclosed in proposal form and questionnaire. Repudiation upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Policy had two renewal breaks, making inception the current commencement date. Treating doctor notes showed back pain history started before commencement, so repudiation was upheld.
Hospitalization was for observation of side effects from oral chemotherapy for breast cancer. Given the gravity of cancer and serious treatment, insurer ordered to pay full settlement.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalized for triple vessel disease and CABG six months after policy inception. Insurer relied on presumptive medical opinions without specific documentary proof of pre-existence. Repudiation set aside and full claim ordered.
Hospitalized for osteoarthritis hip requiring replacement, claimed as accidental injury. Case papers showed no trauma, and a late certificate was obtained from the surgeon. Repudiation upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization lasted less than 24 hours, failing minimum period stipulation. Repudiation upheld.
A 12-year-old girl fell and suffered severe back pain, hospitalized on specialist advice after failed OPD treatment. Respondent directed to pay full claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Consultant surgeon and hospital records consistently noted clinical history of high blood pressure for 10 years. Repudiation upheld.
Hospitalized for acid peptic disorder and gastroparesis, connected to pre-existing diabetes mellitus of 10 years and policy exclusion. Repudiation upheld.

Repudiated for hospitalization under 24 hours and congenital external condition. Documents showed admission for 26 hours for a 2-year-old child's hernia operation. Surgeon stated swelling appeared 15 days prior. Repudiation set aside.
Oral chemotherapy treatment taken at home beyond 60 days of hospital discharge. Policy allows post-hospitalization up to 60 days. Repudiation upheld.

Mediclaim claim was repudiated for non-submission of required letters. Since the insurer exhibited valid proof of payment and the complainant was absent from the hearing, the complaint was taken as resolved.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized following a fall and diagnosed with vertigo and a small brain tumor. The insurer repudiated the claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary as only oral medicines and diagnostic tests were performed. The ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for neurological complaints and underwent an MRI and routine blood tests. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds that admission was unnecessary and tests could be done on an outpatient basis. The ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Insured was hospitalized for back and leg pain and underwent an MRI and CT scan, receiving only oral medications. The insurer rejected the claim under the exclusion for hospitalization primarily for diagnostic purposes. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured's wife was operated for hernia. The insurer closed the file because required documents were not submitted in time and the matter became time-barred. The complainant was absent from the hearing, and the case was closed.

Insured's mother was hospitalized for asthma and pulmonary koch's during the first year of the policy. Medical records showed she had suffered from these conditions for years prior to inception. The insurer repudiated the claim, and the complaint was dismissed.

Complainant was hospitalized following a fall and diagnosed with an old compression fracture and spinal stenosis. The insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing since the policy was taken only 48 days prior and medical opinion confirmed an old injury. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured was hospitalized for headache and chest pain where tests were conducted. The insurer repudiated the claim because attending doctors noted no abnormalities in the reports, rendering hospitalization primarily for diagnostic tests. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured's mother was hospitalized for vomiting and a paralytic attack. The insurer rejected the claim stating the conditions were directly related to long-standing hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease declared as pre-existing at policy inception. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's son was hospitalized for neck bone dislocation and underwent an MRI. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds that admission was for diagnostic tests only. The complainant was absent from the hearing, and the case was closed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife was operated for hernia during the second year of the policy. The complainant stated the hernia developed two to three months before surgery, which fell within the first year exclusion period for hernia. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's son was hospitalized in a nursing home that lacked the minimum required inpatient beds, qualified round-the-clock nursing staff, and registration. The insurer repudiated the claim based on the policy's hospital definition clause. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured's pregnant wife was hospitalized and treated for malaria and jaundice. The TPA rejected the claim under pregnancy exclusions, but during the hearing, the insurer approved the full claim and issued a discharge voucher. The complaint was resolved.

Complainant was hospitalized for throat swelling and operated on, but the claim was rejected under general debility and intoxicating drug exclusions due to a mention of beedi use. The TPA acknowledged the mistake during the hearing, and the insurer was directed to decide the claim on merit.

Insured was hospitalized and diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. The insurer rejected the claim because admission was solely for diagnostic tests and oral medication, violating exclusion clause 4.10. The complaint was dismissed.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for acute stomach pain in a hospital that did not meet the 15-bed requirement. The complainant, an insurance agent, failed to justify why he bypassed several nearby compliant hospitals. The complaint was dismissed.

Complainant was hospitalized for investigations regarding hepatitis B. The insurer treated the claim as no-claim on the grounds that no active treatment was given and tests could be done on an OPD basis. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was operated on for a slip disc. The insurer repudiated the claim citing a pre-existing history of backache based on a cut prescription. The ombudsman found hospital records proved the illness started only 20 days prior and ordered the insurer to pay the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for cervical spondylosis, vertigo, and diabetes to undergo an MRI and other tests. The insurer repudiated the claim because admission was unnecessary and for diagnostic purposes only. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured died of pneumonia and ARDS associated with HIV. The insurer rejected the claim under the AIDS exclusion clause. Considering the complainant's severe financial distress, the ombudsman directed the insurer to pay an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 50,000.

Insured son was hospitalized for hypertension and blood pressure. Insured had history of marked obesity for 8 years and admission was for investigation only. Claim was rejected as pre-existing disease and admission for investigation only. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Policy renewal was delayed due to administrative delay in processing advance premium, causing a break in continuity across multiple years. Ombudsman ordered correction of dates in subsequent policies to maintain continuity.

Complainant took overseas mediclaim policy. Due to a clerical data entry error, illness cover was restricted to USD 10,000 instead of standard USD 500,000 despite paying full premium. Insurer admitted mistake. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 3,000 as ex-gratia.

Insured was hospitalized during previous policy period and died after renewal. Insurer rejected claim stating sum insured was exhausted in previous period and hospitalization started before renewal. Ombudsman held treatment post-renewal is payable and ordered payment.

Insured renewed policy for years, but insurer added exclusion endorsements for prostate and heart diseases. District Consumer Forum had already ruled heart disease was not pre-existing. Ombudsman ordered expunging heart disease exclusion while noting prostate stands excluded under general rules.

Insured was hospitalized for acute pancreatitis, incurring Rs. 4.75 lakh. Claim was rejected because pancreatitis was caused by chronic alcoholism, falling under policy exclusion 4.8. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint based on medical records.

Insured was hospitalized for diabetic foot. Insurer rejected claim under pre-existing disease clause as policy was converted from mediclaim to mediguard a year prior and diabetes was old. Ombudsman granted 50 percent of claim as terms were not made known.

Insured underwent spinal disc surgery after backache and claim was rejected as pre-existing based on MRI degenerative changes. Ombudsman held that degenerative changes and lack of prior treatment do not prove pre-existing disease without knowledge, and directed settlement.

Complainant's mother was hospitalized and cashless facility was denied by TPA due to recently diagnosed diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman held that insurer has discretion to evaluate cashless requests and declined to interfere.

Insured was hospitalized for sudden back pain and MRI showed a condition. Claim was rejected as pre-existing on fresh policy. Ombudsman noted medical team did not establish insured's prior knowledge, and gave benefit of doubt, directing claim admission.
