Insured was hospitalized for recurrent incisional hernia. Insurer rejected claim as pre-existing due to prior hernia surgery in 2001. Specialist opined 2004 repair was a fresh episode. Ombudsman allowed 75 percent of claim.

Insured underwent CABG for Coronary Artery Disease. Insurer repudiated claim for non-disclosure of past myocardial infarction and hypertension. Ombudsman noted old cardiac event had no manifestation for 20 years and allowed 50 percent ex-gratia.

Insured underwent CABG surgery. Claim was rejected because of a single-day break in policy renewal years ago following a 1997 CAD treatment. Ombudsman directed insurer to condone the single day delay and settle the claim.

Insured underwent laser correction surgery for severe hypermetropia. TPA rejected claim as cosmetic surgery under exclusion 4.5. Attending doctor certified severe visual disability equivalent to eligible myopia. Ombudsman directed insurer to settle.

Insured underwent angioplasty and claimed package expenses. Insurer paid restricted amount based on package limits and policy clauses. Ombudsman verified calculations and found insured received full eligible amount including post-hospitalization limits.

Insured underwent cholecystectomy for gall bladder stones. Insurer rejected claim as pre-existing due to stone size, non-disclosure of 1981 surgery, and high LFT indicating alcoholism. Ombudsman granted 50 percent ex-gratia award.

Insured was hospitalized for borderline CAD and other conditions. Claim was repudiated citing pre-existing diabetes and hypothyroidism as predisposing factors and evaluation nature. Ombudsman held proximate cause was not established and directed claim payment excluding pre-existing ailments.

Claim was repudiated on grounds that hospitalization was for investigation only without active management. Ombudsman noted severe symptoms including significant weight loss warranted admission, and directed payment of 75 percent of admissible expenses.

Insured was hospitalized for intestinal obstruction and hernia. Insurer rejected claim as pre-existing, linking it to a caesarean section 11 years prior. Ombudsman held a scar tissue is not a disease and directed insurer to pay admissible expenses.

Insured underwent surgery for sleep apnoea. Claim was rejected as pre-existing based on childhood adenoid enlargement and non-disclosure of diabetes/hypertension. Ombudsman found pre-existence and nexus unproven, directing claim settlement.

Insured underwent bypass surgery in 1995 and was later hospitalized in 2004 for heart-related ailments. Insurer repudiated due to pre-existing disease, citing exclusion clause 4.1. The forum found that the insurer had misled the insured into believing the policy was a continuous renewal without exclusions, and allowed the claim on an ex-gratia basis for 60% of admissible expenses.

Insured hospitalized for severe back pain and underwent surgery. Claim was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing tuberculosis. The insurer failed to prove prior awareness or treatment. The ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Insured underwent total knee replacement in the third policy year after enhancing sum insured. Claim repudiated for non-disclosure of prior knee pain. Forum held that enhancing sum insured equates to a new policy for the increased amount, so the disease was pre-existing to the increased sum insured. Claim allowed only as per the original sum insured.

Insured incurred expenses for diagnostic tests for intermittent fever in the USA. Claim rejected due to past history of malaria and typhoid 14 years prior, treated as pre-existing non-disclosure. Forum held that past infections from 14 years ago do not constitute suppression of material facts and ordered full settlement.

Insured hospitalized for severe cluster headache after outpatient treatments failed. Insurer rejected claim arguing hospitalization was unnecessary and could be managed as outpatient. Forum noted attending doctor's advice warranted emergency admission and ordered claim settlement.

Insurer partially settled hospitalization expenses, disallowing post-operative expenses like physiotherapy and nursing because the discharge summary lacked explicit advice for further treatment. Forum observed that stroke recovery warrants physiotherapy and directed the insurer to pay the remaining claimed amount.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured under a Hospital Cash Plan was hospitalized for acute brain infarct and claimed daily cash benefits. Insurer rejected the claim stating hypertension was pre-existing and caused the stroke. Forum found no medical record of prior hypertension and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent CABG surgery and claim was rejected on grounds of circulatory disease exclusion introduced in the second year and non-disclosed mitral valve prolapse. Forum noted the exclusion was sweeping and unjustified, directing the insurer to settle the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for cataract surgery was rejected because policy modifications increased the waiting period for cataract from 1 year to 3 years. Insured had completed 2 years and 9 months. Forum ordered a 50% ex-gratia settlement due to frequent uncommunicated policy changes.

Claim for sudden chest pain and angiogram was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. While no records disproved diabetes and hypertension, panel doctors opined heart disease was not necessarily pre-existing. Forum ordered 50% ex-gratia settlement.

Cashless facility and claim for incisional hernia surgery were denied because the insured had a previous Caesarean section 5 years prior to policy inception. Forum held that only the scar tissue existed previously, not the hernia itself, and directed the insurer to settle.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for road accident injuries requiring wound suturing was rejected on grounds of insufficient hospitalization and lack of medical necessity based on panel doctor opinion. Forum held that attending doctors decide hospitalization necessity and ordered settlement.

Dental surgery claim was rejected under dental exclusions and because the hospital did not meet the minimum requirement of 15 beds. The complainant failed to produce evidence of bed capacity, so the dismissal was upheld.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Part of a claim for hysterectomy expenses was disallowed for hormone replacement therapy / Lupride Depot administration. Medical specialists confirmed the treatment was prophylactic and not for a diagnosed active condition. Insurer's partial rejection was upheld.
Mediclaim for a deceased policyholder was left unsettled for over a year because the insurer lost the documents and failed to respond. Ombudsman ordered full payment with 8% interest.

Claim for hospitalization due to vertigo and related tests was rejected on the grounds that tests could be done on an OPD basis. Ombudsman held that hospitalization was justified to determine gravity of illness and awarded the claim amount with interest.

Claim for hip surgery was repudiated because the insured failed to disclose a bone fracture from 8 years prior, which led to degenerative changes. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's repudiation for non-disclosure.

Claim for hospitalization due to severe bone and joint pains was classified as 'No Claim' on the basis that the patient was admitted only for investigations. Ombudsman observed that the 7-8 day hospital stay was necessary for a definite disease and awarded the claim.

Claim for hysterectomy due to fibromyoma was repudiated because the policy's first-year exclusion list explicitly excludes hysterectomy for fibromyoma during the initial policy year. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for calculus cholecystitis surgery was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease since hospital records indicated symptoms started before policy inception. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Insured underwent cataract surgery after a policy renewal gap of 114 days. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion for the first year of operation, treating it as a fresh policy.

Insured son was hospitalised for sub acute bowel obstruction. Insurer rejected claim citing a 1997 gastric pull surgery as pre-existing, but failed to prove medical nexus or post-operative complications during the intervening seven years.

Doctor insured under a medical policy was hospitalised for acute coronary heart disease. The insurer repudiated the claim based on pre-existing diabetes and hypertension, supported by a 1990 ECG showing signs of silent myocardial infarction.

Insured underwent CABG and the claim was rejected citing pre-existing hypertension. Hospital records only showed ailments for the previous two to three months, with no proof of prior awareness or diagnosis before the policy inception.

Insured was admitted for Coronary Angiogram and diagnosed with Double Vessel Disease. The insurer rejected the claim stating hospitalisation was purely for diagnostic investigation, but the ombudsman noted the procedure revealed positive existence of an ailment.
Insurer declined to renew a Universal Health Insurance policy because the insured failed to produce proof of being below the poverty line as mandated by the scheme guidelines.

Death claim was intimated after a 14-month delay. The insurer accepted the genuineness of the claim but initially resisted due to the delay. Separately, a delayed payment of a hip surgery claim led to an order for interest and compensation.

Insured was hospitalised for an eye problem and the claim was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing diabetes for 10 years. Treating doctor certified diabetes started later, and the insurer had previously settled two similar claims.

Insured mother was hospitalised for hypertension and IHD. Claim was rejected for pre-existing conditions and non-disclosure, but the insurer provided no expert opinion on the duration or asymptomatic nature of the illness.

Insured underwent PTCA and the claim was rejected under pre-existing disease exclusion. TPA panel doctor contradictory notes and lack of evidence supporting pre-existence led to the ombudsman setting aside the rejection.

Insured underwent Stereotactic Radio surgery. Claim was rejected due to a 35-day renewal break treating it as a fresh policy and citing pre-existing ear problems. Ombudsman awarded 75% on an ex-gratia basis.
Insured was hospitalised for piles and the claim was rejected because hospitalisation was for less than 24 hours, alongside renewal break issues. The 24-hour minimum condition was upheld.

Insured was treated for myocardial infarction and heart block. The TPA made a 10% deduction for pre-existing diabetes and hypertension without any policy condition to support it. Insurer ordered to pay the balance and bank charges.

Insured underwent knee surgery. Claim was settled partly because knee pain was consulted before an enhanced sum insured was taken. Ombudsman directed rectification of cumulative bonus and payment of interest for delayed settlement.
Health check-up claim was rejected because of a 15-day break in policy renewal during a prior year, breaking the required continuous four-year claim-free period. Insurer's decision was upheld.

Insured died of a cardiac arrest after being diagnosed with Single Vessel Disease. TPA rejected the claim alleging pre-existing hypertension, but the ombudsman noted continuous insurance for 10 years and no tangible evidence of prior hypertension.

Insured underwent bilateral knee replacement. Individual mediclaim insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing Grade III Osteoarthritis based on insidious onset and joint deformity, while a separate group policy had already paid out.

Total knee replacement claim was rejected under pre-existing disease clause. Medical records and dictionary extracts confirmed bilateral arthritis of the knees prior to the inception of the first-year policy.

Claims for multiple hospitalisations for diabetes, CAD, and peripheral nephropathy were rejected. A past renewal gap caused the policy to be treated as fresh with explicit exclusions matching the claimed ailments.
Claim for daughter's squint surgery was repudiated under exclusion of external congenital diseases. Photo identity card submitted by the insured clearly displayed the squint prior to policy issue.

Insured claimed reimbursement for coronary angioplasty and CABG. Insurer repudiated citing pre-existing AWMI treated in 1996, and records showed no valid Mediclaim cover prior to 1997. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant underwent stent placement and PTCA for coronary artery disease. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing IHD and hypertension. Hospital records showed recent onset of TVD, and hypertension was known and accepted at proposal stage. Insurer directed to honour claims with interest and damages.

Insured was hospitalized for two days for ankle pain and diagnosed with Seronegative Rheumatoid Arthritis, treated only with oral drugs. Claim was rejected as hospitalization was unnecessary. Lack of outpatient treatment papers led Ombudsman to uphold the insurer's decision.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for L4/L5 disc injury and lumbar spondylosis. TPA rejected the claim as a pre-existing disease and argued hospitalization was unnecessary. Insurer failed to produce evidence of pre-existing back pain, so Ombudsman found the repudiation unjustified.

Insured underwent CABG for Triple Vessel Disease shortly after taking a new policy. Insurer repudiated for non-disclosure of hypertension and prior myocardial infarction. Medical evidence and prior LIC proposal records confirmed suppression of material health facts. Complaint dismissed.

Insured's wife underwent stent placement for coronary artery disease while on an overseas trip. Claim was rejected because the policy excluded CAD treatment. An independent medical opinion confirmed the new lesion was attributable to prior heart condition. Insurer's decision upheld.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife sought treatment in the USA for persistent dry cough existing for over six weeks. Claim was denied under the pre-existing condition exclusion since symptoms clearly began in India prior to departure. Insurer's decision upheld.

Insured underwent laminectomy and discectomy for intervertebral disc prolapse shortly after policy inception. Investigation revealed he had received outpatient treatment for low back ache prior to purchasing the policy, which was not disclosed. Insurer's rejection justified.

Complainant's son underwent back surgery for disc prolapse. Claim was rejected for pre-existing ailment. Complainant's scooter fall theory was unsupported by hospital records stating no history of injury. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's repudiation.

Insured was hospitalized for shortness of breath and diagnosed with RHD, later passing away. Claim was repudiated on the ground of pre-existing RHD. Ombudsman noted treatment for other concurrent ailments was admissible and ordered settlement for those specific days.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for a breast lump and underwent surgery for fibrocystic disease. TPA rejected the claim as pre-existing. Outpatient and discharge records confirmed the lump was noticed only days before admission. Insurer directed to honor the claim.

Insured's mother underwent leg amputation due to septicemia. Claim was repudiated under pre-existing diabetes clause. Verification of past policies showed continuous coverage since 1999, with diabetes diagnosed years after inception. Insurers directed to honor the claim.

Mediclaim for a husband and wife was delayed significantly. The insurer settled the main claims during the Ombudsman proceedings after terminating the negligent TPA. Ombudsman ordered the insurer to pay Rs. 3,600 towards the complainant's miscellaneous expenses.

Under Universal Health Insurance Plan, claims for cerebral ischaemia and hemorrhoids were repudiated for alleged non-disclosure and first-year exclusion. Ombudsman found no proof of suppression and awarded the amount admissible for ischaemia treatment.

Insured underwent surgery for an atrial septal defect (congenital heart defect). Claim was repudiated because the policy explicitly excluded all congenital diseases. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured's son, a known case of meningitis with an exclusion for it, was hospitalized for constipation and urinary incontinence. TPA rejected the entire claim. Ombudsman directed partial allowance, excluding diagnostic MRI charges related to meningitis history.

Insured met with an accident and incurred hospital expenses across two centers. Insurer partially reimbursed the claim, cutting an amount deemed not reasonably and necessarily incurred. Ombudsman ordered additional payment of Rs. 7,785.

Claim for cataract surgery was rejected under pre-existing and 1st year exclusion clauses after the policy was renewed 12 days late with a fresh proposal form. Ombudsman ruled the policy was in continuity and set aside the repudiation, granting medical reimbursement.

Insured underwent angioplasty costing Rs. 2,10,000 and claimed the sum insured of Rs. 1,00,000. Settlement was delayed due to a misplaced file. Insurer admitted liability during proceedings and agreed to pay the full sum insured, satisfying the complainant.
Insured's wife underwent treatment at a Siddha clinic. Claim was rejected because the facility had only 8 beds and failed to meet the policy definition of a hospital. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Complainant claimed reimbursement for heart ailment treatment. Insurer repudiated based on a doctor's remark in a previous discharge summary mentioning hypertension for 20 years, without supporting evidence. Ombudsman noted lack of corroborative medical records and advised the insurer to honour the claim subject to bill verification.

Complainant's son was hospitalized for vascular headache evaluation and CT scan under the Jana Arogya Scheme. Insurer repudiated the entire claim arguing it was solely for evaluation. Ombudsman found admission was per medical advice and allowed boarding, nursing, and room rent expenses amounting to Rs. 490.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Group mediclaim policyholder underwent Lasik eye surgery. Insurer initially rejected the claim as cosmetic, then paid part of it. Ombudsman found hospitalization, scan, and appropriate surgeon charges totaling a balance of Rs. 125 were payable and allowed it.

Complainant alleged delay in issuing cashless ID card and failure to avail cashless facility for glaucoma surgery. Insurer stated cards were dispatched and received. Ombudsman noted cards issued lacked photographs, but hospital records showed the card was never produced, and dismissed the grievance regarding reimbursement.

Complainant challenged a 100% premium loading charged at age 77 upon renewing his mediclaim policy. Ombudsman noted the policy was accepted knowingly without coercion and insurers have the prerogative to load premiums based on risk perception, though suggested reviewing claims experience for future reduction.

Insurer rejected the third claim of the policy year on the ground that the sum insured and cumulative bonus were completely exhausted by earlier settlements. Complainant argued treatment extended into the renewed policy period. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision that claims must be settled against the sum insured of the specific policy period they occurred in.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for hernia surgery was repudiated by TPA on the ground that it was related to previous abdominal operations (cesarean and hysterectomy) done prior to policy inception. Ombudsman upheld the panel doctor's opinion linking the current condition to past surgeries in the absence of contrary medical evidence.

Complainant underwent prostate surgery within the first year of the policy. Insurer repudiated the claim under first-year exclusion clause 4.3. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation, stating that policy terms agreed upon via the proposal form are binding and specific exclusions apply during the first year.

Claim for treatment of osteolytic lesion of the femur was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease and delayed intimation. Clinical history indicated a history of hip and knee pain since childhood. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation based on pre-existing condition under clause 4.1.

Claim for cholecystectomy was repudiated by TPA as a pre-existing disease. Family physician certified the condition was not known before routine investigation. Ombudsman found no conclusive medical evidence proving pre-existing manifestation at policy inception and reversed the insurer's decision.

Claim for treatment of Syndrome X with GERD and cerebral infarction was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension and diabetes mellitus. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on medical panel opinions linking the acute condition to long-standing pre-existing metabolic disorders.

Claim for knee surgery was rejected because historical policy breaks broke continuity and medical records showed treatment for knee deformity prior to the current policy inception date. Ombudsman upheld the closure of the claim.

Complainant sought pre and post-hospitalization expenses for a relapse occurring within 105 days of discharge. Since policy conditions treated this as a continuous illness and limits were mostly exhausted during the initial hospitalization, the ombudsman allowed only 4 days of remaining post-hospitalization expenses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for IHD and obesity treatment was repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and hypertriglyceridemia. Medical records indicated irregular medication history. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation due to non-disclosure and pre-existing illness.

Claim for treatment of retroviral disease was rejected under exclusion clause 4.9 relating to immunodeficiency conditions and AIDS. Ombudsman upheld the rejection, noting that symptoms stemmed from a retroviral infection indicating immune system failure.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim was repudiated under clauses 4.1 (pre-existing) and 4.10 (hospitalization primarily for diagnostic purpose). Records showed past history of jaundice and hospitalization mainly for evaluation. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim was rejected on the ground of non-cooperation for failing to supply duration of inguinal pain. Ombudsman noted that hospital case papers and a doctor's certificate regarding pain duration were submitted, making the non-cooperation charge invalid, and ordered the claim to be paid in full.

Claim for coronary angiography (CAG) hospitalization was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.10 for diagnostic evaluation without treatment. Ombudsman noted the TMT was strongly positive and CAG was medically necessary, setting aside the total repudiation to allow the cost of CAG and diagnostic tests.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for hypothyroidism, diabetes, and hypertension treatment was repudiated due to pre-existing conditions and suppression of medical history. Hospital records noted a 5-6 year duration. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for cerebral palsy treatment of a child was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was primarily for investigation with no active treatment. Ombudsman noted hospital admission was necessary for proper diagnosis, but balanced equity by ordering payment of 50% of the total hospital expenses.

Insured suffered a hip fracture and osteoporosis after a fall. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion clause citing history of hemiplegia and heart ailments. Ombudsman noted that contributory factors like vertigo and osteoporosis played a part and ordered payment of 40 percent of admissible expenses.

Insured hospitalized for knee pain (Janusoola), arthritis, and varicose veins. Insurer repudiated claim under exclusion clause 4.1. Ombudsman observed that these conditions have a prolonged onset and can be managed at home with physiotherapy, failing to meet the requirement of extreme criticality for hospitalisation, hence upheld the rejection.

Insured minor hospitalized for testis atrophy due to torsion and underwent surgery. Claim rejected under pre-existing disease exclusion. Ombudsman noted hospital records and external shape showed the condition existed before policy inception, so the repudiation was upheld.

Patient admitted for coronary angioplasty with history of diabetes and hypertension. Insurer repudiated claim for pre-existing disease. Investigation and initial hospital records confirmed long-standing illness and attempts to alter duration history, leading the Ombudsman to uphold the insurer's rejection.

Insured hospitalized for angiography and angioplasty after increasing sum insured in 2001. Insurer settled for original sum insured, denying the enhanced amount due to non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as records proved hypertension existed prior to sum insured enhancement.

Insured hospitalized for superior sagittal sinus thrombosis with venous infarct. Claim rejected under first-year exclusion clause 4.3 for sinus conditions. Ombudsman noted the insurer failed to distinguish between common nasal sinusitis and major sinus thrombosis, making the rejection unjustified.

Minor hospitalized for phimosis and balanoposthitis requiring circumcision. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion clauses for congenital external disease and routine circumcision. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as the defect was present since birth.

Child hospitalized for retinal degeneration and hole in both eyes. Claim repudiated for pre-existing condition. Ombudsman observed that high myopia and retinal degeneration at age two indicated a pre-existing condition, sustaining the insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for osteoarthritis of the knee and total knee replacement. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing conditions including hip replacement, diabetes, and hypertension predating the policy. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's repudiation.

Insured hospitalized for polymyalgia rheumatica. Claim partially settled after deductions for echo, CT scan, and diet charges. Ombudsman allowed an additional 50 percent cost of the CT scan since it aided final diagnosis.

Insured hospitalized for lymphadenitis and claimed expenses exceeding the cashless limit imposed by the TPA. Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle an increased amount over the initial limit to cover the hospital bills.

Insured's son hospitalized for malaria and typhoid within thirty days of policy inception. Claim repudiated under exclusion clause 4.2. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as the claim was lodged during the initial 30-day waiting period.

Insured hospitalized for abdominal pain, vomiting, and diagnosed with corrosive gastroduodenitis and hiatus hernia. Claim rejected under pre-existing disease clause due to history of long-standing abdominal pain and prior medical conditions. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim for chronic prolapsed lumbar disc rejected because the nursing home lacked proper registration and the confinement was under 24 hours. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as hospitalisation was unnecessary and treatment could be done in OPD.

Insured hospitalized for polysomnography. TPA settled hospital charges but deducted the cost of a CPAP machine used for sleep disorder. Ombudsman upheld the deduction, ruling that external apparatuses for sleep fall outside policy coverage.

Cancer patient claimed expenses for oral chemotherapy tablets taken at home. Insurer repudiated claims as treatment did not involve hospitalisation or satisfy domiciliary conditions. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for polysomnography. Insurer deducted the cost of a CPAP breathing machine. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation for the machine cost, stating external adjunct apparatuses are excluded under the policy.

Insured admitted for diarrhoea and colonoscopy under a fresh policy. Claim repudiated as hospitalisation was only for investigation without acute emergency or dehydration. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection under exclusion clause 4.10.

Insured renewed policy after a break, facing specific exclusions. Admitted for infected pre-peritoneal haematoma following prior surgeries. Claim repudiated under pre-existing disease clause. Ombudsman upheld the decision as haematoma was a fallout of previous abdominal surgery.

Insured hospitalized and claimed expenses including the cost of a pneumatic walker prescribed by a doctor. Insurer rejected the walker cost. Ombudsman upheld the rejection, noting the policy excludes external appliances.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was treated for chronic calcified pancreatitis. The insurer initially offered 75% non-standard settlement, later repudiated based on panel doctor opinion. The Ombudsman set aside full repudiation and recommended a non-standard 75% settlement.

Insured hospitalized for obstructed right-sided inguinal hernia. Claim repudiated for pre-existing illness and non-disclosure due to past surgeries decades ago. The Ombudsman awarded a 50% compromise settlement.

Insured diagnosed with TB Meningitis and claim repudiated on grounds of pre-existing pulmonary kochs. Since policy was continuously renewed since 1994 across branches, the Ombudsman held the disease was not pre-existing at inception and allowed the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent CABG following coronary artery disease. Claim rejected under exclusion clause because policy was issued with a specific exclusion for diabetes and related problems, which triggered the cardiac condition. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for wife's cataract surgery rejected because the policy had a 24-month waiting period/exclusion for cataract and the claim arose in the second year after a policy break. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Insured hospitalized for benign prostate hypertrophy. Insurer settled part of the claim and disallowed the balance strictly in terms of policy limits. Ombudsman found the settlement correct and dismissed the complaint.

Claim for wife's hospitalization for haematemesis, hiatus hernia and anaemia repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary and for investigations only. Ombudsman rejected the insurer's contention and allowed the claim.

Claim for vaginal hysterectomy due to uterine prolapse repudiated because records indicated the condition existed for 4-5 years prior. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation noting attempts to alter records were invalid.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for excision of gynaecomastia repudiated as cosmetic surgery. Ombudsman noted severe pain and medical necessity, set aside the repudiation, and allowed the complaint.

Insurer deducted charges for laparoscopic instruments and harmonic scalpel during a claim settlement. Ombudsman upheld the deduction as these are reusable surgical instruments, dismissing the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for knee replacement restricted to original sum insured before a major enhancement, as osteoarthritis symptoms existed prior to increasing the sum insured without disclosure. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's restriction.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for myocardial infarction repudiated on grounds of pre-existing hypertension. Insurer failed to produce past medical records. Ombudsman ordered 50% settlement of admissible expenses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for myocardial infarction rejected due to pre-existing hypertension and diabetes, supported by hospital records showing long-term medication use. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Claim for treatment of dysmenorrhoea and endometriotic cysts repudiated on the ground that it was treatment for infertility. Ombudsman noted the procedure cured severe pain and was not infertility treatment, setting aside repudiation.
Claim for 24-hour hospitalization for headache and fever repudiated under exclusion clause as being for investigation and observation only without emergency. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for incisional hernia repudiated under pre-existing disease clause due to history of multiple caesarean sections weakening the abdominal wall and long-standing swelling. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for angioplasty repudiated on grounds of pre-existing heart condition without documentary proof. Ombudsman awarded a non-standard settlement of 60% of admissible expenses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for piles surgery at an authorized day-care ambulatory surgery clinic repudiated because no indoor facility/overnight stay was involved. Ombudsman ruled treatment at a registered center is valid and allowed the claim.

Overseas mediclaim dispute regarding partial settlement of ankle fracture treatment in Canada and currency conversion/deductibles. Ombudsman found calculations as per policy terms and dismissed additional claims.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for deep vein thrombosis and multiple associated ailments rejected due to long-standing pre-existing symptoms. Ombudsman awarded 10% of admissible cost and a lumpsum of Rs. 7,000 as a compromise settlement.
Insured hospitalized for Sarcoidosis atypical pneumonia. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing illness and non-disclosure. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for Left Cardiovascular Embolism with Hemiplegia and IHD. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing condition, but doctor clarified a typo in records. Ombudsman ruled claim sustainable.

Insured hospitalized for Ischemic Heart Disease and underwent PTCA. Insurer deducted cost of Coronary Angiography based on administrative guidelines and policy terms. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.
Insured hospitalized for Single Vessel CAD, PTCA Stent, and Diabetes Mellitus. Policy had an explicit exclusion for diabetes and complications. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Insured admitted for Left MCA Infarct with Right Hemiplegia. Claim rejected due to pre-existing hypertension of 15 years. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.
Insured hospitalized for cataract surgery. Claim capped as per revised group policy terms introduced for specific ailments. Ombudsman upheld insurer's limit.
Domiciliary hospitalization claim rejected for non-submission of bed availability certificate from hospitals. Ombudsman found the rejection unjustified and set it aside.
Insured hospitalized for Botox injection for dystonia. Claim rejected as local injection treatment. Ombudsman recommended a compromise settlement allowing 75% of expenses.
Insured hospitalized for dental implant surgery related to periodontitis. Claim rejected under pre-existing illness clause. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.
Insured hospitalized for thrombotic stroke. Claim rejected due to pre-existing hypertension of 15 years. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for cataract surgery rejected due to lack of past continuous policy documents. Ombudsman ordered 50% settlement taking a liberal view.

Insured hospitalized for bulky cervix and general debility/investigations with negative findings. Claim rejected under exclusion clauses for investigations and general debility. Ombudsman upheld rejection.
Balance claim for Total Knee Arthroplasty under a newer policy rejected due to pre-existing osteoarthritis. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.
Insured hospitalized for vaginal hysterectomy due to adenomyosis. Claim rejected due to pre-existing progressive condition. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for CABG treatment spanning policy years partially paid up to sum insured with zero cumulative bonus. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's calculation.
Claim for CABG rejected on grounds of pre-existing diabetes. Ombudsman ordered a 50:50 compromise settlement due to absence of conclusive proof of pre-existing duration.
Claim for ulcerative colitis closed due to non-availability of documents. Ombudsman reverted the complaint back to insurer for fresh decision based on merits.
Insured hospitalized for Budd-Chiari Syndrome and liver ailments. Claim repudiated due to tampering of medical records and suppression of chronic history. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.
Claim for thumb abscess incision and drainage rejected as non-emergency OPD procedure not requiring hospitalization. Ombudsman upheld the decision.
Claim for subdural haematoma rejected under exclusion clause 4.1. Ombudsman ordered a 50% compromise settlement of the admissible amount.

Insured was hospitalized for heart ailments and diabetes and claimed Rs. 1,03,65,425, out of which Rs. 6,50,288 was settled. The insurer restricted liability based on sum insured limits and past history. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to examine a small disputed amount further.

Insured took an overseas mediclaim policy with specific exclusions for heart and circulatory disorders. While in the USA, he experienced chest pain and was hospitalized for investigations, resulting in a diagnosis of non-cardiac chest pain. The claim was repudiated as expenses related to excluded cardiac conditions and tests without active treatment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for left ureteric calculus. The insurer repudiated the claim based on a remark in hospital papers indicating a similar complaint during pregnancy, invoking a pre-existing exclusion. The Ombudsman noted lack of conclusive proof and allowed admissible expenses as a special case.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for ectopic pregnancy and laparoscopic salpingectomy. The insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.12, as the policy was issued with specific exclusions regarding fallopian tube surgery due to prior tubectomy complications. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured was hospitalized for positional vertigo and claimed reimbursement. The TPA and insurer repudiated the claim stating treatment could have been managed on an OPD basis and invoked exclusion clauses for avoidable hospitalization and investigations. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured's mother was hospitalized for unstable angina and coronary artery disease with stent insertion. The policy was issued with an exclusion for diabetes mellitus. The insurer repudiated the claim stating diabetes was the proximate cause of the heart ailment. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent coronary artery bypass graft and claimed expenses. The insurer restricted the sum insured for heart ailments based on an earlier policy modification. The Ombudsman set aside the partial rejection and directed payment of the balance sum insured with accrued cumulative bonus.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for myocardial infarction and angioplasty, claiming Rs. 6,17,815. The insurer settled Rs. 1,50,000 based on policy terms, excluding diabetes and related complications. The Ombudsman held the insurer's decision to limit the claim to be tenable.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A group personal accident policy was issued to a bank, but the insurer later attempted cancellation. Multiple claims were pending. The Ombudsman reverted the pending complaints back to the insurer for due examination and settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for weakness and frequent micturition. The insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.10, stating the treatment and routine investigations could have been managed on an OPD basis without medical emergency. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized and diagnosed with carcinoma ovary. The insurer repudiated the claim and demanded a refund of a past claim, citing non-disclosure of a hysterectomy performed 17 years prior. The Ombudsman held the repudiation sustainable on non-disclosure grounds but ruled against refunding past amounts.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent coronary artery bypass graft and claimed expenses. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.1, citing a 13-year history of hypertension as a proximate cause of ischemic heart disease. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured's mother underwent cataract surgery and a claim was filed. The insurer repudiated the claim on grounds of pre-existing disease and refractive error exclusions. The Ombudsman granted a 50% settlement considering the policy was in its second year.

Insured's mother was hospitalized for ischemic heart disease. The insurer rejected the claim assuming pre-existing hypertension caused concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. The Ombudsman found no medical records supporting past history and set aside the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for myocardial infarction and a claim was filed. The insurer requested past medical records regarding hypertension and diabetes, but the insured failed to submit them. The insurer repudiated the claim for non-cooperation and non-submission of documents. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for steroid-induced duodenal ulcer and claimed Rs. 1,00,083, of which Rs. 92,683 was settled. Disallowances included charges for an injector needle. The Ombudsman recommended a lump sum of Rs. 2,000 be allowed for the needles.

Insured's minor son underwent herniotomy for inguinal hernia. The TPA and insurer rejected the claim stating the hernia was congenital and pre-existing, and the insured failed to provide rebuttal medical evidence or past records. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for coronary artery disease and underwent angioplasty. The insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.1 for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and irregular heart rhythm of 15 years. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured underwent photo therapeutic keratectomy for vision correction following earlier cataract surgery. The insurer rejected the claim on the grounds of lack of hospital admission necessity and cosmetic surgery. The Ombudsman awarded a 50% settlement as a compromise.

Insured's wife underwent surgery and treatment for breast cancer. The TPA restricted post-hospitalization and hormone treatment expenses. The Ombudsman advised the insurer to pay the exact admissible amount up to July 2004 plus grant one more hormone therapy dose as a special case.

Insured underwent angiography and angioplasty, seeking higher sum insured after increasing it from 2 to 3 lakhs. Insurer restricted liability to 2 lakhs due to pre-existing hypertension and diabetes noted in earlier records. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as the increase in sum insured constituted a fresh contract.

A 15-year-old was hospitalized for bilateral breast abscesses and operated under general anesthesia. TPA repudiated the claim alleging concealment and lack of USG evidence for abscesses. Ombudsman held the claim was genuine and dismissed the allegation of concealment, awarding a net amount after trimming excess investigation costs.

Claim for unstable angina and cardiac evaluation was rejected because hospital records showed the insured had pre-existing diabetes and hypertension for over 5 years, which were concealed or misstated as recent onset.

Claim for vaginal total plication and entero rectocele repair was rejected under pre-existing disease and non-disclosure clauses since treating doctor confirmed it was a recurring prolapse existing prior to policy inception.

Insured underwent angioplasty under a group mediclaim policy. Claim was repudiated because the insured was a known diabetic and hypertensive with chronic pulmonary issues prior to the claim, creating direct medical nexus to cardiovascular disease.

Claim for renal artery stenosis was rejected on the grounds that it is a complication of diabetes, which was expressly excluded from the policy from inception. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's underwriting exclusion.

Claim for acute myocardial infarction and angioplasty was rejected because hospital records indicated long-standing hypertension antedating the policy, and attempts were made to alter medical history certificates.
Claim for hypertensive brain hemorrhage leading to hemiplegia was rejected because blood pressure and cardiac problems were explicitly excluded under the policy terms.

Insured was hospitalized for a knee ligament injury following a scooter fall. Insurer rejected the claim stating treatment could have been managed as an outpatient. Ombudsman set aside total rejection and awarded a lump sum amount.

Claim for hospitalizations due to multiple sclerosis and the high cost of imported Avonex injections was partially restricted by the insurer due to limits on continuous long-term treatment. Ombudsman recommended covering up to the post-hospitalization period with an extra vial as a special case.

Claim for umbilical and incisional hernia repair following a prior cesarean section was rejected under pregnancy exclusion clauses. Ombudsman set aside full rejection and directed payment of 50 percent of the admissible amount.

Claim arising from the death of the insured due to chronic liver disease caused by alcoholic abuse was rejected under policy exclusion clauses pertaining to alcoholism. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.
Claim for total knee replacement due to osteoarthritis was rejected because hospital records showed knee pain existed for eight years, predating the policy inception.

Claim for acute coronary syndrome with hypertension and diabetes was rejected because hospital records showed overwriting in the duration of pre-existing diseases. Ombudsman awarded 50 percent of the claim due to insufficient proof of deliberate non-disclosure.

Claim for chronic pancreatitis was rejected because the policy required four uninterrupted claim-free years for pre-existing disease coverage, but the insured had received intervening medical treatment within that period.
Claim under Universal Health Policy for skin disease treatment was rejected because the insured was never admitted as an inpatient for 24 hours, receiving only daycare treatments lasting a few hours.
Claim for rheumatic heart disease management was rejected because the condition is chronic and typically acquired in childhood, falling under pre-existing disease exclusions.
Claim for congenital heart disease surgery was rejected as congenital anomalies and defects are specifically excluded under policy conditions. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for nasal surgery was rejected because the insured was not hospitalized for over 24 hours due to bed unavailability and was treated as an outpatient.

Claim for heart diagnostic tests and knee swelling treatment was rejected on grounds that cardiac tests showed normal function without positive disease and knee treatment required no hospitalization. Ombudsman upheld rejection of heart test costs but ordered settlement for the knee treatment.

Insured was admitted for depression with anxiety disorders and stayed in ICU for a night. Insurer repudiated the claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary, but Ombudsman held the admission was genuine and ordered settlement.

Policy was cancelled by insurer with prorata refund of balance premium based on claim experience. Subsequent renewal cheque was returned. Ombudsman found cancellation and refusal to renew as per policy conditions.

Policy was cancelled by insurer with prorata refund of balance premium based on claim experience. Subsequent renewal cheque was returned. Ombudsman found cancellation and refusal to renew as per policy conditions.

Insured underwent bypass surgery within eight months of policy inception. Repudiated on grounds of pre-existing CAD and hypertension. Ombudsman noted severe blockages take time to develop and upheld repudiation.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for acute pancreatitis. Claim rejected under pre-existing exclusion due to history of hypothyroidism and other conditions. Insurer directed to obtain medical opinion on nexus and settle pancreatitis expenses if unrelated.

Insured underwent knee surgery following an alleged scooter fall during the first policy year. Claim repudiated due to non-disclosure of pre-existing rheumatoid arthritis. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured underwent ayurvedic treatment for backache as a follow-up to previous hospitalization. Insurer rejected claim as post-hospitalization treatment exceeding the 60-day limit. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.
Renewal cheque was mutilated in transit causing policy cancellation and loss of cumulative bonus upon renewal via demand draft. Ombudsman ordered policy renewal from due date without loss of bonus.

Claim for wife's hospitalization due to enteric fever was delayed by TPA demanding justification for 11 days of admission. Ombudsman ruled TPA cannot question doctor's clinical judgment and ordered settlement.

Insurer treated renewed policy as fresh because interim overseas mediclaim policy was taken from another insurer. Ombudsman held the overseas period counts as continuous extension and ordered claim settlement.
Claim for jaw fracture surgery delayed because pre-operative X-ray was misplaced. Hospital records and post-operative X-rays confirmed treatment. Ombudsman ordered claim settlement.

Claim for hospitalization due to chest pain and high BP was repudiated because tests showed normal results and admission was for investigation purposes. Ombudsman upheld the rejection under exclusion clause.
Insured was hospitalized for readjustment of medication for atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Insurer rejected claim as hospitalization was unwarranted. Ombudsman dismissed complaint.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: Travel health insurance claim for foot infection was rejected as pre-existing. Ombudsman noted policy covers emergency measures to relieve acute pain even in pre-existing conditions and directed insurer to pay for pain relief.

Claim for unstable angina and hypertension rejected due to pre-existing history. Insurer failed to prove existence prior to policy inception date, but insured lacked transparency. Ombudsman granted 40% relief.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd
facts: Claim for cardiac treatment repudiated due to policy break of 7 months, treating subsequent policy as fresh and invoking pre-existing disease exclusion. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for heart treatment rejected due to pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman noted hypertension is only a risk factor and directed insurer to settle expenses exclusively related to ischaemic heart disease.

insurer: The Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for myocardial infarction and angioplasty rejected due to non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman allowed 60% of admissible expenses noting multiple risk factors.

Overseas mediclaim policy claim for delayed baggage expenses including food, taxi, and telephone bills was rejected because policy covers replacement items in baggage, not incidental expenses. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Mouth flap surgery claim rejected due to pre-existing chronic periodontitis, short policy duration, hospital lacking required 20 beds, and stay under 24 hours. Complaint dismissed.

Insured underwent surgery for Incisional Hernia. Insurer rejected claim as pre-existing, linking it to a Caesarian operation done years prior. Forum noted that only the scar was pre-existing, not the hernia itself, and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Insured hospitalized following a road accident and heart treatment. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Forum observed insurer failed to conclusively establish diabetes and hypertension as the proximate cause of the heart problem and directed settlement.

insurer: The Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd
facts: Insured hospitalized for hemithyroidectomy and diagnosed with Papillary Carcinoma. Claim rejected on pre-existing grounds. Ombudsman noted no prior manifestation of symptoms before policy inception and directed the insurer to settle the claim.
Insured underwent Zyoptix surgery for both eyes. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion 4.5. Independent expert opinion confirmed the surgery was cosmetic or aesthetic. Complaint dismissed.

Complainant underwent Ayurvedic treatment following a short break in policy renewal. Insurer treated it as a fresh policy and rejected the claim as pre-existing. Ombudsman allowed 50% of the claim because the insurer failed to obtain a fresh proposal for the renewed policy.

Insured underwent domiciliary treatment for chicken pox. Insurer repudiated claim saying it did not satisfy policy requirements. Doctor clarified lack of hospital isolation facilities. Insurer directed to honour the claim.

Insured underwent thyroid operation. Claim rejected because a break in policy renewal made it a fresh policy, and records proved the disease pre-existed the new commencement date. Repudiation upheld and complaint dismissed.

Insured hospitalized for Cervical spondylosis. Claim repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion due to policy break. Forum noted insured was unaware of diagnosis until hospital admission, and asked insurer to settle the claim.

Insured underwent tests for chest pain following prior angioplasty. Insurer rejected claim stating tests were purely diagnostic and non-payable. Forum found tests were part of continuous treatment and ordered settlement of the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured sought to enhance sum insured. Insurer unilaterally issued policy excluding heart disease for the wife after accepting premium. Forum held insurer's action of imposing restrictions without consent was irregular and against natural justice.

Insured took overseas mediclaim policy, disclosed diabetes and hypertension, and was hospitalized abroad for Haemophilus Parainfluenza Endocarditis. Claim rejected for pre-existing condition. Ombudsman awarded 50% of the claim considering independent genesis of bacterial infection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent coronary angioplasty after enhancing sum insured. Claim restricted to previous lower sum insured because heart ailment was diagnosed prior to the enhancement. Insurer's decision upheld.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for low back pain and inflammatory pseudotumor. Claim declined as tumor was excluded for two years. Forum confirmed it was an infective inflammation, not a true tumor, and directed claim settlement.

Insured hospitalized for thrombosis and infarct. Claim repudiated under pre-existing clause. Insured produced tax records showing policy existed earlier than insurer claimed. Due to conflicting old records, Ombudsman decided on a 50:50 basis.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant claimed compensation for delay in claim settlement. Discharge voucher was executed in full and final settlement. Complaint disposed of without relief as settled cases cannot be reopened.

Insurer deducted registration, ambulance charges, and reduced operation and anaesthetist fees as unreasonable. Ombudsman directed insurer to pay the recovered amount as gradation practice was not authorized.
Insured underwent wisdom tooth removal in a dental clinic operating on OPD basis. Claim repudiated as treatment did not involve hospitalization. Repudiation upheld.
Claim repudiated due to late submission of documents beyond the 30-day policy limit. Complainant blamed insurance agent for delay. Repudiation upheld.
Insured admitted for psychiatric symptoms with negligible medicine expenses. Claim repudiated as hospitalization was for diagnostic purposes. Repudiation upheld.
Insurer denied receipt of claim papers sent by post. Complainant produced courier dispatch proof. Insurer instructed to obtain affidavit and settle full claim.

Claim was repudiated for delayed submission of documents beyond 30 days of discharge. The prospectus allowed 30 days from completion of treatment. Since clauses were inconsistent, the interpretation favouring the policyholder applied and full claim was awarded.
Insured was admitted primarily for diagnostic evaluations to rule out disease. Since investigations did not lead to any precise diagnosis, the insurer's repudiation of the claim was upheld.

Insured underwent CABG following triple vessel disease. The policy excluded complications of Coronary Artery Disease. The insurer's repudiation was upheld as the condition was a complication of previous illness.
Complainant deployed four boats for search and assistance of a sinking boat. The surveyor assessed the sue and labour amount at Rs. 35,000, which was awarded as full and final settlement.
Deductions made from accidental injury claim included doctor home visits and x-ray charges which were conceded as payable, while ambulance charges were inadmissible under the policy.
Insured underwent root canal treatment at a dental clinic without hospitalization. Since policy terms required hospitalization for dental treatment admissibility, the repudiation was upheld.

Insured shifted between hospitals without certificates and incurred overlapping bills. Additionally, expenses incurred after 60 days of discharge were not reimbursable under policy rules, upholding the deduction.

Claim for surgery to remove an ovarian cyst was repudiated under sterility and pregnancy exclusions. Medical evidence showed the hospitalization was for dysmenorrhoea rather than infertility, so the insurer was directed to pay.
Claim was repudiated because the insured failed to disclose a prior laminectomy operation for spondylosis in the proposal form, breaching utmost good faith.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured claimed for UTI and renal stones but failed to disclose a previous history of aortic valve replacement, renal stone surgery, and recurrent UTI in the proposal form.

Claim was repudiated for non-disclosure, but documents showed the policy continuously incepted earlier from a different branch of the same insurer which had previously settled a claim. However, the dismissal outcome was maintained based on overall findings.

Claim for post-partum breast abscess following child birth was repudiated under policy exclusions for treatments arising from pregnancy or child birth. The medical nexus was established, upholding the repudiation.
Hospital records noted prior history of myocardial infarction and hypertension not disclosed in the proposal form. The insurer's repudiation for non-disclosure was upheld.

Claim for osteoarthritis of the knee was repudiated on medical opinion that the disease takes years to develop. Since the insurer produced no indisputable evidence of pre-existence, full payment was ordered.

Claim for shoulder dislocation was repudiated on the ground that no anaesthesia was used and treatment could be on OPD basis. The ombudsman noted anaesthesia was avoided due to age and diabetes, ordering full settlement.

Insured sought expenses for secondary hospitalization for hemiplegia without clear medical advice. Furthermore, the complainant had executed an unqualified discharge voucher in full settlement, estopping reopening.
Complainant contested the calculation of cumulative bonus. The insurer admitted to a calculation error during the hearing and was directed to pay the balance amount.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for tumor in buccal mucosa was repudiated under an exclusion clause excluding tumors and cysts within the first two years of the policy.

Householder insurance claim for domestic appliances damaged by voltage fluctuation was repudiated solely because the insured failed to intimate a change of address. Insurer was directed to pay the assessed loss.

Claim for cardiac failure was repudiated as pre-existing due to a seven-day policy renewal break in 2002. Since no fresh proposal was taken and cumulative bonus was not reduced, the gap was deemed condoned and full claim was awarded.

Insured underwent CABG, HPT and DM, leading to claim repudiation for pre-existing disease after a 7-day policy renewal break in 2002. The ombudsman noted no fresh proposal was taken and directed full claim payment.

A toddler was hospitalised for acute watery diarrhoea and severe dehydration within the first 30 days of the policy. The insurer rejected the claim under the initial 30-day waiting period clause. The ombudsman found the rejection unjustified given the sudden illness and ordered full payment.
Insured was admitted for coronary artery bypass surgery and had a 20-year history of hypertension. The insurer's repudiation for pre-existing disease was upheld by the ombudsman.

Insured was operated for right eye sub-retinal neovascular membrane. Clinical history showed high myopia since age 10, proving a causal nexus with the condition predating the policy. The insurer's repudiation was upheld.

Insured underwent naturopathy treatment for tonsillitis and bronchitis. The insurer rejected the claim arguing naturopathy was excluded. As the policy did not explicitly exclude naturopathy, the insurer was directed to pay the full claim.
Insured underwent naturopathy treatment for tonsillitis and bronchitis, which the insurer rejected. The ombudsman noted no exclusion for naturopathy existed in the policy and directed full payment.

Insured underwent abdominal hysterectomy for a chocolate cyst. The insurer repudiated the claim due to prior history of chocolate cysts and non-disclosure in the proposal form. The insurer's decision was upheld.

A claim lodged on 23-02-2005 experienced significant delays due to TPA requirements and processing, resulting in an inordinate delay. The ombudsman ordered simple interest at 8% p.a. for the delayed settlement.

Insured was hospitalised for left breast abscess a month after giving birth. The insurer rejected the claim under the exclusion for treatments arising from child birth. The ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured underwent coronary angioplasty but had a 10-year history of hypertension not disclosed in the proposal form. The non-disclosure vitiated the contract, and the insurer's repudiation was upheld.

Claim was rejected for late submission after 6 months, though prospectuses allowed submission within 30 days of treatment completion. Due to inconsistent clauses favouring the policyholder, the insurer was directed to pay the full claim.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was treated for unstable angina and coronary artery disease within 11 months of policy inception. The insurer rejected it as pre-existing based on medical referee presumption without documents. The ombudsman directed full payment.

Insured failed to disclose a history of left breast cancer in the proposal form. Subsequent bone metastasis led to hospitalisation. Misstatement breached utmost good faith, and the insurer's repudiation was upheld.

Insured was hospitalised for post-hysterectomy left ureteric stricture. The insurer rejected the claim due to a past history of urethral dilation. The ombudsman noted the urethra and ureter are anatomically different, and directed full payment.

Insured was admitted for removal of a dermoid ovarian cyst within two years of policy inception, rejected as a congenital internal disease. Medical literature showed dermoid cysts are not strictly congenital. Repudiation was set aside and full claim ordered.
Insured was operated for sub-acute intestinal obstruction caused by adhesions from a prior LSCS surgery predating the policy. The nexus was established, and the insurer's repudiation was upheld.
Insured was discharged within 22 hours of surgery. The policy explicitly required a minimum 24-hour hospitalisation. The insurer's repudiation was upheld.

Insured suffered sudden chest pain and underwent coronary angioplasty within 10 months of policy inception. The insurer rejected it as pre-existing based on medical opinion without supporting documents. Full claim was awarded.

Claim was rejected because the hospital supposedly had only 9 in-patient beds instead of the required 15. The insured produced certificates proving the hospital had 16 beds, and the insurer was directed to pay the full claim.

Insured was hospitalised for giddiness for a day of investigations. Since charges incurred primarily for investigative examinations are excluded under the policy, the insurer's repudiation was upheld.
Complainant was hospitalised for fracture within the policy period. The insurer deducted Rs. 4742 on specific items. During the hearing, parties agreed to an additional payment of Rs. 2150.

Insured was hospitalised for acute chest pain. Insurer repudiated due to inconsistencies in submission papers, but the ombudsman held this insufficient and directed payment after deducting expenses for the period beyond post-hospitalisation.

Insured claimed for pyrexia with convulsions. Policy sum insured was enhanced in the second year. Insurer treated the ailment as pre-existing and settled only for the original sum insured. The ombudsman upheld this decision.

Insured was operated for large CBD stone, having previously undergone cholecystectomy 12 years prior. Insurer repudiated due to pre-existing condition and non-disclosure, which was upheld by the ombudsman.
Insured was operated for stenosing tenosynovitis on expert advice. Insurer's repudiation on the grounds of investigative hospitalisation was set aside and full claim was awarded.

Insured was hospitalised for foot cellulitis with non-healing ulcer and had a 10-year history of diabetes and heart disease. Nexus with pre-existing condition being established, repudiation was upheld.
Insured was hospitalised for severe back pain on specialist advice. Insurer rejected claiming OPD treatment sufficed, but the ombudsman set aside the rejection and directed full payment.
Insured was hospitalised for hypertension and thyroidism. Conflicting documents regarding the duration of past hypertension led the ombudsman to uphold the insurer's repudiation.
Insurer deducted treatment charges citing unreasonable hospital fees. As neither prospectus nor policy schedule contained such restrictions, the insurer was directed to refund the deducted amount.
Insured underwent breast reduction surgery for chronic back and shoulder pain. Repudiation under plastic surgery exclusion was set aside as the operation was certified as illness-related.
Deductions were made for room charges and medicine during a hysterectomy treatment. Since the validity of hospital payments was undisputed, full payment was ordered.
Duplicate case entry regarding vaginal hysterectomy deductions for room charges and medicines. The insurer was directed to pay the full claim.
A 3-year-old child was hospitalised for fever and convulsions, having a history of neonatal ICU stay and recurrent convulsions prior to policy inception. Repudiation was upheld.
Insurer disallowed costs for oxygen instruments and glucometer strips during pulmonary fibrosis treatment. The ombudsman held that domiciliary oxygen is life-saving and ordered payment.
Insurer disallowed oxygen therapy machine costs for pulmonary fibrosis. The ombudsman ruled it as life-saving and ordered reimbursement.
First hospitalisation occurred prior to policy inception and second was a direct consequence of the first. Insurer's repudiation was upheld.
Complainant was hospitalised for diagnostic investigations regarding leg pain. Marginal medicine costs indicated hospitalisation was primarily for diagnostics, upholding the repudiation.
Insured was treated for rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, linked to past pregnancy-induced hypertension not disclosed in the proposal form. Repudiation upheld.
Insured operated for incisional hernia with past history of caesarean and cholecystectomy. Direct nexus with prior surgeries established, upholding the repudiation.
Claim was submitted after a delay of over 65 days against the 30-day policy requirement. With vague reasons for delay, repudiation was upheld.

Complainant sought reimbursement for multiple papilloma nose/oral cavities treatment. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing disease (hypertension and history of surgeries) under exclusion clause 4.1. Ombudsman found the insurer's decision fair and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant met with an accident and suffered a leg fracture requiring hospitalization. Insurer failed to respond or settle the claim. Ombudsman held the insurer's inaction unjust and ordered full payment with interest.

Complainant's wife was diagnosed with breast cancer and operated during the first 30 days of the policy. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion 4.2 for diseases contracted within the initial 30 days. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant was hospitalized for illness while visiting family and sought reimbursement. TPA delayed and demanded documents the complainant could not provide. Ombudsman ruled the non-settlement unjust and ordered payment with interest.

Complainant was hospitalized for diagnostic investigations and tests without active treatment. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion 4.10 as hospitalization was unnecessary and could be done on an OPD basis. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Complainant's daughter was hospitalized for headache and underwent tests without positive ailment requiring confinement. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion 4.10 for diagnostic admissions. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant underwent surgery for avascular necrosis of the right femur. Insurer rejected the reimbursement claim citing pre-existing hip pain predating the policy by 2-3 years under exclusion C-1. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Complainant's daughter was treated for tectal plate glioma with hydrocephalus. Insurer repudiated the claim stating the condition was congenital under exclusion 4.8. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for abortion. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.12 regarding pregnancy-related treatments. Ombudsman found the rejection justified and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant's mother was treated for a femur fracture. Insurer restricted the claim payout based on the previous year's lower sum insured due to a pre-existing condition clause. Ombudsman upheld the reduced payout.

Complainant hospitalized for acute on chronic renal failure and cardiac conditions. Insurer repudiated claim due to non-disclosure of pre-existing illnesses dating back over 10 years and policy breaks. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Complainant underwent PTCA for coronary artery disease after holding a policy since 1998, disclosing past IHD that was cured. Insurer rejected the claim for pre-existence. Ombudsman ordered full payment as the insurer failed to prove exclusion application.

Complainant's child underwent surgery for nasal polyp. Insurer repudiated the claim claiming treatment for sinusitis under exclusion 4.3. Treating doctor confirmed it was tonsillitis, not sinusitis. Ombudsman ordered full reimbursement.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for medical tests that did not confirm a positive ailment. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion 4.10 for unnecessary hospitalization. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Complainant's son was treated for cavernous sinus thrombosis and periorbital cellulitis. Insurer denied cashless service and claim under exclusion 3.3 for sinusitis. Records showed surgery was for eye infection. Ombudsman ordered payment.

Complainant sought 25% balance hospitalization expenses for wife's treatment of nasal fungal infection and diabetes. TPA rejected claim citing sinusitis. Ombudsman noted treatment was for fungal infection and diabetes, which were not excluded, and ordered payment.

Complainant hospitalized for CAD and treated for cardiac issues. TPA rejected claim as pre-existing diabetes under a new policy. Ombudsman held that a 7-day renewal grace period applied, making it a continuous policy without pre-existing exclusion grounds, and ordered payment.

Complainant and wife underwent knee treatment using Sytotron Therapy. Insurer rejected claim arguing hospitalization was unnecessary. Specialist confirmed specialized infrastructure requirements. Ombudsman ordered payment of admissible claim.

Complainant met with an accident resulting in facial trauma and dental fractures, later completing dental treatment. Insurer rejected dental costs as unnotified post-hospitalization. Ombudsman noted prior intimation was given and ordered payment.

Complainant was hospitalized for high blood sugar after 6-7 years of policy continuity. Insurer settled the claim but unilaterally cancelled the policy under clause 5.9. Ombudsman cited high court rulings against arbitrary renewal refusal and ordered policy reinstatement.

Insured couple underwent laser surgeries at a hospital and submitted reimbursement claims. Insurer paid partly based on reasonable and necessary expenses, citing quotations from other hospitals. Ombudsman noted TPA failed to warn about high hospital charges before admission and directed settlement of pre-hospitalisation expenses on an ex-gratia basis.

Complainant was hospitalised for hypertension, headache, and burning micturition. Insurer repudiated the claim stating hospitalisation was purely for diagnostic purposes and routine health check-up under exclusion clause 4.10. Forum observed the hospitalisation was warranted due to increased systolic BP and angina, and directed reimbursement while disallowing age-related ENT expenses.

Complainant argued short settlement of a flood damage claim where the insurer disallowed the crankshaft because the repairer failed to submit a required survey certificate. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the crankshaft claim while disallowing parts not affected by floodwater.

Complainant's wife was hospitalised and died. The claim was declined because the spouse was not covered under the group mediclaim policy, as the proposal and premium were for the complainant only. The complainant attempted to use a pre-printed tax certificate for tax benefits to claim coverage. Complaint was dismissed.

Complainant hospitalized for Melaney’s Gangrene. Insurer repudiated claim under exclusion clause 4.1 due to non-disclosure of diabetes for 14 years. Medical records established that Diabetes Mellitus existed prior to policy inception in 2001 and caused the diabetic foot condition. Complaint was dismissed.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought reimbursement for injuries from a two-wheeler fall. Insurer rejected the claim stating treatment was primarily for pre-existing Cervical Spondylosis and there was no proof of accident. An orthopedic surgeon opined the meniscal tear was unrelated to a fall and recommended treatments were not administered. Complaint was dismissed.

Complainant hospitalized for vocal nodule surgery incurring Rs 49,466, but claim was paid only up to Rs 25,000 based on reasonable and necessary hospital expenses compared to standard hospital rates. The forum allowed an additional ex-gratia amount of Rs 10,000 considering the insured's helplessness regarding hospital charges.

Complainant's wife was hospitalised for headache and giddiness. Insurer repudiated the claim stating the ailment did not warrant hospitalisation and no significant medication was given. Forum noted subsequent psychiatric consultation implied physical or mental health problems and partly allowed the claim for specific diagnostic and room-rent expenses.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for chest discomfort, systemic hypertension, and atypical chest pain. TPA rejected the claim citing pre-existing diabetes based on an erroneous discharge summary note. Attending doctor clarified the patient had no diabetes. Since policy was active since 1995 and insurer failed to prove pre-existing diabetes, settlement was ordered.

Complainant's wife was hospitalised for hernia. TPA repudiated the claim citing non-disclosure of past LSCS and tubectomy operations in 1998, alleging a pre-existing condition. Forum noted the insured did not consider childbirth a disease requiring disclosure, and there was no specific query in the proposal form. Insurer was directed to settle the claim.

Complainant underwent heart surgery following an angiogram and submitted a reimbursement claim. Insurer repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1 for non-disclosure of pre-existing ailments. Hospital medical records from Madras Medical Mission showed the patient was a known diabetic for 20 years and hypertensive for 10 years. Complaint was dismissed.

Complainant sought domiciliary hospitalization expenses for physiotherapy administered by a trained nurse due to lack of a female physiotherapist locally. Insurer short-settled due to lack of pukka bills and attending doctor certificates. Ombudsman allowed the claim on an ex-gratia basis to prevent further harassment and delay.

Complainant was hospitalised for allergic rhinosinusitis, diabetes, and hypertension, but cashless facility and reimbursement were denied. Insurer initially cited pre-existing disease and later changed stance to first-year policy exclusion for sinusitis due to a 42-day policy break. Forum noted sinusitis falls under first-year exclusion and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant hospitalized for jaundice. Claim was rejected on the grounds of pre-existing Hepatitis B contracted 7 years prior, which was disclosed in the pre-authorization form signed by the complainant but omitted from the proposal form. Forum observed that a prior Hepatitis B infection makes the person an all-time carrier, and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant's wife had a Mediclaim policy for 10 years before shifting to a Medi-guard policy. At renewal, the insurer imposed a 200% premium loading and excluded cancer due to high previous claims. Forum noted the insured was doubly penalized and ordered the insurer to rescind the cancer exclusion since the policy had been renewed continuously without a break.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalised and diagnosed with cholelithiasis (gall bladder stones). Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing condition because the 22 mm stone and 'chronic' histopathology report implied it took over 6 months to form.
