Forum noted no medical records proved pre-existence before policy inception and ordered the insurer to settle the claim.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant held credit card hospital cash plans and was hospitalized for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD). Insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension and ischemic heart disease (IHD) dating back 13 years. Forum perused medical records confirming pre-existing IHD and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant hospitalized for proteinuria and hypertension. Insurer repudiated claim alleging proteinuria was pre-existing since 2001. Forum observed that neither the attending doctor's certification nor the discharge summary indicated significant proteinuria before 2002, and the insurer failed to conduct investigations or submit biopsy reports proving hypertension caused it. Claim was allowed.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for pneumonia and incurred Rs 30,476 under a UTI cardholder mediclaim policy. Insurer settled Rs 30,143, disallowing Rs 333 for pre- and post-hospitalization expenses not covered under the scheme. Forum found the delay and disallowance unjustified for extra relief, and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant's mother was hospitalized for atherosclerotic coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and unstable angina. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing diabetes for 17 years. Forum found diabetes and hypothyroidism were pre-existing, but the insurer failed to prove diabetes was the proximate cause for CAD. Direction was given to settle the claim.

Insured was hospitalized for nasal bleeding. The claim was rejected on the ground of pre-existing hypertension. The insurer failed to establish by documentary evidence that the nasal bleeding was caused by hypertension. The complaint was allowed.

Insured was hospitalized for chronic calculus cholecystitis and chronic appendicitis. The claim was rejected due to pre-existing disease and a break in insurance. The insurer failed to prove prior diagnosis or awareness. The complaint was allowed.

Insured underwent emergency lower segment caesarean section following infertility treatment. The claim was rejected under the policy exclusion for maternity and childbirth treatments. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured was hospitalized for contusion of knee and internal derangement of knee. The claim was declined on the ground that hospitalization was not warranted as treatment was managed via outpatient care. The complaint was dismissed.

Complainant claimed Rs 22,722 for daughter's fever treatment, but received Rs 7,722 due to exorbitant room rent and prolonged stay after fever subsided. The forum noted tariff variations and attending doctor's advice, directing settlement of the balance subject to policy terms.

Insured suffered a complete anterior cruciate ligament tear requiring arthroscopic surgery. The claim was repudiated on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary and for diagnostic purposes only. The forum found active treatment was warranted, and allowed the complaint.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and triple vessel disease during a train journey. The claim was repudiated as pre-existing. As the insurer failed to prove prior onset, the complaint was allowed.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured daughter was hospitalized for ureteric calculi and underwent cystoscopy and lithotripsy. The claim was rejected on the ground of pre-existing symptoms from a stone two years prior. The insurer failed to prove continuous existence, and the complaint was allowed.

Child was hospitalized for a neck swelling surgery. The claim was repudiated under first-year congenital disease exclusion. The insurer failed to establish a congenital defect, and the complaint was allowed.

Insured was hospitalized for incisional hernia. The claim was rejected under exclusion 4.1 because an open hysterectomy was done 14 years prior. The forum noted only the scar was pre-existing, not the hernia, and allowed the complaint.

Complainant fell and was hospitalized for hypertension, vestibular neuronitis, and tendinitis. The claim was rejected as hospitalization was unnecessary and manageable as an outpatient. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured underwent coronary artery bypass surgery after cardiac arrest. The claim was rejected due to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. The forum directed the insurer to pay expenses related to the CAD treatment alone.

insurer: Cholamandalam MS Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd
facts: Insured underwent I-131 ablation therapy for thyroid cancer complications. The claim was rejected as pre-existing. Since the insured had no treatment for over 24 months prior to inception, the condition did not qualify as pre-existing. The complaint was allowed.

Insured was hospitalized for pneumonia and pulmonary oedema and subsequently died. The claim was rejected due to pre-existing diabetes. The death summary confirmed pneumonia as the cause without prior indication, so the complaint was allowed.

Insured wife underwent cataract surgery. The claim was initially repudiated under first-year exclusion due to overlapping policies. Verification showed continuous prior coverage under Jan Arokya Policy, so the complaint was allowed.

Insured was hospitalized for cirrhosis of liver. Prior claims were short-settled and the third claim rejected as pre-existing. The insurer failed to prove awareness or prior symptoms at inception, so all claims were allowed.

Insured was hospitalized for papillary endocervicitis after an 11-day renewal break caused by a bounced cheque. The claim was rejected under first-year exclusion. The insurer had granted cumulative bonus indicating continuity, so the complaint was allowed.

Insured wife was hospitalized for degenerative lumbar canal stenosis. The claim was rejected because she had a 5-6 year history of back pain and prior hospitalizations which were not disclosed in the 2005 proposal form following an insurance break. The complaint was dismissed.
Insured underwent surgery for complications from a prior surgery. The claim was rejected for non-disclosure of past illness during a 3-month insurance break. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured was hospitalized for heart disease. The claim was repudiated due to pre-existing hypertension. The insurer failed to establish hypertension as the proximate cause of coronary artery disease, so the complaint was allowed.

The insured was hospitalized for proximal weakness following physical strain. The insurer rejected the claim stating that only evaluations and general vitamins were given, which could be managed as an OPD procedure without requiring hospital infrastructure. The Ombudsman upheld the dismissal.

The insured complained about retrospective policy renewal without coverage and non-renewal of credit card medical plans. The Ombudsman directed a refund of premium for the retroactive gap period, offered prospective family floater coverage on EMI, and waived the insurance break period for benefits.

The insured's wife was hospitalized for incisional hernia. The insurer rejected the claim as a pre-existing condition due to prior surgeries. The Ombudsman noted that the policy excludes pre-existing diseases, not prior scars, and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

The insured was hospitalized for a non-healing wound over the left knee with hemophilia, diabetes, and hypertension. The insurer rejected the claim due to non-disclosure and pre-existing conditions. The Ombudsman ordered 50% payment of the claim amount.

The insured's wife underwent knee surgery and the claim was rejected under congenital disease and pre-existing exclusions. Since the insurer failed to provide documentary evidence proving the condition was congenital or pre-existing prior to inception, the Ombudsman allowed the complaint.

The insured was hospitalized for chest pain and underwent coronary angiography. The claim was rejected on pre-existing grounds due to hypertension and diabetes. The Ombudsman found that the policy predated the alleged onset of ailments and directed settlement.

The insured was hospitalized for ischemic heart disease. The insurer rejected the claim citing a pre-existing heart condition since 2000 based on ECG variations. The Ombudsman found no conclusive proof of awareness or active treatment and allowed the complaint.

The insured was hospitalized for coronary artery disease. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing heart issues from 20 years prior and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman noted an isolated old chest pain episode without treatment history did not justify exclusion and allowed the claim.

The insured's wife was treated for arthritis and skin lesions. The insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing joint pain. The Ombudsman upheld the denial for 'Vatha' complaints due to prior records but allowed reimbursement for 'Pittha' treatments as they lacked specific exclusion.

The insured's mother was hospitalized for depressive illness and hypertension. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing conditions and lack of medical necessity. The Ombudsman noted the attending doctor's assessment justified admission and ordered settlement.

Under a hospital cash plan, the insured claimed benefits for hospitalization due to coronary angiography. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. The Ombudsman noted insufficient proof of prior CAD and awarded cash benefits strictly for the 2 days hospitalized.

The insured was hospitalized for continuous hematuria and bladder issues. The insurer repudiated the claim for pre-existing bladder cancer and suppression of material facts. Finding overwhelming evidence of prior treatment and lack of transparency, the Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

The insured suffered loss of luggage, laptop, and camera at a railway station. The insurer demanded a court closure order for the police FIR. The Ombudsman held that missing baggage is an accident or misfortune covered under all-risks policies and allowed the claim for the laptop and camera subject to limits.

The insured was hospitalized for chest pain and diagnosed with CAD under a two-month-old policy. The insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing based on smoking history and ECG findings. As there was no documentary proof of prior CAD symptoms before policy inception, the Ombudsman allowed the claim.

The insured was hospitalized for lower abdominal pain. The insurer repudiated the claim due to non-disclosure of a prior abdominal surgery prior to policy inception. Finding material concealment, the Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

The insurer refused to renew a long-standing mediclaim policy due to a one-day delay in premium submission, following a prior claim. The Ombudsman noted divisional managers had authority to waive gaps up to 15 days and directed the insurer to renew the policy without medical examination.

The insured was hospitalized for acute pancreatitis. Cashless access was initially approved but later repudiated on the grounds of alcohol intake. The Ombudsman noted normal liver function tests and medical evidence showing alcohol was an unlikely cause, and allowed the claim.

The insured's child was hospitalized for respiratory infections. The insurer repudiated the claim based on pre-existing tricuspid regurgitation and pulmonary arterial hypertension diagnosed prior to policy inception. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

The insured underwent surgery for a brain tumor (plasmacytoma) and multiple myeloma. The insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing based on a history of eye proptosis and headache. The Ombudsman found no proof the insured suffered from the tumor prior to inception and awarded the claim with interest.

The insured underwent bilateral total knee replacement for osteoarthritis. The insurer rejected the claim alleging degenerative changes could not develop so quickly and were pre-existing. Since the insured had continuous prior coverage exceeding the waiting period, the Ombudsman allowed the claim.

Insured claimed reimbursement for medical expenses. Insurer paid part but deducted admission charges and various supplies as non-payable. The Ombudsman noted the insurer's assurance to pay the full amount and directed payment of the remaining balance along with return of original records.

Insured's wife underwent Total Abdominal Hysterectomy for fibroids and cervicitis. Insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing condition based on past history of vaginal discharge and MTPs over 10-12 years. The Ombudsman held that common symptoms do not constitute a specific pre-existing disease and ruled the claim payable.

Insured underwent Septoplasty surgery. Claim was repudiated because medical records and treating doctor's certificate showed he was under treatment for common cold and nasal blocking prior to the inception of the policy. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured claimed for machinery breakdown of an air conditioner under a household policy. Insurer repudiated based on a surveyor report attributing loss to wear and tear. The Ombudsman found the survey deficient as the compressor was never opened and awarded 50% of the estimated loss with interest.

Insured with declared diabetes was hospitalized for nasal bleeding and accelerated hypertension. Insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing under clause 4.2. The Ombudsman observed that hypertension was not related to diabetes and ordered payment of the claim with interest.

Insured underwent surgery for Hernia during the first year of a new policy following a 12-day break in continuity. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.3 which excludes hernia in the first year. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision due to the policy break.

Insured contracted hepatitis C and claimed reimbursement for outpatient treatment involving weekly injections. Insurer rejected the claim on the grounds that treatment was taken on OPD basis without hospitalization. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as mediclaim covers hospitalization expenses only.

Insured faced policy renewal delay and gap, losing accumulated bonus. Claims were filed for prostate treatment and hepatitis C. Insurer disallowed prostate treatment as a first-year exclusion and paid the hepatitis C claim. The Ombudsman upheld the disallowance of the prostate claim.

Retired employee claimed reimbursement for a CPAP machine prescribed for his wife. Insurer disallowed the amount treating it as an external equipment. The Ombudsman held that since artificial limbs and similar expenses are covered, and there was no specific exclusion, the cost of the machine must be paid.

Insured filed a claim for wife's hospitalization for diabetes. Insurer repudiated after long delay alleging pre-existing diabetes of 16 years. The Ombudsman noted discrepancies in the insurer's stance given the long-standing policy history and cumulative bonuses.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for acute cholecystitis. Insurer repudiated the claim invoking pre-existing exclusion due to a short renewal gap and past abdominal pain recorded in a consultation. The Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existence of the specific disease and ordered fresh assessment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured submitted a claim for son's treatment. TPA heavily reduced the payout without reasons. The Ombudsman assessed the actual vouchers and made a lumpsum reasonable award accepted by the insured.

Insured claimed reimbursement for multiple medical bills. Insurer paid some claims but rejected one using the pre-existing disease clause based on a doctor's certificate. The Ombudsman referred the matter back to the insurer for exhaustive review due to inadequate records.

Insured was hospitalized for diabetes complications. Claim was repudiated because diabetes was diagnosed in 1978, prior to policy inception in 1993, and there was a delay in renewal making it a fresh policy. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for medical expenses of insured's 22-year-old son was rejected because dependents above 21 years were covered only if pursuing full-time higher studies, which was not proved. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured's wife underwent hernia surgery. Claim was rejected because the hernia resulted from a hysterectomy done in 1976, which was not disclosed in the proposal form. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation based on non-disclosure of material facts.

Insured under a Janata Personal Accident policy suffered traumatic paraparesis resulting in 50% partial disability. Insurer rejected the claim as the policy only covered total and permanent disablement. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Commercial truck met with an accident. Insurer offered a settlement amount which the insured refused as inadequate. Since no bills or estimates were submitted by the insured, the Ombudsman directed the insurer to reassess based on documents and surveyor report.

Insured underwent treatment for vocal cord polyp. TPA rejected the claim under pre-existing clause. Since the insurer's panel doctor opined the disease was not pre-existing and the insurer had already recommended review, the Ombudsman referred the matter back for final decision.

Insured claimed pre-hospitalization costs following heart surgery. TPA rejected the claim due to non-declaration of diabetes and hypertension in pre-authorization. As the insurer had not taken a final decision and file was missing from TPA, the Ombudsman directed the insurer to retrieve the file and decide.

Insured claimed reimbursement for incisional hernia surgery. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing condition related to a previous total hysterectomy. The Ombudsman held that the insurer failed to prove pre-existence or prior knowledge, and the hernia was detected months after policy inception. Complaint allowed.

Insured's claim for dysfunctional uterine bleeding treatment was rejected because hospitalization was under 24 hours and bills appeared excessive. The Ombudsman noted conflicting discharge certificates regarding admission duration and directed the insurer to constitute a medical board for expert verification.

Insured underwent surgeries for lumbar canal stenosis. Insurer rejected claims citing pre-existing backache and a policy break due to a dishonored renewal cheque. The Ombudsman found the continuous policy status valid and rejected the pre-existing disease plea due to lack of concrete proof. Claims ordered to be settled.

Insured's wife underwent bypass surgery for arterial occlusion. Insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing based on the severity of blockage. The Ombudsman observed that symptoms arose months after policy inception and pre-existence was not established. Complaint allowed.

Insured underwent mastectomy and chemotherapy for breast malignancy in the first year of policy. Cashless and reimbursement claims were rejected under policy exclusion for internal tumors during the first two consecutive years. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured claimed post-hospitalization expenses towards attender charges at home following treatment for depression and other ailments. Insurer rejected the claim stating attender charges are domiciliary expenses not covered under the policy. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured was admitted for headache and abdominal pain. TPA reimbursed only a health check-up fee of 1 percent, treating the hospitalization as a routine check-up. Ombudsman held that the admission was due to actual ailments and directed settlement of treatment costs excluding unrelated executive check-ups.

Insured's son underwent surgical reduction for inferior turbinate hypertrophy. Claim was rejected on the ground that first-year policies exclude sinusitis and related disorders. Based on expert medical opinion that the condition was allergic rhinitis and unrelated to sinusitis, the Ombudsman allowed the complaint.

Insurer initially approved cashless treatment but later repudiated the claim citing alcohol abuse under policy exclusions. During proceedings, the insurer settled the hospital bills. Ombudsman awarded compensation for delay caused by poor communication between insurer and TPA.

Insured's wife underwent angioplasty. Claim was rejected due to pre-existing coronary artery disease and a policy renewal gap. Ombudsman upheld the exclusion based on proposal declarations but awarded ex-gratia compensation due to contradictory policy drafting.

Insured underwent flap surgeries and bone grafting for chronic periodontitis and claimed hospitalization expenses. Insurer rejected the claim stating the procedure did not warrant inpatient admission. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as hospitalization was unjustified and hypertension history was unproven.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for evaluation of polyarthritis. Claim was rejected on the ground that investigations could be done on an outpatient basis. Ombudsman agreed the admission was for evaluation and directed payment for health check-up as offered by the insurer.

Insured underwent surgery for retro calcaneal bursitis. Claim was rejected as pre-existing by the TPA. During proceedings, the insurer agreed to pay the claim upon re-submission of papers. Ombudsman directed the insured to re-submit documents.

Insured was hospitalized for chest pain and diagnosed with hypertension and an absent left kidney. Claim was rejected for pre-existing hypertension and non-disclosure. Ombudsman found hospital bedside notes showed recent onset of blood pressure issues and allowed the claim.

Insured was admitted for fever and evaluated for early Parkinson's disease. TPA initially approved cashless part, then withdrew it claiming hospitalization was for investigation only. Ombudsman directed partial ex-gratia settlement considering lapses on both sides.

Insured claimed reimbursement for eye treatment expenses which included an advance payment for medicines under a pharma company scheme. Insurer disallowed part of the claim alleging exhaustion of sum insured under another policy. Ombudsman verified invoice dates and directed full payment with interest.

Insured suffered a chemical eye injury leading to total blindness and claimed 50 percent of the sum insured. Insurer rejected the claim due to delayed intimation and lack of accidental proof. Ombudsman directed the insurer to condone the delay and process the claim upon document submission.

Insured met with a road accident and succumbed to injuries. Insurer rejected personal accident claim due to delayed intimation and document submission. Ombudsman held that police records clearly established the cause of death and directed the insurer to process the claim.

Insured underwent cataract surgery in the second policy year and third policy year. Insurer partially paid then later repudiated the second claim invoking first-year cataract exclusion based on incorrect policy start dates. Ombudsman found the insurer's data wrong and ordered full payment.

Insured died of acute renal failure secondary to long-standing hypertension. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing hypertension, edema, and filariasis not disclosed in the proposal. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured underwent knee replacement surgery in 2006. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds of pre-existing disease after the sum insured was enhanced in May 2005. The Ombudsman held that the condition was pre-existing for the enhanced sum insured, but directed the insurer to honor the claim for the basic sum insured of Rs. 95,000 with cumulative bonus.

Complainant underwent angioplasty and claimed Rs. 2,46,063. The insurer partially paid, restricting the sum insured to a previous lower amount due to alleged pre-existing hypertension and diabetes predating a sum insured enhancement. The Ombudsman found no evidence of non-disclosure or pre-existence at enhancement, directing the insurer to pay the balance of Rs. 84,063.

Complainant's father underwent CABG surgery. The insurer repudiated the claim alleging suppression of hypertension in the proposal form. Medical records showed conflicting durations of hypertension which did not pre-date the policy inception. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and directed the insurer to pay Rs. 1,15,523.

Insurer repudiated a claim for Rs. 16,274 citing a 15-day break in policy renewal created a fresh policy subject to initial waiting periods. The Ombudsman noted the insurer could not prove a fresh proposal was submitted and the renewal traced back to the original 2002 proposal, allowing the claim.

Complainant underwent thyroid surgery following a policy renewal break. The insurer rejected the claim as a pre-existing condition. Expert medical opinion confirmed the condition likely existed for a long duration. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant's father was hospitalized for giddiness and hearing loss, but records showed only investigations were performed by shifting between centers without actual inpatient treatment. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection since hospitalization was unnecessary and could be handled on an OPD basis.

Insurer repudiated a claim of Rs. 1,882.02 for vertigo treatment on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary. The Ombudsman noted the insurer dealt with the case casually despite the insured being admitted on a doctor's advice, and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Insurer rejected a mediclaim for breast cancer surgery due to non-submission of pre-treatment prescriptions prior to a specific date, following a minor policy renewal gap. The Ombudsman held that rejecting the claim on mere absence of prior prescriptions was unacceptable and ordered settlement with interest.

Complainant sought removal of specific policy endorsements excluding cataract and urinary tract infections upon renewal. The insurer maintained these were special exclusions agreed upon at inception. The Ombudsman held that insurers have the right to specifically exclude conditions outside standard clause 4.3, dismissing the petition.

TPA rejected a claim for acute abdominal pain treatment (esophageal candidiasis) arguing hospitalization was solely for investigation. The Ombudsman found the patient was admitted under serious pre-conditions on medical advice, setting aside the rejection and ordering payment of Rs. 18,303.

Insurer partially settled a bypass surgery claim, cutting Rs. 40,934 on the ground that a sum insured enhancement was made when hypertension was pre-existing. Text cuts off during the decision analysis.

Insurer repudiated a claim for bronchoscopy and lung treatment citing pre-existing rheumatic heart disease. The Ombudsman found no evidence that tests for lung disease were connected to the heart condition, and directed the insurer to pay Rs. 15,987.

Insurer imposed a restriction upon sum insured enhancement stating the increased portion was excluded for the first year. The Ombudsman held that the restriction was imposed without proposer's consent while accepting full premium, and ordered the insurer to withdraw the restriction and provide full coverage.

Insurer repudiated a cataract surgery claim because the policy was renewed late by 41 days due to a bounced cheque, treating it as a first-year policy. The Ombudsman noted technical correctness of the insurer but awarded an ex-gratia payment of Rs. 8,000 considering the unintentional lapse.

Insurer repudiated a claim for thyroid cancer treatment citing pre-existing disease based on panel doctor opinion. The Ombudsman noted the insurer failed to provide proof of pre-existence, directing them to settle the claim.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer repudiated a bypass surgery claim for Rs. 1,84,504.75 citing pre-existing diabetes, hypertension, and smoking-related cardiac issues under a first-year policy. Text cuts off during the analysis of conflicting medical reports.

Complainant contested ongoing policy exclusions for heart disease and hysterectomy based on a pre-inception ECG report. The Ombudsman declined to interfere with the current expiring policy terms, noting underwriting risk assessment is the insurer's prerogative, but advised seeking specialist opinion for future renewals.

Insurer repudiated a hysterectomy claim because a 60-day renewal gap treated the policy as fresh, invoking pre-existing disease and first-year exclusion clauses. The Ombudsman found no past history of the uterine condition and awarded an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 80,000.

Insurer repudiated a claim for cerebellar degeneration by linking it to a 1996 spine surgery for disc prolapse. The Ombudsman held that the conditions were unrelated and ordered the insurer to settle the claim for Rs. 39,995.10 and restore cumulative bonus.

Insurer rejected a prostate surgery claim because the insured failed to disclose a major prostate surgery performed in 1987 in the initial proposal form. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection as non-disclosure of a major surgery deprived the insurer of underwriting the risk.

Complainant claimed for hospitalisation of his mother who suffered from nephropathy, hypertension, and diabetes. Insurer repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing diabetes. The Ombudsman noted the insurance company was aware of prior disclosures and the attending physician confirmed the disease arose after policy inception. The award text was truncated.

Complainant alleged non-receipt of insurance policies and premium receipts after paying renewal premiums. Insurer stated the complainant was an agent and barred from paying self-insurance under Section 41 of the Insurance Act to avoid commission rebates. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as non-maintainable under RPG Rules, ordering the return of uncashed cheques.

Complainant sought reimbursement for treatment of enlarged prostate and osteoarthritis. Insurer repudiated on the ground of pre-existing disease, claiming a three-day gap made the policy fresh. The Ombudsman observed the policy ran continuously from 1999 and the insurer failed to prove pre-existence or insured's knowledge.

Complainant's wife underwent surgery for a ruptured aneurysm. Insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing, linking it to prior hypertension and diabetes. The attending surgeon clarified the emergency had no relation to hypertension. The Ombudsman noted conflicting medical opinions and lack of proof regarding insured's prior knowledge.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought reimbursement for coronary artery disease and heart block treatments. Insurer repudiated subsequent claims as pre-existing based on medical history dating back to 1969. The Ombudsman reviewed discharge summaries and past settlements, noting previous approvals for similar cardiac treatments.

Complainant's wife was treated for gastric erosion. Insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing based on hospital records showing a history of symptoms for 2 to 3 years and recurrent vomiting. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as it was supported by hospital documentation.

Complainant's mother underwent pelvic floor repair. Insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing based solely on the TPA medical officer's opinion without hospital records or evidence of prior knowledge. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and ordered full payment of Rs. 26,790.85.

Complainant was hospitalised for abdominal pain and underwent extensive diagnostic tests without receiving medication during confinement. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.10, stating admission was solely for investigation. The Ombudsman upheld the dismissal.

Complainant's deceased wife was covered under a bank group policy (which waived pre-existing clauses) and an individual policy. After exhausting the group policy limits, the complainant sought the balance under the individual policy. Insurer denied cashless and rejected the claim due to pre-existing conditions applicable under the individual policy. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stance.

Complainant was hospitalised for abdominal pain and obstruction caused by adhesions from a prior hysterectomy and chocolate cyst operation done in 2003. Insurer repudiated the claim for non-disclosure of past illness and surgery in the proposal form. The Ombudsman noted the non-disclosure of material facts.

Complainant filed for pre and post-hospitalisation expenses nearly three years after the actual hospitalisation and subsequent to an Ombudsman award for the main claim. The insurer repudiated due to delayed submission. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint citing unreasonable delay and finality of the previous award.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant stayed in a diagnostic centre for 23 hours and 10 minutes for tests and investigations. Insurer repudiated the claim under clause 2.3 (hospitalisation under 24 hours). The Ombudsman observed that the admission was solely for diagnostic tests and upheld the repudiation under clause 4.10.

Complainant sought reimbursement for chest pain hospitalisation. Insurer delayed and sought details of a 1994 hospitalisation for oesophagitis. Due to lack of forum infrastructure to determine if current ailment linked to past history, the Ombudsman directed the insurer to appoint an independent specialist doctor.

Complainant faced a six-month delay in settling a post-hospitalisation claim for accidental injury because the TPA failed to collect documents from the hospital. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim of Rs. 9,454 with interest.

Complainant underwent cataract surgery at a clinic's partner hospital but submitted a receipt from the intermediary clinic rather than the operating doctor or hospital. Insurer partially paid the claim, demanding a valid receipt. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's requirement for a proper receipt.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought cashless facility for gall stone surgery within six months of policy inception. TPA denied cashless based on panel doctor opinion that multiple calculi could not develop within six months. The Ombudsman noted cashless denial is outside RPG Rules scope if the underlying claim is not established and disposed of the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was admitted for chest pain, underwent tests which revealed non-cardiac musculoskeletal pain, and was discharged without active treatment or diagnosis. Insurer repudiated under clause 4.10. The Ombudsman confirmed the repudiation as hospitalisation was solely for investigation.

Complainant was hospitalised for generalised body ache and joint pain, underwent numerous normal blood and diagnostic tests, and was treated conservatively. Insurer repudiated under clause 4.10 for hospitalisation primarily for investigation. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Complainant sought reimbursement for heart and kidney ailment after sum insured was enhanced from Rs. 30,000 to Rs. 1,50,000. Insurer partially paid, applying pre-existing exclusion to the incremental sum insured. The Ombudsman held that since the insurer did not explicitly exclude known pre-existing conditions at the time of enhancement, partial repudiation was unjustified and ordered full payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife underwent knee injection treatments across three separate admissions lasting less than 24 hours each. Insurer repudiated the claims under clause 2.3 for hospitalisation under 24 hours. The Ombudsman discussed the policy terms and restrictions on relaxing the 24-hour limit for chronic conditions.
A claim for pelvic adhesions was repudiated by the insurer on the grounds that it was related to an excluded appendix condition. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Cashless treatment was denied for neck and back pain hospitalization because admission was primarily for investigation and evaluation of a suspected disease, attracting policy exclusions. The complaint was disposed of.

A claim for Hepatitis B treatment within four months of policy inception was repudiated as pre-existing chronic liver disease. The Ombudsman found no conclusive medical evidence of pre-existence and ordered the insurer to pay the full claim.

A hospitalization claim for an Ovarian Cyst was repudiated because the patient was treated for primary infertility, an excluded peril. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to obtain an independent expert opinion to determine if the treatment was connected to infertility.

A gall bladder surgery claim was repudiated due to delayed intimation and claim submission exceeding policy timeframes. The Ombudsman confirmed the repudiation as no reasonable cause for delay was established.

A claim involving malaria, diabetes, and renal failure was repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to obtain an independent specialist report regarding the duration of the ailments.

A liver disease claim under a renewed policy was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing chronic liver disease following a brief four-day renewal gap. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation, holding that the insurer failed to prove pre-existence.

A claim for sleep apnea treatment at Vellore remained unsettled as required hospitalization documents were not furnished. The Ombudsman requested the insured to cooperate and submit documents for claim processing.
An oral cancer claim was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing disease based on dental prescriptions indicating symptoms for years prior to policy inception.

A heart disease hospitalization claim was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing diabetes. The Ombudsman noted that past illness details were declared in representations and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

A stroke (CVA) claim was repudiated for non-disclosure of long-standing hypertension. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to appoint an independent specialist doctor to determine if the disease was pre-existing.

A hospitalization claim for prostate enlargement was repudiated on the grounds that prostatomegaly existed for three years prior to policy inception. The Ombudsman held that mere enlargement without cancer knowledge does not constitute a pre-existing disease.

An eye surgery claim for excessive conjunctival folds was repudiated under clause 4.8 as a congenital external anomaly. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to refer the matter to an independent specialist to determine if it was a congenital anomaly.

An acute appendicitis claim was repudiated under clause 4.1, alleging pain began before the policy waiting threshold. The Ombudsman found technical miscalculations by the insurer and ordered the claim to be paid.

An incisional hernia claim following a prior gall bladder surgery was repudiated as pre-existing. The Ombudsman ruled that the insurer failed to prove when the hernia actually occurred and directed full payment.

Cashless treatment for brain hemorrhage was initially partially approved then denied on pre-existing grounds. The Ombudsman noted lack of full documents and advised the complainant to file a formal reimbursement claim.
A tractor insurance claim estimate was heavily cut by the insurer based on policy endorsements. The Ombudsman awarded the computed liability amount in full settlement.

A claim for Myasthenia Gravis treatment was repudiated as a pre-existing disease. An independent neurosurgeon could not confirm pre-existence prior to the policy date, so the Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and ordered processing.
A claim for diabetes complications was repudiated as pre-existing. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

A hospitalisation claim for laparoscopic drainage of a chocolate cyst was repudiated under clause 4.8 because the initial medical visit involved infertility. The Ombudsman held that cyst removal is a valid surgical intervention and allowed the claim while disallowing pre-admission expenses.

Insured hospitalized for Acute Coronary Syndrome. Insurer rejected claim under pre-existing disease citing long-standing hypertension based on LVH. Ombudsman noted absence of corroborative medical records proving prior hypertension and ruled in favor of complainant.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured hospitalized for chest pain. Insurer repudiated claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary and purely for diagnostic tests. Ombudsman found no critical emergency or active treatment warranting confinement, upholding the insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for abdominal pain and vomiting, treated with oral medications, and discharged on request. Insurer rejected the claim stating hospitalization was not necessary for the treatment. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stand.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for uterine fibroid surgery was partially restricted by insurer citing that increased sum insured was subject to waiting periods and specific exclusions for hysterectomy. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's limitation to the original sum insured plus cumulative bonus.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for mastectomy due to breast lump was repudiated for non-disclosure of a colon cancer surgery done in 1990. Ombudsman noted insurer failed to produce the original proposal form and evidence of non-disclosure, setting aside the repudiation.

Insurer partially settled a hysterectomy claim by deducting surgeon and anesthetist fees as excessive compared to standard hospital tariffs. Ombudsman reviewed rate charts and upheld deductions for non-payable/unreasonable charges.

Claim for total knee replacement due to osteoarthritis was partially rejected as pre-existing under an enhanced sum insured policy. Ombudsman observed progressive degenerative changes and upheld the insurer's decision to restrict the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for left MI stenosis and stenting was repudiated for pre-existing Parkinson's disease and non-disclosure. Ombudsman reviewed hospital records and expert opinion confirming prior medical history, upholding the rejection.

Claim for anemia due to gastric ulcers following a fall was rejected because hospitalization was primarily for diagnostic tests. Ombudsman granted 50% of expenses on an ex-gratia basis acknowledging the accidental fall origin.

Insurer partially settled a viral hepatitis hospitalization claim after trimming prolonged hospital stay and high doctor visiting fees. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's cuts based on reasonable and necessary expense principles.

Claim for pulmonary embolism was repudiated due to pre-existing deep vein thrombosis and diabetes. Ombudsman found direct medical linkage between prior vascular issues and the current event, upholding the insurer's rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for excision of an infected in-growing toe nail under local anesthesia with hospital admission was rejected for lack of necessity. Ombudsman agreed that the procedure could have been managed on an OPD basis.

Claim for myocardial infarction with diabetes was repudiated for non-disclosure of long-standing diabetes and pre-existing heart disease. Ombudsman examined policy history and upheld the insurer's repudiation.

Claim for hepatitis B and hepatocellular carcinoma following a kidney transplant 25 years prior was repudiated for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection due to concealment of the transplant and chronic illness.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for breast abscess treatment was rejected because records proved treatment was taken on an OPD basis without 24 hours hospitalization, and potentially related to maternity exclusions. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim for laparoscopic hysterectomy due to uterine fibroids was repudiated for pre-existing menorrhagia based on past medical history notes. Ombudsman ruled that symptoms do not prove pre-existing disease, setting aside the rejection and allowing the claim.

Claim for UTI and antral gastritis was repudiated under exclusion clause for alcoholism after medical reports noted alcohol consumption and fatty liver. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stand linking gastritis to alcohol and dietary habits.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured contested partial settlement of post-hospitalization expenses, specifically the disallowance of private nursing charges at home. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision to disallow private nursing since hospital facility was adequate and dressings did not require special nursing.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for intestinal obstruction and CVA hemiplegia was repudiated for pre-existing conditions. Ombudsman noted the patient suffered from multiple pre-existing bedridden ailments causing complications, upholding the insurer's decision.

Claim for acute anterior wall myocardial infarction with stenting was rejected on the grounds of pre-existing IHD from 30 years prior. Ombudsman found no proof of continuous treatment or positive existence of IHD, setting aside the repudiation.
Insured was hospitalized for ventral hernia and intestinal obstruction. Claim was rejected under pre-existing disease and non-disclosure clauses due to a major road accident in 1993.
Insured was hospitalized for ITP (bleeding disorder). Insurer rejected claim as pre-existing due to heavy menstrual bleeding history. Ombudsman granted 50 percent of admissible expenses.
Insured was hospitalized for abdominal pain and investigations. Claim was rejected because hospitalisation was for investigation only and treatment was oral medication.
Insured's mother was hospitalized for uterine prolapse and underwent vaginal hysterectomy. Claim rejected under pre-existing disease clause. Ombudsman allowed 50 percent of admissible expenses.

Insured underwent total laparoscopic hysterectomy. TPA made deductions from surgeon, anesthetist, and assistant charges as well as missing report bills. Ombudsman upheld reasonable and customary cuts.
Insured was hospitalized for 35 days for sciatica low back pain. Claim was rejected as treatment involved oil massage and oral drugs which did not warrant hospitalization.
Insured's wife was operated for incisional hernia. Claim was rejected linking it to a caesarean section done 27 years ago. Ombudsman allowed 85 percent of admissible expenses.
Insured was hospitalized for vaginal bleeding and uterine fibroid. Claim was rejected as admission was for investigations and known condition without emergency.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's father was hospitalized for acute myocardial infarction and LVF. Claim was rejected because the policy had a specific exclusion for diabetes and its consequences.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for disc prolapse. TPA disallowed high surgeon fees. Ombudsman directed payment of the full surgeon fee of Rs. 2.50 lacs as declared in pre-authorization.

Insured's claim for lupus nephritis was rejected as pre-existing due to a short policy break caused by a bounced renewal cheque. Ombudsman restored continuity from the original inception date in 1997.

Insured claimed for coronary artery disease treatment. Claim was rejected under pre-existing clause citing 6-7 years of hypertension. Ombudsman allowed the claim as hypertension prior to policy inception was unproven.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was hospitalized twice for Koch's dorsal spine. First claim had stay days curtailed; second claim was rejected for lack of necessity. Ombudsman allowed full first claim and 50 percent ex-gratia for second hospitalization.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for Hepatitis C infection. Claim was repudiated for non-disclosure of a past road accident and blood transfusion in 1989. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for liver failure. Post-hospitalization claim was partially disallowed for family physician home visits. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent angiography for chest pain. Claim was rejected under clause 4.10 and internal circulars disallowing repeat angiography without intervention. Ombudsman set aside internal rules and allowed the claim.

Insured hospitalized for heart ailments and renal angioplasty. Claim rejected due to pre-existing hypertension and heart disease. Ombudsman allowed 50 percent of admissible expenses due to inconsistent medical history records.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's son was hospitalized for allergic rhinitis and asthma. Claim was rejected under pre-existing disease clause based on history of recurrent symptoms for years prior to policy inception.
Insured's claims for dialysis and angioplasty were rejected. Hospital records and post-policy tests indicated pre-existing diabetes dating back many years. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured was hospitalized for unstable angina, diabetes, hypertension, and dengue. Claim was rejected due to pre-existing diabetes. Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia payment of Rs. 25,000 considering age, dengue, and financial condition.

A claim for day-care dental surgery and 6 hours of hospitalization was rejected by the insurer under exclusion clauses and condition 2.3. The forum upheld the repudiation as the discharge summary noted only pain and pericoronitis without complications justifying hospitalization.

The insurer repudiated a mediclaim on the grounds that hospitalization was not justified, relying on a medical referee. The ombudsman set aside the decision since the hospitalization followed actual examination by a qualified specialist, and directed full payment.

Insured was hospitalised for Koch's Spine with abscess, Rheumatic Fever and lung Fibrosis just three months after policy inception. Clinical history showed past history of tuberculosis, rheumatic heart disease, and lung disease, establishing a pre-existing nexus. Repudiation upheld.

The insurer rejected a claim for piles treated by K.S. Application because the treating physician held an M.D. in Ayurveda. The ombudsman noted the procedure is standard and the hospital was duly registered, directing full payment.

Partial settlement involved deductions for assisting doctor's charges and chemist bills lacking patient name. The ombudsman found full payment was made by cheque and chemist bill omissions are common, ordering the insurer to pay the deducted balance of 13933 rupees.

Reimbursement for oral chemotherapy drugs taken at home for breast cancer was denied because bills exceeded 60 days post-discharge. The ombudsman ruled that technical progress allowing oral administration certified by an oncologist should not be mechanically excluded, ordering full payment.

Claim for breast abscess surgery 1.5 months after childbirth was repudiated under the policy exclusion for treatments traceable to childbirth. The ombudsman upheld the rejection as the abscess was a post-delivery lactation infection.

Claim for coronary artery double vessel disease was rejected on pre-existing grounds. Since treating doctor and discharge notes certified no past history of hypertension or diabetes, and records showed no prior indication of disease, the insurer was directed to pay full claim.

Claim was settled after deductions for missing bills, doctor home visit charges, and post-hospitalisation medicines. The ombudsman upheld the deductions as justified requirements to determine payable amounts.

Insurer rejected a dental dislocation claim after an accident, classifying it as dental treatment. The ombudsman held that injuries caused by an accident should be covered and ordered full settlement.
Hospitalization for prolapsed IV disc with DVT was repudiated due to pre-existing spine degeneration shown in old X-rays and non-disclosure in proposal. Repudiation upheld.

Claim for oral targeted therapy for lung cancer was denied due to lack of hospitalization. The ombudsman noted medical advancements make hospital stays unnecessary for such therapy, and ruled hospitalization alone cannot deny reimbursement.
Retinal detachment claim was rejected because previous cataract surgery and high myopia pre-dated the policy and were not disclosed in the proposal form. Repudiation upheld.

Claim was repudiated because indoor case papers were not submitted, though the hospital uncooperatively withheld them despite insured's efforts. The ombudsman set aside repudiation and ordered full payment.
Claim was repudiated due to misstatement of coverage details in a proposal for enhanced sum insured. Complainant admitted the misstatement during hearing, leading to dismissal.
Piles treatment via Ayurvedic K.S. Application was rejected because the doctor held an M.D. in Ayurveda. The ombudsman ruled the treatment valid and directed full claim payment.

Heart disease treatment claim was rejected because hospital records showed a 6-month history of chest pain and blood pressure prior to treatment, falling within a 2-year policy exclusion for hypertension. Repudiation upheld.

Death due to septicaemia, diabetes, and renal failure following foot blisters from hot terrace floors was repudiated. Records showed 15-year history of diabetes causing diabetic neuropathy leading to blisters, preceding policy inception. Repudiation upheld.
Laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery for morbid obesity was rejected as cosmetic surgery. The ombudsman noted obesity is recognized as a disease by the WHO, directing full claim payment.

Hospitalization for liver cirrhosis and portal hypertension was repudiated because medical history showed prior blood vomiting and sclerotherapy before policy inception, establishing pre-existing disease and non-disclosure. Repudiation upheld.
Insurer deducted Rs. 7,450 for OT procedure, nursing charges, miscellaneous, and registration fees. The ombudsman directed payment of Rs. 5,700.

Claim for varicose vein treatment via sclerotherapy was repudiated stating hospitalisation was not necessary. The ombudsman noted sclerotherapy is a recognised procedure performed in hospital, setting aside the rejection.
Insurer deducted charges for special room stay, nursing, and miscellaneous items. The ombudsman ordered payment of Rs. 4,950 out of Rs. 4,966 deducted.

Piles treatment using K.S. Application performed by an Ayurvedic MD was rejected because the doctor was not qualified in Allopathy. The ombudsman ruled that the procedure is recognized and directed full payment.
Piles treatment using K.S. Application by an Ayurvedic doctor was rejected over medical practitioner definitions. The ombudsman ordered full payment.
Piles treatment using K.S. Application by an Ayurvedic doctor was rejected over medical practitioner definitions. The ombudsman ordered full payment.
Hysterectomy claim repudiated under first-year policy exclusion for planned surgery. Since the doctor noted the condition was acute and noticed earlier, full claim payment was ordered.
Cataract claim in the first policy year was repudiated. Records showed the cataract resulted from an eye injury three months prior, making the exclusion inapplicable, so full payment was ordered.
Piles treatment using K.S. Application by an Ayurvedic practitioner was rejected. The ombudsman set aside the rejection and ordered full payment.
Piles treatment using K.S. Application by an Ayurvedic practitioner was rejected. The ombudsman set aside the rejection and ordered full payment.
Gynaecomastia surgery was repudiated as cosmetic treatment. The ombudsman noted it was actual treatment for an illness and ordered full payment.
Claim repudiated due to missing hospital admission records. Exhaustive treatment documents submitted during the hearing invalidated the grounds for rejection, and full payment was ordered.
Hospitalisation for SLE with ITP and AIHA was repudiated because records showed pre-existing onset since 2002 and non-disclosure in the proposal form. The insurer's decision was upheld.
Re-implantation of ureter for left VU-reflux commenced in the first policy year. Medical reports confirmed the condition was an internal congenital disease, so the repudiation was upheld.
Laparoscopic gastric bypass for morbid obesity was rejected as cosmetic surgery without expert opinion. The WHO recognises obesity as a disease, so full claim payment was ordered.

Treatment for rare orthopaedic disease Perthes involved conflicting technical expert opinions. As the forum lacked capacity to resolve deep technical debates, the complainant was advised to approach a court.

Claim for trauma admission was rejected as treatable on an OPD basis. Since the insured's brother's claim for injuries from the same accident was honoured, denying this claim offended equity, and full payment was ordered.
Piles treatment using K.S. Application by an Ayurvedic practitioner was rejected over medical practitioner qualifications. Full payment was ordered.
Insurer deducted 15% hospital service charges for small bowel treatment. As similar charges were allowed for the insured's spouse in another case, the insurer was directed to pay the deducted amount.
Claim was repudiated for lack of documents regarding the onset date of diabetes. The ombudsman noted the insured can only provide documents in possession and ordered full claim payment.

Insured was hospitalized for Disc Lesion C5-L1. Treatment papers noted an operation for P.I.D. L5-S1 four years prior, while the policy was only active for two years. This established a pre-existing disease and non-disclosure in the proposal form, leading to claim repudiation.

Insured underwent Hysterectomy in the second policy year. The claim was repudiated under policy conditions excluding Hysterectomy in the first two years. The complainant argued previous coverage with another insurer as transfer of mediclaim, but the policy had no such provision.

Insured was hospitalized for a vehicular accident and transported by air ambulance. The insurer disallowed air fare, ambulance charges, and late medicine purchases. The ombudsman allowed medicines purchased slightly late since the insured was fit much later, and the cost of a knee brace, ordering a partial payment.

A mediclaim settlement faced a delay of five and a half months due to discrepancy letters and processing time. The ombudsman directed the insurer to pay simple interest at 8 percent per annum for the 130 days of delay beyond the reasonable processing time.

Insured underwent treatment for a dog bite and submitted bills later. The insurer repudiated the claim for late filing beyond 30 days. The ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the claim as the delay by the rural illiterate woman was not deliberate.

Insured was hospitalized for fever and submitted bills past the 30-day stipulated period. The insurer repudiated the claim based on policy conditions. The ombudsman ruled that the disease was not excluded and ordered full payment as the delay did not absolve liability.

Insured underwent a hernia operation along with a voluntary vasectomy. The insurer deducted the vasectomy amount and settled partially. The ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the balance after deducting only surgeon charges for the vasectomy, noting arbitrary deductions.

Insured's spouse was treated for an ovarian cyst within three months of policy commencement. The insurer repudiated the claim claiming pre-existing disease based on cyst size. The ombudsman directed payment as the insurer failed to produce medical opinion supporting pre-existence.

Insured met with a road accident involving dogs, sustained knee injuries, and was hospitalized. The insurer repudiated the claim citing discrepancies in the cause of accident between the station diary and claim form, and delayed police intimation. The ombudsman ordered settlement as the accident was genuine.

Following an accident, the TPA disallowed part of the claim due to non-submission of test reports and instrument charges. The ombudsman directed payment of the disallowed amount since reports were retained by the hospital and only minor deductions lacked names on bills.

Insured suffered back pain after a fall, leading to hospitalization and physiotherapy for disk problems. The TPA rejected the claim arguing hospitalization was unnecessary and for investigations only. The ombudsman ruled in favor of the insured due to immobility and ordered payment with interest.

Insured underwent PTCA for single vessel disease. The claim was rejected on grounds of pre-existing hypertension and smoking history. The ombudsman noted no evidence proved hypertension existed before the policy and smoking is not a pre-existing disease, ordering claim payment.

Insured underwent sudden kidney removal surgery. Cashless facility was denied for pre-existing disease, and the claim was treated as no-claim due to non-submission of bills. The ombudsman held the cashless denial unjustified and ordered payment with interest upon document submission.

Insured underwent specialized radiotherapy for knees and shoulder mobility. The insurer rejected the claim arguing late intimation, no hospitalization requirement for osteoarthritis, and chronic nature. The ombudsman held that special machinery required hospitalization, ordering payment minus minor pre-hospitalization test deductions.

Insured underwent surgery for sinusitis during the third policy year. The insurer repudiated the claim citing a 5-day policy renewal break, non-qualifying hospital bed strength, and lack of hospitalization need. The ombudsman ruled that grace periods apply, hospital supervision sufficed, and doctors decide hospitalization.

Insured was treated for chronic ischaemic heart disease. The TPA repudiated the claim citing pre-existing disease due to a 4-day policy renewal break in 2002. The ombudsman noted standard grace periods apply and ordered payment of the admissible claim.

Insured was treated for fibroid uterus. The claim was repudiated on pre-existing grounds because discharge summaries mentioned suffering for 1.5 years, aligning with a brief policy revival gap. The ombudsman gave the benefit of doubt to the insured as no prior treatment records existed.

Insured's daughter was hospitalized for treatment. The TPA rejected the claim alleging the hospital did not meet policy criteria. The ombudsman found the hospital was duly registered and 15-bedded, ordering full payment.

Insured was admitted to emergency for urinary retention. The TPA repudiated the claim treating it as an OPD case due to lack of a formal ward discharge summary. The ombudsman verified emergency hospitalization documents and ordered claim payment.

Insured was hospitalized for rheumatic heart disease. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing rheumatic fever without proposal form disclosures or prior hospital records. The ombudsman ordered claim payment and directed cashless facility provision for future treatments.

Insured suffered head injury from a fall in the bathroom and underwent brain surgery within 30 days of policy inception. Insurer rejected the claim under waiting period clause. Ombudsman held that the medical opinion was general and the injury resulted from an accidental fall, ordering claim payment.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for sudden convulsions for less than 24 hours after five years of continuous policy coverage. Insurer rejected the claim under the 24-hour hospitalization rule. Ombudsman noted delay in repudiation and technological exceptions, ordering payment.

Insured underwent coronary angiography and was diagnosed with CAD four years after policy inception. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman held that angiography was unrelated to pre-existing hypertension and ordered claim settlement.

Insured was hospitalized for pleural effusion and fever. Insurer rejected the claim on grounds of non-disclosure of congenital epilepsy and hypertension in the proposal form. Ombudsman upheld the rejection due to material non-disclosure rendering the policy void.

Insured underwent surgery for Cholelithiasis after one year of policy coverage. Insurer rejected the claim alleging pre-existing gall bladder disease based on panel doctor opinion. Ombudsman held that pre-existence was not proven by treating doctors and ordered claim payment.

Insured underwent open heart surgery after four years of policy coverage. Insurer rejected the claim citing non-disclosure of diabetes based on an incomplete proposal form and hospital discharge summary. Ombudsman held insurer failed to prove pre-existence and ordered payment.

Insured was hospitalized for prolapsed disc and managed conservatively. Insurer rejected the claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary for evaluation. Ombudsman held that treatment decisions rest with the treating doctor and ordered payment.

Insured's daughter underwent surgery for a tibia deformity resulting from a prior road accident covered by the same insurer. Insurer rejected the claim citing a brief policy break and pre-existing exclusion. Ombudsman held proper exclusion procedures were not followed and ordered payment.

Insured's wife suffered a wrist fracture and received outpatient orthopedic treatment without hospitalization. Insurer rejected the claim as no hospitalization took place. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Insured was hospitalized for ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and renal failure. Insurer rejected the claim due to non-disclosure of pre-existing renal problems dating back to 2001 when shifting policies. Ombudsman confirmed prior existence and dismissed the complaint.

Insured's mother was hospitalized for bronchial asthma and acute exacerbation. Insurer rejected the claim as management of a pre-existing COPD condition of 15 years. Ombudsman found active treatment was for asthma and dismissed the complaint.

Insured was hospitalized for chest pain, systemic hypertension, and coronary artery disease. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing hypertension and heart disease dating back to 1987. Ombudsman upheld the rejection based on medical records and dismissed the complaint.

Insured submitted hospitalization claim documents seven months after discharge instead of the stipulated 30-day period. Insurer rejected the claim for late submission without extraordinary circumstances. Ombudsman upheld the rejection and dismissed the complaint.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for strangulated vertical hernia. Insurer rejected the claim citing a prior cholecystectomy done 20 years ago as a pre-existing condition. Ombudsman held that the hernia was a new development and ordered claim settlement.

Insured's wife underwent kidney transplantation for chronic renal failure. Insurer rejected the claim under pre-existing disease exclusion based on medical records showing two years of prior treatment. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Insured was hospitalized for cardiac observation following sweating and discomfort. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and CAD dating back to 2000. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as prior CAD was established.

Insured claimed hospitalization expenses after a road accident. Insurer offered a reduced settlement alleging excessive hospital charges and missing discharge summaries. Ombudsman ordered partial payment of Rs. 23,800 after disallowing unsupported amounts.

Insured's daughter underwent surgery for microtia (congenital ear condition) in the second year of a Good Health policy. Insurer rejected the claim as a congenital pre-existing condition. Ombudsman allowed the claim as continuous prior service coverage waived pre-existing exclusions.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for menstruation problems and skin rashes, undergoing routine blood and ultrasound investigations. Insurer rejected the claim as hospitalization was unnecessary for outpatient-level tests. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Insured underwent angioplasty and bypass surgery across two policies. Insurer rejected claims citing pre-existing diabetes and 30-day waiting period. Ombudsman held insurer failed to prove non-disclosure during telemarketing and ordered settlement of two specific claims while dismissing a third.

Insured claimed for wife's hospitalization after enhancing sum insured. Insurer paid partially based on previous sum insured due to a policy condition. Ombudsman allowed the complaint on ex-gratia basis for a specific additional amount.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for post cricoids growth following a 21-day policy renewal break. Insurer rejected the claim as a pre-existing disease. Ombudsman found no medical records proving manifestation prior to policy inception and allowed the complaint.

Claim for hernia surgery was rejected on grounds of pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of previous childbirth surgeries. Ombudsman noted that scars were pre-existing, not hernia, and childbirth is not an illness. Complaint allowed.

insurer: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Bypass surgery claim was rejected for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of diabetes. Ombudsman noted lack of proof that heart ailment existed prior to policy inception, but noted failure to disclose diabetes, and allowed an ex-gratia amount.
Claim for laser eye surgery for high myopia was rejected as pre-existing based on high refractive error. Complainant failed to furnish requested clarification. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for uterine and PCO treatment at an infertility center was rejected under exclusions for sterility and pre-existing conditions. Complainant failed to establish treatment was unrelated to infertility. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for ischemic heart disease and renal failure was rejected due to non-disclosure of pre-existing renal problems dating back to 2001 after a policy break. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for spinal disc prolapse following a fall was rejected as pre-existing based on medical opinions and MRI reports showing chronic changes. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for fibroid uterus hospitalization was rejected as pre-existing following a 4-day policy renewal break. Ombudsman observed continuous coverage since 2000 and ruled the condition was not pre-existing. Complaint allowed.

Claim for son's circumcision due to phimosis was rejected as a congenital external disorder exclusion. Ombudsman found the condition was acquired recently due to infection and was payable. Complaint allowed with interest.

Claim for vocal cord polyp treatment was rejected under pre-existing clause. As the insurer's panel doctor and branch office favored a review, the Ombudsman remanded the matter back to the insurer for a final decision.

Claim for treatment of diabetes, hypertension, and COPD was withheld. Ombudsman noted diabetes was disclosed in the proposal form and there was no concealment. Complaint allowed subject to document production.

Hospitalization claim was paid, but critical illness benefit for a first heart attack was denied because enzyme levels were within normal range, failing policy criteria. Complaint closed as benefits were fully rendered.
Balance medical claim was treated as no claim due to non-submission of documents requested by TPA. Ombudsman directed the insured to submit documents and the insurer to settle the admissible amount.
Claim for cholecystitis treatment was rejected as pre-existing without supporting evidence of prior consultation or knowledge. Ombudsman allowed the complaint subject to document verification.

Claim for vagina plasty following previous fibroid surgery was rejected as a pre-existing related condition without expert medical opinion. Ombudsman ordered an expert medical board to examine the issue.

Claim for pancreatitis and gastritis was rejected as a chronic pre-existing disease. Ombudsman noted lack of evidence of prior knowledge and directed the insurer to review the claim with a medical board or make reimbursement.
Claim for carcinoma treatment was rejected as pre-existing due to close proximity between policy inception and disease onset, along with prior outpatient records. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for hernia surgery was rejected because the insured failed to disclose a previous hysterectomy in proposal forms despite policy breaks. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation due to non-disclosure of material facts.

Pre-hospitalization claim was rejected because the parent hospitalization claim was rejected for non-declaration of diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman directed the insurer to collect files from TPA and record final findings.

The insurer rejected a mediclaim arguing hospitalization was under 24 hours and medicine bills were excessive. The Ombudsman noted hospitalization met the 24-hour criteria based on hospital records, but permitted the insurer to conduct a detailed medical investigation into the cash memos.

An insured under a Group Critical Illness policy underwent CABG. The claim was rejected because he had a 5-year history of hypertension prior to policy inception. The insured failed to provide contradicting consultation papers, upholding the pre-existing condition exclusion.

A claim for emergency hospitalization was rejected on grounds of pre-existing degenerative disease. Independent neurological opinion indicated the condition could remain asymptomatic for years, and insurers failed to provide documentary proof of pre-existence at policy inception. Complaint allowed.

Part of a medical claim was disallowed because the policy was renewed with a 12-day gap, and the patient had long-standing diabetes mellitus and hypertension existing prior to the commencement of the fresh policy term.

Reimbursement was denied due to pre-existing cardiac problems when the policy first incepted, treated as concurrent rather than continuous. During proceedings, the insurer settled the claim as a sympathetic gesture, and the Ombudsman ordered interest for delayed payment.

An insured disputed the removal of cumulative bonus upon renewal following a policy modification. The insurer explained revised terms were applied and additional coverage was given. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint regarding bonus deletion while noting communication gaps.

An Accident Relief Care policy claim was partially cut due to diabetes treatment during hospital stay and room rent/doctor fee caps. Ombudsman held that rates were not handed over to the insured and treatment was interconnected, ordering the balance payment.
A heart ailment claim was rejected because the disease existed prior to the earliest date of continuous insurance without a break, and the policy had a significant renewal gap.

A claim for hernia surgery was rejected as a first-year exclusion because the policy was renewed with a 7-day gap, constituting a fresh contract. The insured failed to provide convincing reasons for the renewal delay.

A claim for shoulder dislocation treatment was rejected on grounds of unclear loss cause and defective cash receipts. The Ombudsman found the hospital breakdown authentic and investigator report favorable, directing the insurer to settle.

A prostate surgery claim was rejected due to an 87-day renewal gap caused by overseas travel. The Ombudsman ruled that the unutilized period under the Indian policy while holding an overseas travel policy should be properly adjusted to maintain continuity.

Bladder Neck Obstruction claim was rejected as first year exclusion due to prostate issues. Ombudsman noted continuity of insurance was established since 2003, making the first-year exclusion inapplicable, and directed settlement upon document submission.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Outpatient treatment claim was rejected and the policy was wrongfully cancelled by the insurer. The Ombudsman ordered a refund of excess premium collected post-cancellation and awarded compensation for misleading the insured regarding outpatient coverage.

CAG and stent implant claim was rejected on grounds of suppressed history of hypertension. Ombudsman noted the insured was continuously insured for years, had no prior related treatment, and likely was unaware of mild hypertension, invalidating repudiation.

Knee replacement claim was rejected due to a 30-day renewal gap in a past year and pre-existing disease. During hearing, the insurer agreed to overlook the gap and settle the claim upon document submission.

Hospitalization claims were rejected because medical records from the treating center clearly established that symptoms existed for four years prior to policy inception, substantiating the pre-existing disease exclusion.

A claim for hip replacement was partially disallowed because the sum insured under the old policy year was exhausted, and the insurer refused to apply the renewed policy for a continuous hospital stay. Ombudsman awarded ex-gratia relief.

Claim for breathlessness and fever was rejected due to pre-existing conditions (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease). Ombudsman noted the treatment also covered unrelated acute ailments like anemia and UTI, awarding ex-gratia payment.

Lasik surgery claim for myopia correction was rejected as refractive errors are excluded under the policy. The complaint was further found non-entertainable due to concurrent proceedings before a Consumer Forum.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim following death from pulmonary complications related to a prior kidney transplant was rejected due to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Insurers failed to prove the conditions existed prior to policy inception, and the Ombudsman ordered full payment.

The insured lodged multiple claims under a Mediguard Policy. Some claims were partially settled and a post-hospitalisation claim was pending. During the hearing, the insurer agreed to settle the balance of the first claim, review the second claim after obtaining clarifications, and consider the post-hospitalisation expenses within policy terms.

The insured lodged a post-hospitalisation claim for gall bladder polyp treatment. The insurer repudiated the claim stating the disease was pre-existing, supported by hospital records showing the ailment existed before policy inception. Due to considerable delay and deficiency in service by the insurer in processing, a compensation of Rs. 1000 was awarded, but the complaint against repudiation was dismissed.

The insured filed claims for hospitalisations related to Pancreatitis, Chronic liver disease, and related conditions. The insurer repudiated the claims citing exclusion 4.8 for ailments resulting from alcohol intake. Hospital case sheets and independent medical opinion confirmed long-term alcohol abuse as the cause, leading to the dismissal of the complaint.

The insured underwent cataract surgery and lodged a claim after cashless facility was withdrawn on the grounds of a pre-existing condition. The initial discharge summary wrongly recorded the ailment duration as two years due to a billing error.
