The insured's son was treated for an infected umbilical sinus leading to sepsis. The insurer repudiated the claim under the congenital disease exclusion clause. The Ombudsman noted sepsis originated from the congenital umbilical sinus and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Under a hospital cash policy, a claim for chemotherapy for stage IV colon cancer was repudiated as a pre-existing disease based on medical literature generalisations. The Ombudsman held the insurer failed to prove pre-existence and awarded Rs. 21,000 with 9% interest.

Out of a claim of Rs. 9,832.20, only Rs. 4,383 was initially paid. The insurer conceded during the hearing that the balance was due and instructions had been issued. The Ombudsman awarded the full claimed amount with interest, accounting for previous payment.

Claims for CAD treatment across multiple hospitals were repudiated as pre-existing based on a clinical history noting similar symptoms for a year. The Ombudsman found no conclusive proof that the patient was aware of or treated for CAD prior to the policy and awarded Rs. 9,597 with interest.

Hospitalization for back and neck pain was repudiated due to lack of active treatment and inability to verify the 24-hour stay. The Ombudsman noted the admission was purely for diagnostics and pain killers without active inpatient treatment, and dismissed the complaint.

The insurer disallowed the cost of a CPAP machine during sleep apnoea treatment under a group mediclaim policy. The Ombudsman held that unlike permanent fixtures such as pacemakers, a CPAP is a reusable breathing machine not covered under specific policy terms, dismissing the complaint.

A claim for liver cirrhosis and other ailments was restricted to Rs. 15,000 based on a pre-existing disease cap. The Ombudsman observed active treatment was given for non-pre-existing conditions like liver cirrhosis and ordered the insurer to pay the balance of Rs. 6,410 with interest and costs.

A claim for stroke treatment was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension noted in hospital records. The complainant produced case sheets showing sudden onset without 10-year hypertension history. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and awarded Rs. 29,641 with interest.

Dispute over sum assured slabs and premium calculation upon policy renewal. The insurer conceded the correct sum assured and premium interpolation during proceedings. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to issue the policy with proper sum assured, refund excess collection, and pay costs.

A claim for knee injury hospitalization was repudiated because the stay was solely for an MRI scan without active medical treatment or medicines prescribed. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's exclusion of diagnostic-only admissions and dismissed the complaint.

A claim for CAD treatment was repudiated citing a prior cardiologist consultation. The Ombudsman found the consultation occurred during treatment for a road traffic accident and general checkups proved no prior heart ailment. The insurer was directed to pay Rs. 10,982 with interest.

Delay in settling a personal accident death claim. The insurer admitted liability and stated settlement documents were processed. The Ombudsman awarded the full sum of Rs. 2 lakhs with interest and costs for delayed payment.

A claim for varicose ulcer treatment at an alternative medicine center was repudiated on grounds of unrecognised hospital, unqualified doctor, and unapproved treatment protocol. The Ombudsman ruled the hospital and doctor met policy definitions, awarding Rs. 17,621 with interest.

A claim for accidental injury was repudiated because hospitalization was solely for diagnostic tests (X-ray, CT scan) with minimal medicines and normal reports. The Ombudsman upheld the exclusion of diagnostic-only admissions and dismissed the complaint.

Insured patient was treated for stomach cancer. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing stomach ailment based on a general history statement. Ombudsman found no prior diagnosis or treatment for cancer and set aside the repudiation, awarding Rs. 50000 with 8% interest.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for disc prolapse and treated with bed rest and traction. Insurer rejected the claim stating treatment could be done on OPD basis and complaint was time-barred. Ombudsman held that active treatment requiring bed rest was given and ordered payment of hospital bill of Rs. 7647 with interest and cost.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was admitted following a fall and diagnosed with Sacroiliac strain treated conservatively with bed rest and analgesics. Insurer repudiated stating treatment fell under exclusion and could be managed on OPD basis. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured was treated for lumbar spondylosis. Insurer deducted a portion for pre-existing diabetes mellitus due to a policy break in 2003. Ombudsman upheld the deduction for pre-existing DM but awarded interest and cost due to delay in settlement.

Insured underwent specialized ayurvedic treatment involving herbal and oil massages. Insurer rejected the claim stating it was mere oil massage that could be done on OPD basis and alleged pre-existing illness. Ombudsman found the treatment specialized requiring hospitalization, reversed the rejection, and awarded Rs. 12250 with interest.

Claim for father's hospitalization was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension and lack of policy continuity proof prior to 2001. Complainant provided history details. The text cuts off in the decision section.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for eye treatment was restricted/denied because the eye condition and surgery occurred prior to the individual policy inception, and the insurer treated a second policy as limited for pre-existing conditions. Ombudsman noted non-disclosure of the prior operation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization claim for incisional hernia repair following a past caesarian section was repudiated as pre-existing. Ombudsman held that hernia is a mechanical event arising from an existing scar rather than a pre-existing disease, and directed the insurer to pay the claim.
Claim for cerebral subarachnoid hemorrhage, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion. The text ends abruptly during the facts description.

Claim for son's adenoidectomy and tonsillectomy was rejected under first-year policy exclusion. Ombudsman noted these procedures are not listed among first-year exclusions and directed the insurer to pay the claim.

Insurer restricted a dialysis and chronic renal failure claim to the original sum insured after the policy sum insured was enhanced, citing pre-existing CRF. Ombudsman noted that restriction terms were never communicated or incorporated into the policy and ordered payment of the balance Rs. 12329.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim was initially closed/repudiated for non-submission of requested documents following the insured person's death. During the proceedings, documents were submitted and the insurer settled the claim for Rs. 20229.
Claim for acute gastroenteritis was repudiated because the hospital was depanelled without notice to the insured, and there was a delay in intimation. Ombudsman allowed 75% of admissible expenses.

Insurer partially settled a laparoscopic cholecystectomy claim, cutting surgeon and operation theatre fees under the reasonableness clause. Ombudsman found the insurer's cuts mostly reasonable but awarded an additional Rs. 11000 due to emergency nature and comparable cases.

Claim for bilateral cataract operation with premium lens implant was partially disallowed under the reasonableness clause. Ombudsman noted the insurer had settled similar claims in full for other policyholders and directed full settlement.

Insurer deducted room charges and diet charges during ayurvedic treatment for Parkinson's disease. Ombudsman held that essential room-associated services (power, water, sanitation, ward boy) and diet are integral parts of hospitalisation expenses and not legally disallowable.

Claim for lumbar slip disc treatment was partially disallowed on the ground that the last 7 days of hospital stay lacked active treatment. Ombudsman allowed 75% of admissible expenses in view of package billing and hospital clarifications.

insurer: The United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for fracture surgery expenses was partially settled by the TPA. During the Ombudsman proceedings, the insurer agreed to settle the full remaining balance of Rs. 25921.

Claim for endovenous laser therapy for varicose veins was repudiated as a pre-existing disease based on hospital records and doctor certificates, despite later contradictory certificates submitted by the insured. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Claim for knee replacement surgery was delayed because implant invoices and stickers were missing. After the insurer sanctioned admissible amounts excluding implants and bulk medicines without receipts, the insured accepted the settlement during proceedings.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: The insured claimed for breast cancer treatment. The insurer rejected it as a pre-existing disease, arguing the policy had been cancelled and re-issued. The Ombudsman noted there was no break in continuity from the original policy date over a year prior, making the claim valid.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims for two hospitalizations were rejected: one for lack of 24-hour stay and another for non-necessary hospitalization. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection for the short stay, but awarded 50% ex-gratia for the second hospitalization given the patient's medical history.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured underwent surgery for Fistula in ano and claimed Rs. 21,968. The insurer paid Rs. 10,000, citing a policy clause capping fistula treatments at 10% of the sum insured. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial payment based on policy terms.

insurer: The United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for cardiac treatment was partially rejected because the policy specifically excluded hypertension and related ailments for the insured family member. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cashless pre-authorisation for coronary bypass surgery was cancelled when records indicated a 15-year history of hypertension. Since no formal claim had been filed with the insurer yet, the Ombudsman advised submitting the claim papers with proof of onset.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: A claim for a second hospitalization due to chronic liver disease was repudiated as pre-existing based on a doctor's initial certificate. Subsequent clarifications from the treating doctor showed the cirrhosis resulted from an acute infection. The Ombudsman found the rejection unsustainable.

insurer: Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for surgery to remove a colloid cyst was initially rejected under the congenital disease exclusion. During the proceedings, the insurer reconsidered, settled the claim for Rs. 1,11,250, and the complaint was closed.

A claim for primary infertility treatment via hystero-laparoscopy was repudiated under the policy exclusion for infertility. The Ombudsman held that hospitalization for evaluation of infertility rather than acute sickness was correctly excluded.

Following surgery for a perianal abscess, the TPA heavily cut surgeon and operation theatre charges using comparative hospital tariffs. The Ombudsman ruled that the policy had no fee caps and the hospital bills were valid, directing full settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: A claim for enteric fever was repudiated after investigation revealed the nursing home was closed during the claimed period and another doctor certified treatment on an OPD basis elsewhere. The Ombudsman upheld the denial due to fraud.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: A claim for diagnostic tests regarding dysphagia was repudiated as a pre-existing condition and for being solely for investigation. The Ombudsman found the tests were incidental to diagnosis and treatment, holding the insurer's rejection untennable.
A claim for fistula surgery was partially settled due to billing discrepancies. During proceedings, the TPA paid the remaining balance of Rs. 1,400, and the complaint was closed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured claimed for Ayurvedic treatment of a digestive disorder requiring a 13-day hospital stay. The claim was denied on the grounds that external oil therapies and oral medications did not warrant hospitalization. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for acute severe cellulitis was repudiated under pre-existing exclusion due to a past history of filariasis. The Ombudsman noted the policy had been active for eight years and the condition did not constitute a pre-existing disease.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The TPA paid part of a varicose vein laser treatment claim based on a network package rate, cutting Rs. 18,000. The Ombudsman found the insurer failed to verify hospital circulars supporting the charged per-leg rate, ruling the deduction unjustified.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: An amendment to a previous award adjusting the payable balance to Rs. 16,210 based on the actual remaining sum insured after prior claim settlements during the policy year.

A claim for knee replacement surgery was partially disallowed by applying reasonableness caps to surgeon and assistant fees. The Ombudsman ruled the reasonableness deduction was not sustainable given standard fees in similar cases.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for osteoarthritis and sciatica treatment was entirely repudiated on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary for the line of treatment given. The Ombudsman ordered an 80% settlement considering the patient's age and condition.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for gastric motility disorder and depression was rejected under pre-existing and lack of hospitalization necessity clauses. The Ombudsman granted 50% of admissible expenses on an ex-gratia basis given the patient's age and pre-hospitalization condition.

A claim for ventral hernia surgery was rejected because the insurer claimed it resulted from a prior cholecystectomy performed four years earlier. In the absence of previous hospital papers to dispute this, the Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured underwent abdominal hysterectomy. Claim was initially delayed due to pending documents like indoor case papers and bill clarification. Insurer later offered partial settlement which the complainant agreed to during the hearing.

Insured's daughter was hospitalized for calculous cholecystitis. Claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion clause 4.1 as hospital records and medical history indicated symptoms existed for two years prior to policy inception.

Insured hospitalized for Hepatitis C infection. Claim repudiated for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of past blood transfusion in 1988 considered a predisposing factor. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for obstructive sleep apnea and required a CPAP machine. Insurer rejected claim stating hospitalization was for investigation only, but Ombudsman found the ailment severe and allowed the claim.

Insured hospitalized for gastro-oesophageal ulcer with hiatus hernia. Insurer rejected claim under pre-existing clause citing aspirin use. Ombudsman noted policy was active for 18 years and lack of proof for aspirin being the cause, ruling in favor of complainant.

Insured underwent hernia operation. Claim repudiated due to specific exclusion of hernia in a fresh policy issued after a short break in renewal. Ombudsman ordered ex-gratia settlement based on original sum insured.

Insured hospitalized for prolapsed intervertebral disc shortly after policy inception. Claim repudiated under pre-existing disease clause due to severe symptoms and lack of prior medical papers. Ombudsman upheld insurer decision.

Insured hospitalized for ankle fracture. Insurer deducted amounts from surgeon and anesthetist fees under reasonableness clause. Ombudsman ruled unilateral cuts unjustified since cashless was allowed and directed full payment.

Insured underwent heart surgery during a gap period when renewing and enhancing the policy. Insurer rejected claim due to break in continuity. Settled via Ombudsman recommendation to pay on original sum insured.
Insured hospitalized for acute lumbar disc prolapse. Claim file closed by TPA due to lack of reply regarding late intimation. Settled during Ombudsman proceedings with payment issued to claimant.

Insured hospitalized for coronary angiogram. Claim rejected as a complication of excluded diabetes mellitus. Ombudsman allowed reimbursement of hospitalization expenses excluding diabetes treatment on an ex-gratia basis.

Insured underwent CABG surgery. Claim repudiated under pre-existing clause alleging diabetes since 1997. Ombudsman noted lack of exact proof regarding diabetes onset before policy inception and favored the complainant.

Insured underwent knee replacement surgery. Claim rejected under pre-existing clause due to a short renewal delay after 11 years of continuous coverage. Ombudsman directed payment of 80% of the admissible claim.
Insured hospitalized for mandibular cyst. Claim rejected under pre-existing disease clause as he had similar mandible infection 10 years prior. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claims for two hospitalizations were rejected under pre-existing clause. First hospitalization was for observation only, making rejection tenable. Second hospitalization for chronic renal failure and MI was directed to be paid as similar past claims were settled.

Insured hospitalized for ureteric calculi and cystoscopy. TPA partially settled surgeon fees invoking reasonableness clause based on super deluxe room tariffs. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as expected behavior of a prudent person.

Insured hospitalized for heart surgery. Claim initially rejected as a complication of excluded diabetes, later partially paid by TPA. Insured sought full settlement. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision while noting already sanctioned amounts should not be recovered.

Insured hospitalized for cardiac and diabetic conditions. Claim rejected under pre-existing clause citing long-standing diabetes. Ombudsman noted continuous coverage since 1989 and previous claim payments, directing settlement.

Insured underwent CABG surgery. Claim rejected under pre-existing clause as heart ailment was considered a complication of excluded diabetes. Ombudsman directed settlement for 80% of admissible expenses on original sum insured.

Insured hospitalized for liver cirrhosis and later expired due to complications. Claim repudiated under exclusion clause 4.8 as medical evidence confirmed the cirrhosis was due to alcohol. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured claimed for cerebral ataxia and vomiting. Insurer rejected under pre-existing diabetes clause. Ombudsman noted diabetes was not necessarily the sole cause and policy was in its second year, directing 50% settlement.

Child hospitalized for undescended testes. Insurer rejected claim citing congenital anomaly exclusion. Ombudsman noted the anomaly went undetected and was not clearly an external defect, ruling in favor of complainant.

Claim for chronic renal failure and dialysis rejected because an earlier hospitalization in 2001 for hypertension and cardiomyopathy was not disclosed in the proposal form. Insurer's decision was upheld.

Claimant underwent bypass surgery and sought balance payment after partial settlement. Insurer rejected based on hospital records showing history of hypertension prior to sum insured enhancement. Ombudsman dismissed due to jurisdictional limits on resolving medical record contradictions.

Claim for lumbar canal stenosis surgery rejected due to non-disclosure of a laminectomy performed 20 years prior. As the past surgery had no recent complications, the Ombudsman ordered 80% settlement with a 20% penalty for non-disclosure.

Claim for acute pancreatitis leading to death was rejected under alcohol abuse exclusion. Hospital records confirmed alcohol consumption and a previous pancreatitis attack. Insurer's rejection was upheld.

Claim for kidney transplant recipient hospitalized for headache and giddiness rejected as hospitalization was unwarranted since only oral medicines and OPD investigations were administered. Insurer's decision upheld.

Insured disputed quantum for bilateral cataract surgeries. Insurer settled according to group policy MOU limits and 30-day cataract waiting period rules after sum insured enhancement. Insurer's partial payment upheld.

Claim for ceacal ulcers following emergency caesarean section rejected as a pregnancy complication. Ombudsman obtained independent medical opinions favoring complainant and reverted the case back to insurer.

TPA disallowed part of surgeon fees during cashless hospitalization. Ombudsman held that network hospital and TPA issues should not burden the insured and directed reimbursement of the extra amount paid.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for pulmonary and cardiac conditions rejected due to pre-existing illness within five months of policy inception. Although telemarketing involved no proposal form, medical records proved chronic prior symptoms. Insurer's decision sustained.

Claim for tuberculosis hospitalization and death rejected because symptoms existed prior to policy inception and hospitalization occurred on the second day of coverage, violating pre-existing and 30-day exclusion clauses.

Cashless facility was denied and claim rejected on grounds that hospitalization for backache and joint pain was for observation/investigation and lacked emergency. Ombudsman awarded 50% on an ex-gratia basis due to patient suffering.
Claim for child heart surgery rejected due to late submission while waiting for primary insurer to process papers. During Ombudsman proceedings, insurer agreed to reopen and process the claim.

Claim for spinal surgery rejected due to non-submission of older consultation notes from 2005. As the insured passed away, family could not produce them. Ombudsman directed the company to properly investigate and resolve the matter.

Insurer paid claim only up to initial sum insured, refusing enhanced sum insured for PTCA heart surgery because the enhancement carried a specific diabetes exclusion, and blood tests confirmed uncontrolled diabetes.

Claim for foot amputation due to diabetes complications rejected due to policy exclusion. Insurer later admitted the exclusion appeared due to a system error, issued a corrective endorsement, and instructed TPA to process the claim.

Claim for malaria treatment was partially cut by TPA for vitamins, unrelated lab tests, and diabetic consultation. Ombudsman ordered reimbursement of prescribed recovery vitamins/tonics but upheld deductions for unrelated stress tests and diabetic consultation.

CABG claim rejected due to 15-year pre-existing diabetes history despite disclosure in proposal. Ombudsman upheld the pre-existing exclusion clause supremacy but ordered 75% ex-gratia settlement given 7 claim-free years.

Claim for heart ailment rejected under pre-existing clause because insured had CABG in 1988. Complainant argued disclosure at 1997 inception and lack of exclusions. Ombudsman held that current policy terms and pre-existing exclusions apply.

Insured was admitted for gout and treated with oral medication and investigations. The insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.10 stating hospitalization was unnecessary. During the hearing, the insurer reviewed the case and settled the claim.

Insured was admitted for acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease. The claim was rejected as pre-existing since bronchitis and asthma were excluded under the policy and considered related lung conditions. The insurer's decision was upheld.

Insured's son underwent subcutaneous mastectomy for gynaecomastia. The insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.5 for cosmetic surgery. The ombudsman set aside the repudiation noting the surgery was due to pain and enlargement from hormonal imbalance, not purely cosmetic.

Insured hospitalized for acute renal failure. Claim rejected because renal failure was linked to long-standing diabetes mellitus and hypertension as pre-existing conditions. The company's decision was upheld, but they were directed to pay 50% ex-gratia.

Insured claimed reimbursement for treatment of bilateral osteoarthritis received at a healthcare centre on an OPD basis involving daily exposure for 21 days without hospital admission. The claim was rightly refused as it did not fulfill the 24-hour hospitalization requirement.

Insured hospitalized for tenosynovitis and dilated cardiomyopathy. Claims were delayed and questioned over diabetes history. Following forum intervention and document review, the company settled the claim for Rs. 71,213 as full and final payment.

Insured hospitalized for generalized weakness and shortness of breath, diagnosed with HIV infection and opportunistic infections. The insurer rejected the claim as HIV/AIDS treatments are excluded under the policy. The forum upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured underwent CAG and PTCA for chest discomfort. Insurer rejected the claim for non-disclosure of diabetes since 6-7 years. Although telemarketing lacked proposal forms, the long-standing diabetes was a major risk factor for heart ailments making repudiation tenable.

Insured's father treated for sub foveal choroidal neovascular membrane (macular degeneration). Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing age-related issues worsened by diabetes and that treatment was a day-care procedure not needing hospitalization. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured underwent vitrectomy and lens removal for complications from a cataract surgery done 10 years prior. Insurer rejected the claim due to missing past records. Given the long continuous policy and charitable hospital origin of past records, benefit of doubt was given and claim allowed.

Complainant was hospitalized for varicocele, phimosis, and frenuloplasty, alongside primary infertility. The insurer invoked clause 4.8 to reject the varicocelectomy due to infertility exclusions. The phimosis and frenuloplasty procedures were allowed and held payable.

Claim for urinary tract infection (UTI) treatment was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause 4.1. The ombudsman noted that an infection is recurrent and temporary, not a continuous pre-existing disease. The respondent was directed to pay the claim.

Claim for road accident fracture treatment and subsequent wire removal was rejected due to alleged 7-day delay in lodgment. The ombudsman found no delay in intimation and directed the respondent to process the validly supported claim papers.

Expenses for myomectomy surgery were refused by TPA for late submission beyond 7 days. Facts showed papers were submitted promptly after final medical fitness certificate. The respondent was directed to call for papers and process the claim.

Claim for renal pelvic stone treatment was initially repudiated under pre-existing disease clause 4.1. Since the continuous policy started in 1998, the ailment became covered after 4 years. The insurer admitted TPA error and settled the claim prior to the hearing.

Claim for right knee operation was refused by TPA for late submission. Verification showed follow-up visits extended until fitness was declared, making the lodgment timely within the post-hospitalization window. The respondent was ordered to decide the claim.

Claim papers were refused for a 14-day delay after post-hospitalization completion, caused by a family bereavement. The ombudsman held that the TPA's outright refusal was unfair and directed the respondent to condone the delay and process the claim.

Claim was repudiated because the insured was suffering from tongue cancer since 1998, prior to the policy inception in 1999, and the fact was not disclosed. Medical referee reports confirmed pre-existence. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for hospitalization due to suicidal depression (alprazolam overdose) was rejected under exclusion 4.8 for intentional self-injury. The respondent failed to prove suicidal intent or police involvement, so rejection was unjustified. The respondent was directed to settle the claim.

Complainant contested the disallowance of post-hospitalization expenses under a mediclaim policy. The insurer established that they had already paid out an amount exceeding the maximum effective sum insured limit due to an oversight. The case was dismissed.

Claim was lodged under a mediclaim policy. The insurer imposed an unexplained restriction of Rs. 2.5 Lakh without justification or notice to the complainant. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to set aside the restriction and settle the claim.

Claim was repudiated for lack of hospitalization and non-submission of discharge summary. The complainant provided a hospital certificate instead. The insurer did not submit documents or attend the hearing. The Ombudsman directed the case to be reopened upon submission of required papers.

Claim for inguinal hernia surgery was rejected under clause 4.8 as a congenital condition. Independent medical opinion established that inguinal hernia may develop at any age. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to settle the claim.

Claim for Folicular Carcinoma of Thyroid was repudiated due to non-disclosure and pre-existing condition, as records showed the ailment existed for 10 years prior to policy inception. The case was dismissed.
Hospitalization claim for Fistula in Ano was repudiated because Ayurvedic treatment was not taken in a government medical college as required by clause 2.1. The case was dismissed.

Claim following an accident was disputed on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. Considering injuries and doctor's advice, the Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim based on facts.

Claim for Acute Ulcerative Colitis was rejected for late submission exceeding 7 days, though policy terms allowed 30 days. The Ombudsman condoned the delay and directed the insurer to process the claim.

Claim for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia was settled for Rs. 50,000 against a claim of Rs. 63,015. The sum insured was enhanced from Rs. 50k to Rs. 1 lakh when the pre-existing ailment arose. The deduction was upheld.
Claim was lodged for malaria and respiratory infection, but records showed treatment was for a pre-existing knee injury explicitly excluded from the cover. The case was dismissed as false.
Claim was settled for Rs. 50,000 based on the pre-enhancement sum insured because the ailment was pre-existing when the sum insured was raised from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 1 Lakh.

Claim for Neurogenic Bladder was repudiated under clause 4.1 due to alleged pre-existing frequent urination since childhood. The insurer did not submit documents. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and ordered payment.
Claim for recurrent urine infection, hydrocele, and phimosis was repudiated under clause 4.8 as a congenital external ailment. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the case.
Claim for burn injuries resulting in death was repudiated as police records and inquest papers pointed towards suicide due to old illness. The complaint failed and the case was dismissed.
Claim for post-discharge treatment of Chronic Osteomyelitis exceeding the 60-day policy limit and submitted past the deadline was dismissed.
Claim for Yag Laser Capsulotomy performed as an outpatient procedure following cataract surgery was repudiated because it is not payable outside hospitalization. The case was dismissed.

Claim for Fistula in Ano operation performed by an Ayurvedic surgeon in a private nursing home was rejected under clause 2.1 requiring inpatient treatment in a government hospital. The case was dismissed.
Claim for dental treatment expenses resulting from an accident was repudiated because the policy strictly restricts payments to treatments involving hospitalization. The case was dismissed.
Claim involving diabetic laser treatment was repudiated because medical documents proved diabetes pre-existed the policy inception. The case was dismissed.

Claim for hospitalization to perform coronary angiography for chest pain was repudiated because the admission was deemed purely for diagnostic purposes rather than active treatment. The case was dismissed.
Claim for bronchitis and respiratory tract infection was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1 as a pre-existing condition known for 10 years. The case was dismissed.
